confirmed.title: Driver drop while a child route is open pops that route instead of Waiting; Waiting is left dead and Finding never restarts the search
confirmed.description: `_onLiveTick` handles `cancelledByDriver` immediately and deliberately bypasses the route-current gate (lines 405-415). `_researchAfterDriverCancel` disposes tracking, reconciles the session back to `findingDriver`, sets `_leaving = true`, then does `final navigator = Navigator.of(context); if (navigator.canPop()) { navigator.pop(true); return; }` (651-659). The app has a single navigator (app.dart:34, MoveraSheet.show uses rootNavigator: true), so `pop(true)` pops whatever route is on top: the driver profile (`_openProfile`, 976), Chat (waiting_sheet_bits 215), the arrived sheet, the cancel/reason sheets, the Safety Kit or the RoutePickerPage opened by `_changeRoute`. Waiting itself stays mounted with `_leaving = true`, `_mapParked = true` and a disposed `DriverTrackingController`; `FindingDrivers._openWaiting` (finding_drivers.dart 535-557) never receives `true`, so `_resumeFindingAfterDriverCancel` never runs and `FindingDriverController.active` stays null. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (Waiting pushed over a parent, DriverProfilePage pushed above it, `MockRideRealtime.cancelByDriver()`): output was `profile still mounted: false`, `waiting still mounted: true`, `waiting route result: null`, `session status: RideStatus.findingDriver`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider is on Waiting and opens the driver's profile (or chat, or the cancel sheet, or 'Change route'); the driver drops the ride. The profile page closes by itself, the rider lands back on a grey, parked Waiting screen showing the old driver with no live updates and no way to cancel (`_confirmCancel` returns on `_leaving`), while the server trip is back in `searching` and the next driver's acceptance is never shown.
confirmed.evidence: waiting_for_driver.dart:410-415 `if (status == RideStatus.cancelledByDriver) { if (!_leaving && !_completedOpened) { unawaited(_researchAfterDriverCancel()); } return; }` ; 651-659 `final navigator = Navigator.of(context); if (navigator.canPop()) { _researching = false; navigator.pop(true); return; }` ; movera_sheet.dart:48-51 `Navigator.of(context, rootNavigator: true).push<T>(route)` ; finding_drivers.dart:556 `if (!mounted || researchDriver != true) return;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pop Waiting's own route by reference (store `ModalRoute.of(context)` in initState and use `Navigator.of(context).popUntil`/`removeRoute` on that route, or `closeRouteByReference`-style logic), or defer the research until `_routeIsCurrent` like the other stage navigations do.

verdicts.reason: waiting_for_driver.dart:410-415 handles cancelledByDriver right away and skips the _routeIsCurrent gate. _researchAfterDriverCancel then calls Navigator.of(context).pop(true) at 651-659. That pops whatever route is on top, not Waiting's own route, and nothing first closes child routes such as _openProfile (Navigator.push at 976) or Chat (waiting_sheet_bits.dart:215). So the child route is popped and Waiting stays mounted with _leaving=true and a disposed tracker. FindingDrivers._openWaiting never gets true back (finding_drivers.dart:556 `if (!mounted || researchDriver != true) return;`), so _resumeFindingAfterDriverCancel never runs. Meanwhile the session has already been reset to findingDriver by resumeSearchingAfterDriverCancel (active_ride_controller.dart:318-335).
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_r27_test.dart, based on test/finding_driver/audit_fix_research_route_test.dart: Finding, then assignNow to reach Waiting, then push a plain child page, then holdAssignment + cancelByDriver, pumped 60x50ms. Output: 'AUDIT child mounted: false', 'AUDIT waiting mounted: true', 'AUDIT finding active controller: null', 'AUDIT session: RideStatus.findingDriver'. The test passed (it only prints). File deleted.

verdicts.reason: _researchAfterDriverCancel calls Navigator.of(context).pop(true) whenever canPop() is true (waiting_for_driver.dart:651-659). That pops whatever route is on top, not Waiting's own route, and nothing checks _routeIsCurrent: the cancelledByDriver branch (410-415) skips that check on purpose. When a child route such as DriverProfilePage (976), chat or a sheet is on top, that child is the one popped. Waiting stays mounted with _leaving=true, its map parked and its tracking disposed. FindingDrivers._openWaiting never gets `true` back (finding_drivers.dart:556), so _resumeFindingAfterDriverCancel never runs and the search controller is never restarted. The rider is left on a dead Waiting screen while the server is searching again.
verdicts.repro: Wrote and ran test/_audit_r27_test.dart (now deleted), based on test/finding_driver/audit_fix_research_route_test.dart. Steps: Finding pushed, assignNow, Waiting shown, a child MaterialPageRoute pushed from Waiting's context, then holdAssignment and cancelByDriver. Output: `child mounted before: true`, `child still mounted: false`, `waiting still mounted: true`, `FindingDriverController.active: null`, `session status: RideStatus.findingDriver`, `waiting route isCurrent: true`. After another assignNow: `waiting count 1, status RideStatus.findingDriver`, so the next driver is never shown.

confirmed.title: History archives book-now rides with a UTC DateTime that is then rendered field-by-field, so times/dates show in UTC
confirmed.description: recordFor stores `scheduledPickupAt: ended.toUtc()` (line 201) and `createdAt: snapshot.createdAt.toUtc()`. The History UI then formats that DateTime with helpers that read the DateTime's own fields rather than converting to local: ReservationFormat.time (lib/features/reservations/presentation/reservation_format.dart:70-74 uses `when.hour`/`when.minute`), ReservationFormat.moment/historyWhen (221-227 compare `when.year/month/day` to a local `DateTime.now()`), weekdayDate/_dayMonth via L10n.formatDate (intl formats the instance's fields; a UTC DateTime prints UTC), called from lib/features/history/presentation/ride_history.dart:546 `ReservationFormat.historyWhen(ride)`. HomeJourneySection.fromRides (lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/home_journey_section.dart:74-83) likewise buckets by `at.year/at.month` and `weeks[(at.day - 1) ~/ 7]` on the UTC value against a local `now`. The only consumer that converts, SupportController (`when: ride.scheduledPickupAt.toLocal()`), shows the correct intent. Verified by throwaway test: a ride ended at 14:30 CEST archived via recordFor and formatted with ReservationFormat.time gave '12:30'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Stockholm rider finishes a ride at 14:30 local (CEST). History lists it as '12:30'. A ride ended 00:40 on 1 May shows as 30 Apr 22:40 and is counted in April on the home 'Your month' card; near midnight the Today/Yesterday split is wrong. In Tunisia (UTC+1) every History time is one hour early.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Either store `ended.toLocal()` in the archived Reservation (consistent with how book-later Reservations hold wall-clock local times) or make every formatter/aggregator call `.toLocal()` before reading fields (ReservationFormat.time/moment/cardDate/weekdayDate, HomeJourneySection.fromRides). Add a test with a UTC-constructed DateTime.

verdicts.reason: recordFor stores scheduledPickupAt as ended.toUtc() (on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:201). The value stays UTC both after the local store round-trips it through toIso8601String/DateTime.tryParse (reservation.dart:408-410) and on the server path via WireTime. ride_history.dart:546 then calls ReservationFormat.historyWhen, which uses cardDate and time (reservation_format.dart:70-74, 138-147, 204-206). Both read the hour, minute and day fields straight off the DateTime without toLocal(), and DateFormat formats a UTC instance's own fields. Every History time and date is therefore shown in UTC, and the day split is computed against a local now.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test (test/_audit_r3637_test.dart, since deleted), run with TZ=Europe/Stockholm. recordFor(..., endedAt: DateTime(2026,6,10,14,30)) and then ReservationFormat.time printed 'AUDIT36 tzOffset=2:00:00.000000 isUtc=true time=12:30'.

verdicts.reason: on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:200-201 stores `scheduledPickupAt: ended.toUtc()`. The stored ISO string ends in 'Z', so Reservation.tryParse (reservation.dart:408-420, DateTime.tryParse) reads it back as a UTC DateTime. ReservationFormat.time (reservation_format.dart:70-74) reads .hour/.minute directly, and historyWhen/cardDate use the same value without toLocal(). HomeJourneySection.fromRides (home_journey_section.dart:74-83) buckets by at.year/month/day. Apart from SupportController:42, nothing in the History or Home paths calls toLocal(). Both the device store (demo) and ApiRideHistoryRepository (release, WireTime UTC) feed this path, so every Book-now History row shows UTC wall-clock time.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_c4b2_hist_test.dart (deleted afterwards), run with TZ=Europe/Stockholm. It calls recordFor(endedAt: DateTime(2026,10,14,14,30)), round-trips the result through toJson/tryParse, and formats it. Output: `R36 tzOffset=2:00:00.000000 time=12:30 afterRoundTrip=12:30 isUtc=true historyWhen=Wed, 14 Oct · 12:30 late=Sat, 31 Oct · 23:40 lateMonth=10`. So a 14:30 ride shows as 12:30, and a ride at 00:40 on 1 Nov shows as 31 Oct 23:40 and is counted in October. `+2: All tests passed!`

confirmed.title: Server-backed History silently drops every fully settled trip (RideStatus.closed) and every paymentFailed trip
confirmed.description: ApiRideHistoryRepository._record (lib/features/history/data/ride_history_repositories.dart:56-66) feeds each server TripProjection through RideProjection.toSnapshot and then OnDemandRideHistoryStore.recordFor(snapshot, terminalStatus: snapshot.status, ...). recordFor maps the status with _reservationStatus (lines 243-259), which returns ReservationStatus.completed only for status.isCompletedSurface (tripCompleted | paymentProcessing | paymentFinalized | ratingPending per lib/core/contracts/ride_status.dart:85-89) and ReservationStatus.cancelled only for an explicit cancelled list. RideStatus.closed (trip completed + payment settled + rating submitted/skipped) and RideStatus.paymentFailed are in neither branch, so _reservationStatus returns null and recordFor returns null (line 194), i.e. the trip is omitted from History. In release builds (ApiRideHistoryRepository) almost every finished trip the server returns is eventually `closed`, so the History tab loses the rider's past rides and their receipts; a payment-failed ride (which the rider must settle) also vanishes. Verified with a throwaway test (test/_audit_datamath_test.dart, since deleted): recordFor(...terminalStatus: RideStatus.closed) and paymentFailed both returned null while ratingPending returned a record (`3 passed` for these cases).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider completes a trip, pays, rates the driver. Server projection now has status completed/paymentStatus settled/ratingStatus submitted -> RideStatusWire.fromTrip -> RideStatus.closed. The History screen loads /trips, _record returns null for it, and the ride (and every older settled ride) is not listed. A rider with 50 past trips sees an empty or near-empty History; a trip whose card payment failed also disappears, so the rider cannot see what is owed.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In _reservationStatus treat RideStatus.closed and RideStatus.paymentFailed as ReservationStatus.completed (optionally carry a payment-failed flag on the Reservation for the receipt), or add a separate mapping for server trips in ApiRideHistoryRepository. Add a test that a `completed`+settled+rated projection appears in History.

verdicts.reason: _reservationStatus (on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:243-259) maps a status to 'completed' only when isCompletedSurface is true (ride_status.dart:85-89), and that excludes closed and paymentFailed. Neither status is in the cancelled list either, so recordFor returns null at :194. In release, di.dart:154 uses ApiRideHistoryRepository, and its _record (ride_history_repositories.dart:56-66) passes snapshot.status. fromTrip (trip_status.dart:178-191) maps completed + settled + rating submitted/skipped to closed, and payment failed to paymentFailed. loadOnDemand then skips those null records at :43-44, so every fully settled and rated trip, and every trip whose payment failed, is missing from History.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test (test/_audit_r3637_test.dart, since deleted). recordFor printed 'closed -> null', 'paymentFailed -> null' and 'ratingPending -> ReservationStatus.completed'. A MockClient /api/v1/rider/trips response with one trip (completed, captured, ratingStatus 'submitted') gave 'api list length=0'. The same trip with ratingStatus 'pending' gave 'api list length=1'.

verdicts.reason: ApiRideHistoryRepository._record (ride_history_repositories.dart:56-66) passes snapshot.status to recordFor. RideStatusWire._afterCompletion (trip_status.dart:179-192) maps completed+settled+rating submitted/skipped to RideStatus.closed, and payment failed to RideStatus.paymentFailed. _reservationStatus (on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:243-259) handles neither one: isCompletedSurface (ride_status.dart:85-89) excludes them and so does the cancelled list. It returns null, recordFor returns null at :194, and the trip is dropped. ApiRideHistoryRepository is the History source in release builds (di.dart:150-154). A trip the rider has paid for and rated, or skipped rating, ends up `closed`, so it disappears from History. The same happens to a payment-failed trip.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_c4b2_hist_test.dart (deleted afterwards). It feeds InProcessMockClient rides with wire projections {completed, captured, submitted}, {completed, captured, skipped}, {completed, failed}, {completed, captured} and {cancelled_by_rider} through ApiRideHistoryRepository.loadOnDemand. Output: `R37 ids=[ondemand-canc, ondemand-final]`, so the closed, skipped and payment-failed trips were all dropped, while paymentFinalized and cancelled were kept.

confirmed.title: "Arrive by" mode books the chosen arrival time as the pickup time
confirmed.description: The scheduling screen offers two modes, "Pickup at" and "Arrive by" (`_modeSelector`, lines 585-608 toggle only `_pickupMode`). In "Arrive by" mode the estimate row shows `_selectedDateTime.subtract(trip)` as the "Estimated pickup" (lines 484-488, 726-749), so the rider understands the chosen time is their arrival. But the time committed to the session is always `_selectedDateTime` itself: `_commitSchedule()` (153-158) calls `captureSchedule(_selectedDateTime, ...)` and the `popOnConfirm` path returns `_selectedDateTime` (130-132). `_pickupMode` is never read anywhere else in the file. The committed time becomes `ScheduledRideSession.scheduledAt` -> `SelectRide.initialScheduledFor` -> `ScheduledRideCheckout.draftFrom(scheduledPickupAt: when)` (scheduled_ride_checkout.dart:21-31), i.e. the pickup time of the reservation.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider taps "Arrive by", picks 10:00 for a 20-minute trip; screen says "Estimated pickup 09:40". The reservation is created with scheduledPickupAt = 10:00; Home chrono counts down to 10:00 and the driver is dispatched for a 10:00 pickup, so the rider arrives at ~10:20 instead of by 10:00.
confirmed.evidence:
select_date_time.dart:82 `bool _pickupMode = true;`
select_date_time.dart:130-132 `if (widget.popOnConfirm) { Navigator.pop(context, _selectedDateTime); return; }`
select_date_time.dart:153-158 `void _commitSchedule() { widget.session?.captureSchedule(_selectedDateTime, timezone: widget.timeZone); }`
select_date_time.dart:484-488 `final estimatedTime = trip == null ? null : _pickupMode ? _selectedDateTime.add(...) : _selectedDateTime.subtract(Duration(minutes: trip));`
scheduled_ride_checkout.dart:31 `scheduledPickupAt: when,`
confirmed.suggested_fix: When `_pickupMode == false` and `tripMinutes` is known, commit/return `_selectedDateTime.subtract(Duration(minutes: trip))` (clamped with `clampPickup`) as the pickup; hide the Arrive-by mode when `tripMinutes` is null.

verdicts.reason: build() renders `_modeSelector()` (select_date_time.dart:523), which offers 'Arrive by' (:600-604). In that mode the estimate row shows 'Estimated pickup' = `_selectedDateTime.subtract(trip)` (:484-488, :739). However `_pickupMode` is only read for that display (:486, :597, :602, :739). `_commitSchedule()` (:153-158) always captures `_selectedDateTime`, and the popOnConfirm path returns `_selectedDateTime` (:130-132). That value becomes session.scheduledAt, then SelectRide.initialScheduledFor (scheduled_category_gate.dart:55), and then the reservation's scheduledPickupAt. No document records Arrive-by as display-only (no match in DECISIONS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md or QA_HOOKS.md), and nothing else in lib reads the mode.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: grep shows `_pickupMode` has no reads outside the display code. Followed captureSchedule into openScheduledCategorySelector and SelectRide(initialScheduledFor: session.scheduledAt).

verdicts.reason: `_pickupMode` (select_date_time.dart:82) is read in only two places: the estimate calculation (lines 484-488) and the estimate label (line 739). `_commitSchedule` (lines 153-158) and the popOnConfirm return (lines 130-132) always use the unadjusted `_selectedDateTime`. That value becomes `selection.scheduledFor` and then `scheduledPickupAt: when` (scheduled_ride_checkout.dart:21-31). So in 'Arrive by' mode the screen tells the rider the pickup is earlier, but the reservation books the arrival time as the pickup time. No document records this as intended.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_r89_test.dart (now deleted). Called ScheduleDateTimeSelector.choose(now: 2026-09-26T10:00Z, tripMinutes: 20), tapped 'Arrive by', then 'Continue'. Output: `AUDIT time texts on screen: [12:30, 12:10]; estimatedPickup shown: true` and `AUDIT picked (returned pickup) = 2026-09-26 12:30:00.000 HH:mm=12:30`. The screen says 'Estimated pickup 12:10', but 12:30 is returned and booked as the pickup.

confirmed.title: A screen-reader scroll action on the trip slide runs the trip step with no confirmation dialog
confirmed.description: PHASE_53 says assistive-technology activation of the slide shows a confirmation dialog before the trip action runs. Only the Semantics onTap (_accessibleConfirm) does that. The inner GestureDetector has onHorizontalDragUpdate/onHorizontalDragEnd and is not excluded from semantics, so Flutter's RawGestureDetector adds SemanticsAction.scrollLeft/scrollRight to the same node. In Flutter (checked in /opt/flutter widgets/gesture_detector.dart:1786-1806 and rendering/proxy_box.dart:4253), scrollRight calls onHorizontalDragUpdate with delta = size.width*0.8 and then calls onEnd straight away. _update sets _fraction = 0.8w/(w-58) >= 0.78, which snaps to 1. _finish() then sees _fraction >= _trigger and awaits widget.onConfirmed(), which is _advanceRide(): Start trip, Complete trip, Go to stop. No dialog is shown. The regression test (test/audit/accessible_confirmation_test.dart) only fires SemanticsAction.tap.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A VoiceOver user focuses the slide ('Complete trip') and does a three-finger horizontal swipe, or a TalkBack user does the scroll gesture. The trip advances (completed, or started before the rider boards) with no 'Confirm this trip action?' dialog.
confirmed.evidence:
accept_ride.dart:1670-1681
  return Semantics(
    button:true, enabled:!_confirming,
    label:widget.label.replaceFirst('Slide to ',''),
    onTap:_confirming ? null : _accessibleConfirm,
    child:FocusableActionDetector(...
      child:GestureDetector(
        behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque,
        onHorizontalDragUpdate: (details) => _update(details.delta.dx, maxTravel),
        onHorizontalDragEnd: (_) => _finish(),
accept_ride.dart:1619-1624 _update: _fraction = next >= _trigger ? 1 : next;
accept_ride.dart:1631-1637 _finish: if (_fraction < _trigger) {...return;} ... await widget.onConfirmed();
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass excludeFromSemantics: true to the slide's GestureDetector (or wrap it in ExcludeSemantics/BlockSemantics), so the only assistive path is the Semantics onTap that opens the confirmation dialog. Add a test that performs SemanticsAction.scrollRight and expects no stage change.

verdicts.reason: The slide's GestureDetector (accept_ride.dart:1676-1681) is not excluded from semantics, so its horizontal-drag recognizers add scrollLeft/scrollRight actions to the same node as the Semantics onTap (accept_ride.dart:1670-1673). When scrollRight runs, Flutter sends a drag update of 0.8*width followed by an end. _update (1619-1625) snaps _fraction to 1, and _finish (1633-1645) then awaits onConfirmed, which is _advanceRide (accept_ride_panel.dart:941-944). _accessibleConfirm's dialog is never shown. The existing test accessible_confirmation_test.dart only performs SemanticsAction.tap.
verdicts.repro: I wrote a throwaway test at test/_audit_u64_test.dart, adapted from test/audit/accessible_confirmation_test.dart. It pumps AcceptRide at waitingForRider, finds the 'start trip' semantics node and performs SemanticsAction.scrollRight. Output: 'hasScrollRight=true hasScrollLeft=true' and then 'DIALOG=0 STAGE=ActiveRideStage.onTrip'. The trip started with no confirmation dialog. I deleted the file afterwards.

verdicts.reason: The slide's GestureDetector (accept_ride.dart:1710-1715, onHorizontalDragUpdate/End) is not excluded from semantics, so it adds scrollLeft/scrollRight to the slide's node. A scrollRight action sends a drag delta of about 0.8 x width, which _update (accept_ride.dart:1653-1660) snaps to _fraction = 1 since it is at least _trigger 0.78. _finish (1667-1680) then awaits widget.onConfirmed() directly. The confirmation dialog in _accessibleConfirm (1682-1692) is skipped. The existing regression test only exercises SemanticsAction.tap.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_u64slide_test.dart performed SemanticsAction.scrollRight on the 'Start trip' node. Output: `stage before=ActiveRideStage.waitingForRider`, `dialog shown=false`, `stage after=ActiveRideStage.onTrip`, i.e. the trip started with no dialog. scrollLeft left the stage unchanged (negative delta). Result: '+2: All tests passed!'. File deleted.

confirmed.title: Device-to-device transfer rules leave the 'root' domain (app_flutter) included, so Ride-check audio recordings move to a new phone despite 'saved only on this phone'
confirmed.description: For apps targeting Android 12+ (targetSdk = flutter.targetSdkVersion = 36), `android:allowBackup="false"` no longer turns off device-to-device migration. Only the `<device-transfer>` rules control it. Those rules exclude only `sharedpref`, `database` and `file` (getFilesDir()). NativeRideCheckRecorder writes recordings to `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()`, which on Android is `PathUtils.getDataDirectory` = `context.getDir("flutter")`, that is /data/data/se.movera.driver/app_flutter. That directory is in the `root` domain, which is not excluded. The recordings are therefore copied to a new device during setup. That contradicts the XML comment ('Driver data ... is excluded from cloud backup and device-to-device transfer'), the RECORD_AUDIO rationale in docs/ANDROID_PERMISSIONS.md ('saved only on this phone and never sent'), and the Ride-check UI copy. privacy_storage_test only checks that a `<device-transfer>` tag exists, so it cannot catch this. (The iOS Documents backup issue is already known; this is the Android counterpart, a different mechanism.)
confirmed.failure_scenario: A driver records audio in a Ride check on an Android 12+ phone, then sets up a new phone with Google's 'copy apps & data' cable or wireless transfer. The rider-incident recordings in app_flutter/ride_check_audio/*.m4a are copied to the new device, although the app promised they stay only on the original phone.
confirmed.evidence:
data_extraction_rules.xml:10-14 `<device-transfer> <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="." /> <exclude domain="database" path="." /> <exclude domain="file" path="." /> </device-transfer>` (no `root`)
lib/core/safety/ride_check_recorder_native.dart:31-37 `'${(await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()).path}/ride_check_audio'` ... `path: '${directory.path}/$recordingId.m4a'`
path_provider_android PathProviderPlugin.getApplicationDocumentsPath -> `PathUtils.getDataDirectory(context)` -> `applicationContext.getDir("flutter", MODE_PRIVATE)`
test/audit/privacy_storage_test.dart:60-62 only `contains('<device-transfer>')`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add `<exclude domain="root" path="." />` (and `external`) to both `<device-transfer>` and `<cloud-backup>`, or store recordings under noBackupFilesDir. Make the test assert the domains.

verdicts.reason: data_extraction_rules.xml:10-14 excludes only the sharedpref, database and file domains from device-transfer. For targetSdk 31 and later (build.gradle.kts:25 uses flutter.targetSdkVersion), AndroidManifest.xml:13 `allowBackup="false"` does not turn off device-to-device migration. NativeRideCheckRecorder.start (ride_check_recorder_native.dart:31-37) writes to getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/ride_check_audio. On Android that is context.getDir("flutter") = <dataDir>/app_flutter, which belongs to the 'root' domain, not 'file' (getFilesDir). The recordings are therefore copied by device-to-device transfer, against the file's own comment (:2-3) and docs/ANDROID_PERMISSIONS.md:10 ('saved only on this phone'). No document records this as intentional.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: read the rules XML, backup_rules.xml, the manifest flags, the targetSdk setting and the recorder's path. Searched docs for any decision allowing transfer and found none.

verdicts.reason: The manifest sets allowBackup=false together with dataExtractionRules (AndroidManifest.xml:13-15), and targetSdk = flutter.targetSdkVersion (build.gradle.kts:25, Android 12+). From Android 12 on, allowBackup=false does not turn off device-to-device transfer, and only <device-transfer> controls it. data_extraction_rules.xml:10-14 excludes only sharedpref, database and file. Everything not excluded is included. ride_check_recorder_native.dart:31-37 writes recordings to getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/ride_check_audio. With the locked path_provider_android 2.2.17, that is PathUtils.getDataDirectory(context) (PathProviderPlugin.java:57-58), which is context.getDir("flutter") = <dataDir>/app_flutter. That directory is in the 'root' domain, not in 'file' (getFilesDir), so no exclusion covers it. This contradicts the XML comment, docs/PRIVACY_SECURITY.md:13, docs/ANDROID_PERMISSIONS.md:10 ('saved only on this phone') and the UI string audioSavedOnlyOnThisPhone.
verdicts.repro: Traced the config and the plugin source: pubspec.lock pins path_provider_android 2.2.17, and ~/.pub-cache/.../path_provider_android-2.2.17/.../PathProviderPlugin.java:58 returns PathUtils.getDataDirectory. The XML has no <exclude domain="root">. Not run on a device, because device-transfer behaviour needs real hardware.

confirmed.title: iOS bundle identifier is still the template com.example.movera, while README and the 16-point record say the bundle id is se.movera.driver
confirmed.description: Android uses applicationId/namespace `se.movera.driver`. README.md:7 says 'Bundle id `se.movera.driver` is unchanged', and FRONTEND_16_POINT_RECORD.md (F04/F15) says the application and bundle id were kept. The Runner target's Debug, Release and Profile configurations all set PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER to the Flutter template value `com.example.movera`, and RunnerTests uses `com.example.movera.RunnerTests`. Flutter's own `build ipa` validation flags this ('Your application still contains the default "com.example" bundle identifier'). Apple does not register App IDs under the reserved example domain, so the iOS release cannot be signed or uploaded under the intended identity. The `ios-release-preflight` job uses `--no-codesign` and never sees this. release_metadata_test.dart checks only the Android gradle file for 'se.movera.driver', so the mismatch passes CI.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The owner archives the iOS release for TestFlight or the App Store. Signing fails because the com.example.movera App ID cannot be registered, or a build goes out under a throwaway identifier that does not match the Android/README identity, so later updates cannot carry over to the real se.movera.driver listing.
confirmed.evidence:
ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:371 `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER = com.example.movera;` (also :550, :572; RunnerTests :387, :404, :419)

confirmed.title: Cold start awaits push re-registration (Firebase init, getToken, POST /push/devices) before runApp, blocking the first frame on the network
confirmed.description: `await _registerExistingPushSession()` runs before `runApp`. In staging/production with stored tokens and an accepted push consent it calls `PushPermissionGate.registerIfConsented` -> `FirebasePushService.register()` (lib/core/notifications/firebase_push_service.dart:198-227), which awaits `_gateway.initialize`, `requestPermission`, `getToken` (FCM network round-trip, no timeout in this code) and `_replaceToken` -> `_api.post('/api/v1/push/devices')` (ApiClient `_timeout` 15 s). Nothing in the app is painted until it resolves. The comment at lines 143-147 states the rider must not be kept waiting on push registration and defers `_pushCoordinator.start()` for that reason, but this earlier await defeats it. On the web the HTML boot screen's fallback timer (web/index.html:144 `setTimeout(clear, 20000)`) can remove the loading screen before Flutter paints, leaving a blank page.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Production rider on a poor connection opens the app: the splash/boot screen stays up to ~15 s (API timeout) plus however long FCM getToken takes before Home appears; on web the boot screen can vanish at 20 s into a blank page.
confirmed.evidence: lib/app/bootstrap.dart:130 `await _registerExistingPushSession();` ... :134-136 `runZonedGuarded(() { runApp(const MoveraApp());` ; :40-42 `await AppScope.instance.pushPermission.registerIfConsented(logEvent: 'push.session_restore_deferred')`; firebase_push_service.dart:210-226 `await _gateway.initialize(...); final permission = await _gateway.requestPermission(); ... final token = await _gateway.getToken(...); ... await _replaceToken(token.trim());`; api_client.dart:42 `static const _timeout = Duration(seconds: 15);`; bootstrap.dart:143-147 comment `...before anything slower runs, so the rider is not kept waiting on push registration.`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Do not await it: `unawaited(_registerExistingPushSession())` after runApp (e.g. in the same post-frame callback as `_pushCoordinator.start()`), or run it with a short timeout.

verdicts.reason: bootstrap.dart:130 awaits _registerExistingPushSession() before runApp at :136. In staging and production (allowsMockTransport is false, env.dart:81-84), with stored tokens and consent=accepted, PushPermissionGate.registerIfConsented (push_permission_gate.dart:69-77) awaits FirebasePushService.register (firebase_push_service.dart:198-227). That chain awaits Firebase.initializeApp, then requestPermission, then on iOS ensureAppleTransportReady (up to 10 x 200 ms of polling, :95-109), then getToken with no timeout, then POST /api/v1/push/devices (15 s ApiClient timeout). The try/catch only catches errors; it puts no limit on time. Nothing paints until all of this finishes, which goes against the intent stated at :143-147 and the 'deferred' log-event name. On web, index.html:144 removes the boot screen after 20 s whether or not Flutter has painted.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: bootstrap.dart:33-48, :130, :134-148, push_permission_gate.dart:69-91, firebase_push_service.dart:95-120 and :198-227, di.dart:123 and :354-357, web/index.html:132-144. Not run, because it needs a real Firebase and network.

verdicts.reason: bootstrap.dart:130 awaits _registerExistingPushSession() before runZonedGuarded/runApp (134-136). In staging/production (allowsMockTransport false) with stored tokens and PushConsent.accepted, PushPermissionGate.registerIfConsented (push_permission_gate.dart:69-77) awaits FirebasePushService.register (firebase_push_service.dart:197-227). That call awaits gateway.initialize, requestPermission, ensureAppleTransportReady (iOS polls up to 10×200 ms = 2 s, :101-105), getToken with no timeout, and _replaceToken → _api.post('/api/v1/push/devices') with a 15 s timeout (api_client.dart:42,153-161). A 401 on that POST can add a refresh (15 s) and a retry. The try/catch only absorbs errors; it does not bound the time. No frame is painted until all of this finishes. This defeats the stated intent at bootstrap.dart:143-147 of not keeping the rider waiting on push registration. Every cold start of a consented production rider pays at least one FCM and one API round trip; on a bad network it waits up to about 15 s or more.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand, no run (bootstrap needs real Firebase and network). Await chain: bootstrap.dart:130 → :40 registerIfConsented → push_permission_gate.dart:76 `await _register` → :81 `await _push.register()` → firebase_push_service.dart:210/211/216/217/226, then the 15 s ApiClient timeout. I found no timeout or unawaited wrapper anywhere on the path.

confirmed.title: Route-change pricing charges booked stops again: bookedKm is the straight pickup-to-destination distance while routeKm goes through the stops, plus a 25 kr fee for every stop
confirmed.description: `_ride()` stores `bookedKm` as the straight pickup->destination distance (lines 2319-2330) even when the booking body carries `stops` (which `_quote` priced through, via `_routedMeters`, lines 2103-2124 / 2134-2137). `_routeChangePricing` (lines 2046-2096) then prices a change as `bookedMinor + stops.length * 25 kr + (routeKm - bookedKm) * perKm`, where `routeKm` is pickup -> stops -> destination (lines 2071-2080). For a ride booked with a stop, a route change that keeps the same stop charges the stop's detour kilometres a second time plus a 25 kr stop fee that the quote never contained. The result is returned as `newTotal`/`difference` from `POST .../route-quote` and `PATCH .../rides/{id}` (routeChange) and, for non-cash methods, written as a `paymentAdjustments` capture (lines 919-932). Reproduced: booking pickup (59.3293,18.0686) -> stop (59.35,18.10) -> dest (59.3326,18.0649), fare 29 100 öre; route-quote of the identical route: `AUDIT B1: bookedKm=0.42 routeKm=5.69 newTotal=37900 difference=8800` (+88 kr for changing nothing).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Demo/dev/test flavors (the stand-in backend the live GitHub Pages build uses). Rider books a multi-stop trip, then edits the destination by a few metres (or just re-confirms the same route) during the ride: the sheet shows a large surcharge (here +88 kr), and for card/wallet methods the mock records a captured adjustment for it. Money shown and 'charged' is wrong on every route change of a multi-stop trip.
confirmed.evidence:
in_process_mock_client.dart:2319-2330 `'bookedKm': body['pickupLat'] is num && ... ? _km(body['pickupLat'] as num, body['pickupLng'] as num, body['destinationLat'] as num, body['destinationLng'] as num) : null,` (no stops)
in_process_mock_client.dart:2071-2087 `for (final stop in stops) { routeKm += _km(lat, lng, stop['lat'] as num, stop['lng'] as num); ... } routeKm += _km(lat, lng, dLat, dLng); ... final newMinor = rates.roundToStep((bookedMinor + stops.length * rates.convertKronor(25) + (routeKm - bookedKm) * rates.perKmMinor).clamp(bookedMinor * 0.5, double.infinity));`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store `bookedKm` from the routed distance through the booked stops (reuse `_routedMeters(body)`), and only add the 25 kr fee for stops that are new relative to the booked `ride['stops']` (or drop the per-stop fee, since `_quote` never charges one).

verdicts.reason: _ride() stores bookedKm as the straight pickup-to-destination distance and ignores stops (in_process_mock_client.dart:2319-2330). _quote prices the booking through the stops (_routedMeters, :2103-2137). _routeChangePricing (:2046-2096) computes routeKm through every stop in the body and adds 25 kr for each stop. The client always sends the full stop list, existing stops included (route_change_controller.dart:174-187 builds `located` from all stops, reusing known points), so a route change on a multi-stop trip bills the booked stops' detour distance and a stop fee a second time. Nothing guards against this: the clamp is only a lower bound. For non-cash methods the PATCH writes a 'captured' paymentAdjustment (:919-932). Medium rather than high or critical: it is wrong money on an edge path (multi-stop trip plus route change), in the demo/stand-in backend only.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_r89_test.dart (since deleted). Quoted and booked pickup (59.3293,18.0686), stop (59.35,18.10), destination (59.3326,18.0649), then POSTed route-quote for the identical route. Output: `R9 booked fare {amountMinor: 29100, currency: SEK} bookedKm 0.42271425800076845` and `R9 route-quote same route: newTotal {amountMinor: 37900, currency: SEK} difference {amountMinor: 8800, currency: SEK} routeKm 5.69`, which is +88 kr for no change. Test passed.

Output: 'quote total=29100', 'bookedKm=0.4227', 'AUDIT r9 status=200 newTotal={amountMinor: 37900} difference={amountMinor: 8800} routeKm=5.69'. The same check without stops gave 'newTotal=22800 difference=0'. That is +88 kr for changing nothing: the 63 kr detour already in the quote plus a 25 kr stop fee.

confirmed.title: `MatchedDriver.fromJson` reads `id`/`vehicleMake`/... but the contract `DriverSummary` carries `driverId` and a nested `vehicle`, so a contract-conformant projection parses to no driver
confirmed.description: The production transport `ApiRideRealtime` builds the driver from the projection with `MatchedDriver.fromJson` (api_ride_realtime.dart lines 201-204), as do `ride_projection.dart:68` and the restore path. `fromJson` requires `json['id']` (line 80, returns null when empty, line 83) and reads flat `vehicleMake/vehicleModel/vehicleColor/plate/photoAsset`. `contracts/openapi.yaml` `DriverSummary` (lines 5281-5305, required `driverId, firstName, vehicle`) and CONTRACT.md §2 (`DriverSummary { driverId, firstName, ..., photoUrl?, vehicle: { make?, model?, color?, plate? } }`) never send `id` or flat vehicle fields. The in-process mock sends `MatchedDriver.toJson()` (`id`, `vehicleMake`, ...), so the mock and the parser agree with each other but not with the shipped contract, and no test can catch it. Against a server that follows `openapi.yaml`, every projection yields `driver == null`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Staging/production flavor against a backend built from `contracts/openapi.yaml`: the trip reaches `accepted`; `ApiRideRealtime` emits `driverAssigned` with `driver: null`; Waiting shows 'Driver details unavailable' (no name, plate, vehicle, photo) for the whole ride, and the history/receipt has no driver either.
confirmed.evidence:
matched_driver.dart:78-83 `static MatchedDriver? fromJson(Map<String, dynamic>? json) { if (json == null) return null; final id = json['id'] as String? ?? ''; final firstName = (json['firstName'] as String? ?? json['name'] as String? ?? '').trim(); if (id.isEmpty || firstName.isEmpty) return null;`
matched_driver.dart:90-94 `vehicleMake: json['vehicleMake'] as String?, vehicleModel: json['vehicleModel'] as String?, vehicleColor: json['vehicleColor'] as String?, plate: json['plate'] as String?, photoAsset: json['photoAsset'] as String?,`
openapi.yaml:5281-5305 `DriverSummary: required: - driverId - firstName - vehicle ... driverId: $ref Id ... photoUrl ... vehicle: $ref VehicleSummary`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Accept `driverId` (and `photoUrl`, nested `vehicle.{make,model,color,plate}`) in `fromJson` alongside the legacy flat keys, and have the mock emit the contract shape so the contract tests exercise it.

verdicts.reason: In production the app uses ApiRideRealtime (di.dart:202, non-mock flavors). It parses `ride['driver']` with MatchedDriver.fromJson (api_ride_realtime.dart:201-204), and ride_projection.dart:67-69 does the same. fromJson requires `json['id']` (matched_driver.dart:80-83) and reads flat vehicleMake/plate/photoAsset (:90-95). The contract's DriverSummary (openapi.yaml:5281-5305, CONTRACT.md:56) sends `driverId` and a nested `vehicle{make,model,color,plate}`, with `id` absent. ride_projection.dart:21 shows the app does accept contract-canonical keys elsewhere (`tripId ?? id ?? rideId`), but not for the driver. No wire normalization exists in lib/core/api.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_c1b2v_test.dart: `MatchedDriver.fromJson({'driverId':'drv_1','firstName':'Anna','vehicle':{...}})` printed `AUDIT driver parsed: null`. File deleted afterwards.

verdicts.reason: In contracts/openapi.yaml, TripProjection.driver is `$ref DriverSummary` (line 5408). DriverSummary (lines 5281-5305) requires `driverId`, `firstName` and a nested `vehicle` (VehicleSummary make/model/color/plate, lines 5266-5280); CONTRACT.md:56 and the driver app's copy of the contract say the same. `MatchedDriver.fromJson` (matched_driver.dart:78-83) needs `json['id']` and returns null without it. It reads only flat `vehicleMake`, `plate` and `photoAsset`. The production paths api_ride_realtime.dart:201-204 and ride_projection.dart:67-69 call it on the raw `ride['driver']` with no adapter in between, so a backend that follows the contract produces no driver at all. The mock emits `toJson()` (the `id`/flat shape), and contracts/fixtures holds no driver object, so no test catches the mismatch. Rated medium because the failure appears only against a backend that follows the contract.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway unit test test/_audit_r16_test.dart (now deleted). Output: `AUDIT contract-shape fromJson -> null` for {driverId, firstName, rating, photoUrl, vehicle:{make, model, color, plate}}, and `AUDIT legacy-shape fromJson -> ABC123` for {id, firstName, plate}.

confirmed.title: isLateEcho drops every camera report for 600 ms after a web flight lands, including the rider's own pan or pinch, so MapView.pose goes stale and the next glide jumps back
confirmed.original_title: isLateEcho drops every camera report for 600 ms after a web flight lands, including the rider's own pan or pinch, so MapView.pose goes stale and the next glide jumps back
confirmed.description: After a JS (web) flight lands, _jsGlide sets view.pose to the goal and _landedAt to now (lines 366-368). For the next cameraEchoGrace (600 ms), CustomGoogleMap._onMove discards any reported pose that is not near the landing pose (custom_google_map.dart:202). The check assumes such reports are late echoes of flight frames. Nothing clears _landedAt when the rider touches or moves the map: interrupt() (lines 80-94) and the touching setter leave it set, and _movedByHand only sets movedByHandAt. So the camera moves from a pan, pinch or wheel zoom in that window are thrown away too, as are those of an app animateCamera bounds fit (runCameraUpdate). view.pose stays at the landing pose. The next stepped glide starts from view.pose (easeCameraTo line 325, _glide line 391) and its first frame is sent from that stale origin. This affects a requested trip-map refit (fitBounds with the 450 ms default, a Dart glide) or a follow update once the 12 s hold ends.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On the web Home map, the rider taps recenter (a 1 s JS flight). Right after it lands, they quickly drag the map a few hundred metres and let go, all within 0.6 s. Every report is dropped as a late echo, so pose still holds the recenter point. Later an app glide (for example the follow update after the 12 s hold, or a 450 ms refit on a trip map) steps from that stale pose. Its first frame moves the camera back next to the old recenter point, then it glides, which looks like a jump. Worked by reading the code: easing is false after landing, so _onMove's only remaining filter is isLateEcho.
confirmed.evidence: map_camera_motion.dart:115-121 `bool isLateEcho(CameraPosition reported) { final landed = _landedAt; ... if (now().difference(landed) > cameraEchoGrace) return false; return !_settled(reported, current); }`; :366-368 `view.pose = view._goal; view._landedAt = MapView.now();`; interrupt() :80-94 never resets _landedAt. custom_google_map.dart:202-204 `if (view != null && !view.easing && !view.isLateEcho(position)) { view.pose = position; }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Clear _landedAt in interrupt() and in the touching setter, and when movedByHandAt is set, so only echoes that arrive before any newer gesture or command are filtered.

verdicts.reason: isLateEcho (map_camera_motion.dart:115-121) rejects any report that is not near the landing pose for 600 ms after _landedAt is set (:366-368). The only thing that writes _landedAt is _jsGlide. interrupt(), the touching setter (:70-75) and _movedByHand (custom_google_map.dart:186-193) never clear it. A web drag sets touching (pointerdown) and calls release() -> _movedByHand, which only stamps movedByHandAt and does not interrupt because easing is already false. Its bounds_changed reports reach _onMove (custom_google_map.dart:202) with easing false, and isLateEcho drops them. If the gesture's last report falls inside the 600 ms window, pose stays at the landing pose. _settleTilt on idle then sees the landing pose's tilt already matching its zoom and does nothing. The next stepped glide (a follow update once the 12 s hold ends, or a 450 ms fitBounds) starts its first _approach frame from that stale pose and jumps back. This needs a fast gesture right after a recenter, so it is an edge path.
verdicts.repro: Static trace only (read-only run). Read isLateEcho, _jsGlide, interrupt and the touching setter, and in CustomGoogleMap: _onMove, _movedByHand, _settleTilt and the RiderMapBridge.listen wiring; also release() in web/rider_map_camera.js. I confirmed by grep that nothing else resets _landedAt.

verdicts.reason: _landedAt is set only at map_camera_motion.dart:368 and nothing clears it. interrupt() (:80-94), the touching setter (:71-77) and _movedByHand (custom_google_map.dart:186-193) all leave it set. For 600 ms after landing (cameraEchoGrace, :147), _onMove (custom_google_map.dart:202) drops every report that is not _settled with the landing pose. The tolerance is 0.00002 deg, about 2 m (:158-163). So the rider's own pan reports in that window are thrown away. A drag that ends inside the window produces no later CameraMoveEvent, and onIdle carries no pose, so view.pose stays at the landing pose. On the web the touch pan is done by the JS layer itself, with no inertia to emit later events. Once the 12 s followHold ends, a follow easeCameraTo starts from that stale pose (:325, _glide :391), and its first frame moves the camera back near the recenter point. A requested fitBounds does the same at once, because _mayMove clears movedByHandAt. The window is narrow (the gesture must finish within 0.6 s of landing), so this is an edge path.
verdicts.repro: Read-only, no run. Worked it by hand. A recenter flight lands at T, so _landedAt = T. The rider drags 300 m between T+100 ms and T+500 ms. Each report r has |r.lat - landing.lat| > 0.00002, so isLateEcho returns true and the report is dropped. After T+500 ms there are no more reports. At T+12.5 s, a GPS fix calls animateCamera(follow:true): heldByRider is false because 12.5 - 0.5 = 12 s has passed, so easeCameraTo runs. It sets from = the landing pose, and the _approach frame sends a pose about 5% of the way from the landing point toward the goal, far from where the camera actually is.
verdicts.evidence: map_camera_motion.dart:115-121 isLateEcho; :366-368 sets _landedAt; interrupt() :80-94 never resets _landedAt; custom_google_map.dart:202-204.

confirmed.title: Off-route fix makes routeFraction 0: the island ETA, remaining distance and leg progress reset to the full route (and can trigger a false 'traffic ahead' strip message) until the reroute lands
confirmed.description: _rebuildBanner sets _progressAlong = progress.offRoute ? null : progress.alongMeters (line 481), so the next projection starts from scratch. routeFraction then reads (_progressAlong ?? 0) / length, so off route the driven share becomes 0 instead of unknown or the last value. AcceptRide uses it directly: _remainingMeters = total * (1 - (routeFraction ?? 0)) and _routeEtaText = seconds * (1 - (routeFraction ?? 0)) (accept_ride.dart:920, 927). The leg progress derived from remaining also drops to 0%. This holds through the 2 s reroute debounce plus the network fetch, and on any single fix more than 50 m off (accuracy up to 50 m is accepted).
confirmed.failure_scenario: 9 km into a 10 km trip, the driver takes a wrong turn or GPS drifts 60 m. The ETA chip jumps from '2 min' to the full original '18 min', the remaining distance shows the whole route, and route progress falls to 0%. They stay that way until the reroute lands, then jump back.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep the last on-route along value for routeFraction (a separate _lastOnRouteAlong field), or return null while off route and let callers keep their previous ETA, instead of treating null as 0.

verdicts.reason: navigation_controller.dart:481 sets _progressAlong to null on an off-route fix (more than 50 m from the polyline, route_progress.dart:34/98). routeFraction (line 156) then returns (null ?? 0)/length = 0. accept_ride.dart:920 and :927 multiply by (1 - 0), so _remainingMeters and _routeEtaText fall back to the full route values. _legFraction (accept_ride.dart:899-911) gets remaining equal to the route total and shows about 0%. While recalculating the island face shows the status, but the strip still renders the ETA and percent: _stripBody uses widget.eta and widget.progress (adaptive_trip_island.dart:836-860), and the strip is tucked only for arrival or a raised sheet (_syncTuck, :233-246). TripStripController.update (trip_island_controller.dart:~325) also sees etaMinutes jump by 2 or more and queues a false 'Traffic ahead +N min' message. This lasts through the 2 s reroute debounce plus the route request.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of navigation_controller.dart:150-157 and 470-496, accept_ride.dart:899-930 and 1285-1296, adaptive_trip_island.dart:233-246 and 791-860. The finding's own throwaway reproduction (routeFraction 0.90 -> 0.0 after one fix 60 m off) matches the code. Not re-run.
verdicts.corrected_title: Off-route fix makes routeFraction 0: the island ETA, remaining distance and leg progress reset to the full route (and can trigger a false 'traffic ahead' strip message) until the reroute lands

verdicts.reason: navigation_controller.dart:481 sets `_progressAlong = progress.offRoute ? null : progress.alongMeters`, and routeFraction at :156 returns `(_progressAlong ?? 0)/length`, so the first off-route fix gives 0. accept_ride.dart:953 (`_remainingMeters = total*(1-(routeFraction??0))`) and :960 (`_routeEtaText`) then show the full route's distance and time again. _legFraction (:932-944) keeps the longest distance seen (the full route), so progress drops to 0. Nothing holds the last on-route value while the controller shows 'Recalculating route…'.
verdicts.repro: Ran a throwaway test (test/_audit_u26nav_test.dart, now deleted) on a real NavigationController with a 2-point route of about 1.1 km, 1080 s. After 9 fixes along the route: `routeFraction=0.8999 offRoute=false eta=2`. After one fix about 68 m east of the line: `routeFraction=0.0 offRoute=true status=Recalculating route…`, `eta minutes=18 remaining=1100.0`. All tests passed.

confirmed.title: Once the car is off route, the ETA and leg progress jump back to the full leg until the reroute arrives
confirmed.description: _rebuildBanner sets _progressAlong to null for an off-route fix. routeFraction then reads `(_progressAlong ?? 0) / length` = 0. AcceptRide's _routeEtaText computes `seconds * (1 - routeFraction)` and _remainingMeters computes `total * (1 - routeFraction)`, so the old route's full duration and distance are shown again. _legFraction then gets remaining == _legTotalMeters and the progress bar drops to 0. This holds for the whole reroute window: a 2 s debounce plus the request, up to the 8 s routing timeout when routing is failing, as in this journey. The same happens right after an accepted GPS jump off the route.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On an 18-minute leg with 3 minutes left, the driver misses a turn, or GPS jumps more than 50 m off the polyline. For about 10 s while the reroute request hangs or fails, the island shows '18 min · <arrival 15 minutes later>' and the leg progress bar resets to empty. confirmed.title: A single fix that projects onto a later leg moves the instruction hint forward for good: the banner skips the turns in between and the car snaps to the other street
confirmed.description: measure() first projects inside [previousAlong-60, previousAlong+400]. The tie rule that prefers forward-consistent progress only applies within 10 m, so any later part of the route that is more than 10 m closer than the current leg wins. This can be a parallel street on an around-the-block route, or the opposite carriageway after a U-turn. The instruction search then starts at instructionHint and only moves forward. NavigationController stores the result unconditionally (_instructionHint = progress.instructionIndex, navigation_controller.dart:480), and DriverCameraPolicy does the same (driver_camera_controller.dart:266). When the next fixes project back onto the real leg (the window misses it, so the global projection is used), along goes back but the hint does not. The maneuvers between the two passes are skipped until a new route object resets the hint: the silent refresh comes after 90 s, or a reroute. The camera policy snaps vehiclePoint to the wrong leg for that fix (driver_camera_controller.dart:269-270), so the car marker jumps to the other street. Fixes with accuracy up to 50 m are accepted, and the jump filter subtracts both accuracies, so a 15-50 m urban-canyon drift is enough.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The pickup is around the block, or across a divided road that needs a U-turn. One GPS sample drifts toward the return leg. From then on the banner shows the arrival ('Pickup in 500 m') instead of the two turns ahead, for up to 90 s. The camera's turn framing is lost, and the car icon jumps onto the parallel street for that fix.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Do not let the windowed projection jump forward past a maneuver unless it is clearly better (for example, require the forward candidate to be consistent with the elapsed distance or speed). Also recompute the instruction index from projection.along when along goes backwards (search from 0, or step the hint back while maneuverAlong[hint-1] > along).

NavigationController keeps that index without a check (navigation_controller.dart:480). The hint resets only on a new route (lines 176, 373, 416). Afterwards the windowed projection [along-60, along+400] no longer covers the true leg. It snaps to the top segment instead, about 35 m away, which is within the 50 m off-route threshold, so the global projection is never consulted and the stale arrival index stays. The fix with the bad offset is accepted because it is under 50 m off the route and the jump filter subtracts both accuracies (navigation_controller.dart:290-299). Downgraded from high to medium: it needs a lateral GPS error of roughly 45 m or more toward a nearby later leg.

confirmed.title: Firebase-configured web builds (none deployed today) would replace the root-scope Firebase SW with Flutter's self-unregistering flutter_service_worker.js on every cold start, forcing a reload and killing the push subscription
confirmed.description: `getToken` passes `serviceWorkerScriptPath: 'firebase-messaging-sw.js'` and firebase_messaging_web registers it with `navigator.serviceWorker.register(path)` and no `scope`, so the registration's scope is the app root (`/movera-rider-app/`). The build never passes `--pwa-strategy=none` (publish-web-live.yml line 45), so Flutter 3.47's `flutter build web` still emits `flutter_service_worker.js` and a `flutter_bootstrap.js` with `serviceWorkerSettings` (flutter_tools web.dart: `includeServiceWorkerSettings = strategy == offlineFirst`, compile.dart defaults to offlineFirst). Flutter's loader (`service_worker_loader.js` lines 105-113) calls `navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistration()` and, whenever ANY registration covers the page, registers `flutter_service_worker.js?v=...` at the same default scope, which replaces the Firebase registration's script. The 3.47 `flutter_service_worker.js` template is a cleanup worker: on activate it `unregister()`s and `client.navigate(client.url)` for every window client. index.html's cleanup (lines 169-176) deliberately keeps the Firebase registration, so on each boot where push consent was accepted: boot waits up to 4 s for SW activation, the page is force-reloaded mid-boot, the push subscription dies with the registration, and `_registerExistingPushSession` then re-registers the Firebase SW and POSTs a brand-new FCM token (`_replaceToken` only unregisters the previous token held in memory, so stale tokens accumulate server-side). The same `getRegistration()` path also fires once for demo visitors who still carry an old `flutter_service_worker.js` registration, because index.html's async `unregister()` races the deferred bootstrap.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Staging/production web build with Firebase defines; rider accepted ride-update notifications. Every cold start: boot screen, 1-4 s pause, page reloads itself once, then boots; `/api/v1/push/devices` receives a new token on every launch and old tokens are never unregistered. If the reload lands during an active search, the search restores from the snapshot but the rider sees the app restart.
confirmed.evidence: lib/core/notifications/firebase_push_service.dart:112-121 `_messaging.getToken(vapidKey: vapidKey, serviceWorkerScriptPath: kIsWeb ? moveraFirebaseMessagingServiceWorker : null)`; firebase_messaging_web-4.2.5 interop/messaging.dart:50-53 `navigator.serviceWorker.register(serviceWorkerScriptPath.toJS)` (no scope); web/index.html:172-176 keeps registrations whose scriptURL contains 'firebase-messaging-sw.js'; web/index.html:570 `<script src="flutter_bootstrap.js" defer>`; /opt/flutter/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/web/file_generators/js/flutter_service_worker.js:7-30 `await self.registration.unregister(); ... client.navigate(client.url)`; engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/flutter_js/src/service_worker_loader.js:106-113 `getRegistration().then(registration => { if (registration) return registerAndActivate(); })`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Build with `--pwa-strategy=none` (or ship a custom web/flutter_bootstrap.js that calls `_flutter.loader.load()` without `serviceWorkerSettings`), and/or register firebase-messaging-sw.js under its own scope (e.g. `firebase-cloud-messaging-push-scope`) so the loader's root-scope `getRegistration()` finds nothing.

verdicts.reason: Each step was traced in the installed Flutter 3.47 SDK and pub cache. (1) `flutter build web` with no --pwa-strategy defaults to offlineFirst (flutter_tools/lib/src/web/compile.dart:120-121). The repo has no web/flutter_bootstrap.js, so the generated bootstrap calls `_flutter.loader.load({serviceWorkerSettings:{serviceWorkerVersion:...}})` (bootstrap.dart:658-670; targets/web.dart:831-841). (2) The shipped bin/cache/flutter_web_sdk/flutter_js/flutter.js contains `getRegistration().then(r=>r?t():Promise.resolve())`, i.e. it registers flutter_service_worker.js at the default scope whenever any registration covers the page (service_worker_loader.js:106-113). (3) firebase_messaging_web 4.2.5 interop/messaging.dart:50-53 registers 'firebase-messaging-sw.js' with no scope. Passed from firebase_push_service.dart:118-119 it resolves against the base href, so its scope is the app root. web/index.html:169-176 deliberately keeps that registration. (4) Registering a different script at the same scope updates that registration. The 3.47 flutter_service_worker.js template calls skipWaiting, then on activate runs registration.unregister() and client.navigate(client.url). The page loaded under the Firebase worker is a controlled client, so it reloads and the Firebase registration and push subscription are gone. The CI workflow batch6-phase78-push.yml:97-99 builds exactly this configuration: a production web build with Firebase defines and no --pwa-strategy. Severity is medium, not high: ARCHITECTURE.md lists FCM/APNs as remaining intentional mocks, and the public demo build has no Firebase config, so no deployed build hits it yet. It will hit every consented web rider once Firebase web push ships.

confirmed.title: After the not-found pause, a successful resync never restarts periodic polling: the ride freezes while the connection reports connected
confirmed.description: `_endNotFound` (lines 347-353) cancels `poll.timer` and sets `poll.timer = null` after `notFoundLimit` consecutive 404s. `reconnectAndResync` (lines 379-390) only flips `poll.ended = false`, lowers `poll.notFound` and runs one forced `_poll`. Nothing re-creates the `Timer.periodic` that `subscribe()`'s `onListen` made (lines 69-77), and `onListen` does not run again because the broadcast controller already has its listener. When the forced poll succeeds, the success path calls `connection.markConnected()` (line 256) so the UI banner clears, but no further GET is ever issued for that ride: the Waiting/in-trip screen keeps showing the projection from that single read until the user triggers another manual resync. Reproduced with a throwaway test (3x404, resync -> 200, pollInterval 20 ms): `AUDIT A: events after resync = 1, state = RealtimeState.connected` then `AUDIT A: calls after 200ms of connected state = 4` (no new polls). Callers: `FindingDriverController` lines 897/1156/1288/1642, `WaitingForDriver` line 929, `RideRestoreCoordinator` line 167, `notification_navigation.dart` line 89 all use `reconnectAndResync` as the recovery path.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Production transport (staging/production flavors). The trip endpoint answers 404 three polls in a row (replica lag, a brief routing fault). Polling pauses and the banner shows failed. The rider taps retry / the app resumes -> `reconnectAndResync` -> 200, banner says connected. From then on the driver's position, arrival, boarding and completion never arrive on this screen; the ride appears stuck at that status indefinitely although the connection state claims it is live.
confirmed.evidence:
api_ride_realtime.dart:347-353 `void _endNotFound(_RidePoll poll) { poll.ended = true; poll.timer?.cancel(); poll.timer = null; ... connection.markFailed(); }`
api_ride_realtime.dart:379-390 `Future<void> reconnectAndResync(String rideId) async { ... if (poll.ended) { poll.ended = false; poll.notFound = poll.notFound > 0 ? notFoundLimit - 1 : 0; } await _poll(poll, force: true); }`
api_ride_realtime.dart:69-77 the only place a timer is created: `onListen: () { if (poll.timer != null) return; ... poll.timer = Timer.periodic(pollInterval, (_) => unawaited(_poll(poll))); }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: In `reconnectAndResync` (or in `_poll`'s success path when `poll.timer == null` and the controller has listeners) re-create `poll.timer = Timer.periodic(pollInterval, (_) => unawaited(_poll(poll)))` once the forced read succeeds; keep it cancelled while `poll.ended` is true.

verdicts.reason: After notFoundLimit consecutive 404s, _endNotFound (api_ride_realtime.dart:347-353) cancels poll.timer and sets it to null. reconnectAndResync (:379-390) only resets poll.ended and poll.notFound and runs a single forced _poll. The only place a Timer.periodic is created is the broadcast controller's onListen (:69-77), and onListen does not fire again while the existing listener (DriverTrackingController._sub, FindingDriverController._sub) stays subscribed. When the forced read succeeds, connection.markConnected() runs, so the UI reports a live connection, but no further GET is ever issued for that ride. Driver position and status changes stop arriving until another manual resync or a resubscribe. All the listed recovery callers (waiting_for_driver.dart:929, finding_driver_controller.dart:897/1156/1288/1642, ride_restore_coordinator.dart:167, notification_navigation.dart:89) use only reconnectAndResync.

Output: `AUDIT before resync calls=3 events=0 state=RealtimeState.failed`, `AUDIT after resync calls=4 events=0 state=RealtimeState.connected`, `AUDIT 300ms later calls=4 (was 4) events=1 state=RealtimeState.connected` -- no polls after the resync while the state reports connected.

The only place a `Timer.periodic` is created is the broadcast controller's `onListen` (:69-77), and that does not fire again while the existing listener stays subscribed. confirmed.title: Mock driver position and arrival are computed against a hard-coded central-Stockholm pickup (never hydrated on resume, hydrated only after the first assignment fix), so after a reload the driver approaches and 'arrives' at Stockholm instead of the trip's pickup
confirmed.description: `_pickupLat/_pickupLng` default to (59.3293, 18.0686) in both the resume path (lines 183-184) and `_assignNow` (lines 263-264), and the driver start position is derived from that default (`lastLat ??= _pickupLat! + 0.0072`, lines 209-210 and 265-266). The real pickup is only fetched by `_hydratePickup()` after the `driverAssigned` event (line 305) and never on the `primeResume` path; after a web reload the stand-in server is empty anyway so `_pickup()` 404s and keeps the default (line 660). `_startGps` therefore lerps toward and declares `driverWaiting` within 50 m of central Stockholm for a Paris/Tunis/Södertälje pickup, `_etaSeconds` is computed against that point, and the resumed `emit()` sets `_acceptedAt ??= now` / `_waitingSince ??= now` (lines 328-333) which `DriverTrackingController` adopts (`acceptedAt = event.acceptedAt ?? acceptedAt`) so the free-cancel/waiting clocks restart at reload time. confirmed.description: `DriverTrackingController._persistLiveStatus` skips terminal statuses (211-212), and `ActiveRideController.resumeSearchingAfterDriverCancel` explicitly does not persist (327-334), so after a driver drop the stored snapshot still says `driverArriving`/`driverAssigned` with the old driver until the next accept. With `ApiRideRealtime` the first poll carries `searching`; `reassigned` is only derived when `poll.lastStatus?.isMatched` (api_ride_realtime.dart 193-199), which is null on a fresh poll, so the event is a plain `findingDriver`. `_onLiveTick` has branches only for `cancelledByDriver`, terminal and completed statuses (410-423); a searching status falls through to the normal sheet rendering, so the screen keeps the 'Driver found' headline (`_headlineFor` → `eta?.headline(status: findingDriver)`), the dropped driver's card, plate and message/call buttons, and no reassignment notice. The rider only learns a new driver was assigned when the next accept arrives; a second reload would restore Finding because `_persistLiveStatus` then saves `findingDriver`.

confirmed.title: Back gesture while the Waiting cancel/end-early request is in flight pops Waiting; Finding underneath stays parked and the cancel result is lost

confirmed.title: A pasted international number (+46 …) at sign-in or Add phone is either rejected or, in the spaced form, cut short and accepted as a wrong number (+4646…) that the OTP is sent to
confirmed.description: `AuthPhoneField` filters input to digits and spaces (auth_controls.dart:289-292), so a pasted `+46 70 123 45 67` becomes `46 70 123 45 67`. `swedishNumberFromField` then prefixes `+46` to anything not starting with `0` (993) giving `+4646701234567`; `toE164` sees 11 digits after +46 and returns null, so the screen shows "invalid Swedish mobile" for a valid number the rider pasted from Contacts.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider pastes their number from the clipboard/contacts in international format on Sign in or Add phone; Continue is refused with an "invalid" error.

auth_controls.dart:289-292 `inputFormatters: [FilteringTextInputFormatter.allow(RegExp(r'[0-9 ]')), LengthLimitingTextInputFormatter(14)],`
auth_navigation.dart:990-994 `final digits = typed.replaceAll(RegExp(r'\s+'), '').trim(); ... return SwedishPhone.toE164(digits.startsWith('0') ? digits : '+46$digits');`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Strip a leading `46`/`0046` before prefixing, or pass the raw digits to `toE164` which already handles `46…`/`0046…` prefixes.

SwedishPhone.toE164 (safety/domain/phone_e164.dart:4-18) only checks for 7-10 digits after +46. A pasted '+46701234567' is rejected as invalid. Worse, the common spaced form '+46 70 123 45 67' becomes the field text '46 70 123 45 6', which is accepted as the wrong number +464670123456. sign_in.dart:96-106 then calls requestOtp with it, so the OTP goes to a non-existent or someone else's number. add_phone.dart:52 uses the same parser. confirmed.title: Finding treats a driver drop (cancelledByDriver) that arrives while a match is deferred as the end of the ride: it archives the ride as cancelled, clears the snapshot and sends the rider Home while the server trip is searching again
confirmed.description: `RideStatus.cancelledByDriver` is in `isTerminal` only so the UI stops tracking the old driver; the trip itself is back in `searching` (core/contracts/ride_status.dart 31-36, trip_status.dart 134). Waiting handles it as a reversible re-dispatch, but the Finding listener does `if (event.status.isTerminal) { unawaited(_completeTerminal(event.status)); return; }` (394-397), and `_completeTerminal` archives `cancelledByDriver` to History as a cancelled ride (1027-1035), clears the snapshot and fires `_onTerminal`, which shows the 'Driver cancelled … Continue' sheet and `RideNavigator.home` (finding_drivers.dart 330-334). The event is reachable while Finding is still the subscriber: `ApiRideRealtime` maps a matched→searching projection to `cancelledByDriver` (api_ride_realtime.dart 193-199), and Finding stays subscribed after an accept whenever `_completeAssigned` is deferred (`_assignmentPending` because an offer raise/pickup edit or a cancel is in flight, 939-945) or during the `_persistAssigned` await before `_openWaiting` disposes the controller.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider raises the offer; while the PATCH is out a driver accepts and immediately drops the ride. The next poll delivers `cancelledByDriver` to Finding: the ride is filed in History as cancelled, the snapshot is cleared and the rider is sent Home, although the server trip is still searching and may be accepted by another driver.

Kept in [RideStatusX.isTerminal] only so the UI stops tracking the old driver; it is never a terminal status on the wire.'
confirmed.suggested_fix: In the Finding listener treat `cancelledByDriver` as 'back to searching' (reset `_assigned`/`_assignmentPending`, keep the search) instead of routing it to `_completeTerminal`.

verdicts.corrected_title: Finding treats a driver drop (cancelledByDriver) that arrives while a match is deferred as the end of the ride: it archives the ride as cancelled, clears the snapshot and sends the rider Home while the server trip is searching again
verdicts.reason: The Finding listener ignores events only when `_disposed || _cancelled || _terminated` (finding_driver_controller.dart:363). It does not check `_assigned`, and the only filter for assigned rides is `_assigned && status == driverAssigned` (381). A `cancelledByDriver` event (api_ride_realtime.dart:193-199 maps matched->searching to it) passes `backendReconcile`, because driverAssigned->cancelledByDriver is legal (ride_transition.dart:55-58). It is `isTerminal` (ride_status.dart:62), so it goes to `_completeTerminal` (394-397). That method guards only on terminated/cancelled/disposed/!isTerminal (1006), archives cancelledByDriver to History (1027-1035), clears the snapshot (1037) and fires onTerminal. `_handleTerminal` then shows the terminal sheet and calls `RideNavigator.home` (finding_drivers.dart:331-334). Finding is disposed only inside `_openWaiting` (finding_drivers.dart:528). The match is deferred whenever `_drainDeferredNavigation` returns early because the route is not current or `_pickupEditOpen` is true (finding_drivers.dart:269-276), for example while the route-change page from `_changeRoute` is open (665). It is also deferred while `_editInFlight`/`_cancelInFlight` sets `_assignmentPending` (939-945). In all of these windows the subscription is still live. The intended handling is a reversible re-dispatch: Waiting re-searches (active_ride_controller.dart:327, ride_status.dart:31-35).
verdicts.repro: Static trace: listener 361-401 -> _completeTerminal 1005-1045 -> FindingDrivers onTerminal 235-239 -> _drainDeferredNavigation 278-283 -> _handleTerminal 319-335. Deferred-match paths: _changeRoute 655-698 and _completeAssigned 937-945. No throwaway test was run for this one.

verdicts.reason: In finding_driver_controller.dart:394-397 the Finding listener sends any `isTerminal` status to `_completeTerminal`. `cancelledByDriver` is in `isTerminal` (core/contracts/ride_status.dart:31-36, where the comment says it is never terminal on the wire). `_completeTerminal` (1009-1046) archives it as a cancelled ride at 1028, clears the snapshot and calls `_onTerminal`. `_onTerminal` (finding_drivers.dart:316-334) shows the 'Driver cancelled / Continue' sheet and then `RideNavigator.home`. Finding stays subscribed after a match while an edit or cancel is in flight, because `_completeAssigned` (937-945) only sets `_assignmentPending` and returns. In production `ApiRideRealtime` (api_ride_realtime.dart:193-199) turns a matched-to-searching projection into `cancelledByDriver`, and it does the same for an admin reassign; only the event kind differs. No guard drops the event: the gate passes it and `backendReconcile` accepts it. The server trip is still searching, but the rider is sent Home with no snapshot, so a driver who accepts next has no rider screen. The race window is narrow: a driver must accept and then drop inside one PATCH or cancel round-trip, with a 2 s poll interval. That makes it an edge path, so medium rather than high.
verdicts.repro: I wrote a throwaway test, test/_audit_r32_test.dart (since deleted). It uses a fake RideRealtime, an http client that holds the PATCH open, and a capturing historyArchiveWriter. It calls `startFrom`, then `confirmPriceIncreaseBy(Money(1000,'SEK'))` while the PATCH is pending, then emits driverAssigned (seq 1) followed by cancelledByDriver (seq 2). Output: `editInFlight=true`, `after assign: matched=0 ride=RideStatus.driverAssigned`, `terminal=RideStatus.cancelledByDriver archived=[RideStatus.cancelledByDriver] snapshot=null`, `raise=false`. All tests passed.

confirmed.title: Home's load() keeps only the first 8 custom places and every Home persist() writes that cut list back, so places 9 and later are deleted from storage

Home's long-press passes only the type: saved_places_row.dart:108-110 calls onEditSavedPlace('custom', customType: place.type), which goes home.dart _editSavedPlace -> _showAddressPicker -> _saveAddressFor -> applyResolved. applyResolved matches the first place of that type (home_places_controller.dart:131-142) and then persists (home.dart:496).
