confirmed.title: Late first GPS fix glides whichever map is on top (pickup / Set pickup / Select ride), not Home's
confirmed.description: _runDetectCurrentAddress ends with `AppScope.instance.maps.animateCamera(target, zoom: homeOpeningZoom, follow: true)` with no check that Home's map is the active owner. While Home is parked (NAV-3 or _withParkedHomeMap) its controller is detached (home.dart:233) and GoogleMapProvider.controller returns `_owners.last.controller` (google_map_provider.dart:24-25), i.e. the map of ConfirmPickupSpot (owner 'pickup', confirm_pickup_spot.dart:333), SetPickupPage (set_pickup_page.dart:870) or SelectRide. _mayMove(map, follow:true) only checks heldByRider (google_map_provider.dart:79-85), so the booking screen's camera eases to the rider's GPS point at zoom 11.7. The sibling path _centerCameraOnQuickFix explicitly guards `if (maps.activeOwner != MapOwners.home) return;` (home.dart:312), showing this guard was intended. detectCurrent can take up to 16 s (detectFixTimeout) while _awaitCurrentFix gives up after 8 s and the flow continues with the fallback pickup, so the fix routinely lands after the rider is on a map screen.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Cold start on web/Safari, slow first fix. Rider taps Where to, picks a destination; _awaitCurrentFix times out at 8 s, SelectRide opens, rider taps Book, Set pickup opens with the fallback pin. At ~12 s the fix lands: Set pickup's camera glides to the GPS point at city zoom 11.7; onCameraMove recomputes _center, _onCameraIdle sets _routeStart/_usable=true, re-resolves the address and re-quotes. The pickup silently moved under the rider; in ConfirmPickupSpot the pin likewise jumps and the shown address changes.
confirmed.evidence:
home.dart:395-399 `await AppScope.instance.maps.animateCamera(GeoPoint(target.latitude, target.longitude), zoom: homeOpeningZoom, follow: true);`
home.dart:311-312 `// Map not created yet: onMapCreated picks the hint up.` / `if (maps.activeOwner != MapOwners.home) return;` (quick fix is guarded, accurate fix is not)
google_map_provider.dart:24-25 `GoogleMapController? get controller => _owners.isEmpty ? null : _owners.last.controller;`
google_map_provider.dart:81 `if (follow) return !view.heldByRider;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: In _runDetectCurrentAddress skip the animateCamera when `_mapParked.value || AppScope.instance.maps.activeOwner != MapOwners.home` (onMapCreated already re-centres from _currentLatLng when Home's map comes back).

verdicts.reason: _runDetectCurrentAddress ends with maps.animateCamera(..., zoom: homeOpeningZoom, follow: true) (home.dart:395-399) and does not check who owns the map. When Home parks, its owner is detached (home.dart:233), and GoogleMapProvider.controller then returns _owners.last.controller (google_map_provider.dart:24-25). That is SelectRide's map (select_ride.dart:1713) or Set pickup's (set_pickup_page.dart:870). _mayMove with follow only checks heldByRider (google_map_provider.dart:79-81), so a map nobody has touched is moved. The sibling quick-fix path does have the guard (home.dart:312). The timing is reachable. _awaitCurrentFix gives up after 8 s (home.dart:338), and _prefillPickup (home.dart:817-821) then carries on with a fallback pickup while detectCurrent can still run for up to detectFixTimeout = 16 s (home_controller.dart:221). A rider who answers Safari's prompt late hits this too. On Set pickup, onCameraMove recomputes _center (set_pickup_page.dart:873-879), and _onCameraIdle then sets _routeStart and _usable=true, re-resolves the address and re-quotes (set_pickup_page.dart:489-507). The pickup therefore moves to wherever the zoom-11.7 camera put the pin, without the rider doing anything.
verdicts.repro: Static trace through home.dart:376-399, 806-821 and 1039-1041 (_withParkedHomeMap before SelectRide), home.dart:226-233 (_parkHomeMap detaches the home owner), google_map_provider.dart:24-27, 79-108, map_camera_motion.dart:61-65 (heldByRider is false on an untouched map), and set_pickup_page.dart:489-507, 866-882. There is no check of activeOwner or _mapParked before the animateCamera.

verdicts.reason: `_runDetectCurrentAddress` always ends with `AppScope.instance.maps.animateCamera(target, zoom: homeOpeningZoom /*11.7*/, follow: true)` (home.dart:395-399). It never checks `_mapParked` or `activeOwner`. A parked Home detaches its own controller (home.dart:233). `GoogleMapProvider.controller` then returns `_owners.last` (google_map_provider.dart:24-25), which is the selectRide or pickup map (select_ride.dart:1713, set_pickup_page.dart:870, confirm_pickup_spot.dart:333). With follow:true, `_mayMove` only refuses while `heldByRider`, which means a finger on the map or a hand move in the last 12 s (google_map_provider.dart:79-81, map_camera_motion.dart:61-65). Nothing cancels the detect when Home parks: pauseLiveUpdates only sets a flag (home_controller.dart:737). The late fix is realistic: requestPermission has no timeout, getCurrentPosition can take up to 16 s (detectFixTimeout), and `_awaitCurrentFix` gives up after 8 s, after which the flow carries on to SelectRide and Set pickup. When the fix lands, SelectRide's route framing or Set pickup's pin eases to the GPS point at city zoom 11.7. Set pickup's onCameraMove and _onCameraIdle then move `_routeStart`, set `_usable=true`, re-resolve the address and re-quote (set_pickup_page.dart:489-506, 873-882). The quick-fix path has this guard (home.dart:312); the accurate-fix path does not.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand: a test cannot attach a real GoogleMapController (debugAttach stores a null controller, so animateCamera returns early). Chain: _awaitCurrentFix gives up at the 8 s deadline (home.dart:341) → fallback PickupMapResult (home.dart:818-822) → SelectRide or SetPickupPage attaches its map → the detect future resolves → animateCamera on maps.controller, now the other screen's map → easeCameraTo moves it (map_camera_motion.dart:302-340).

confirmed.title: A failed forward geocode after the route picker closes, or when a saved place is tapped, aborts the flow silently with an unhandled async error
confirmed.description: After RoutePickerPage pops with a draft, _showRouteAddressPicker runs `Future.wait([_normaliseAddress(rawPickup...), _normaliseAddress(rawDestination...), ...])`. HomeLocationController.normaliseAddress calls `geocoding.forward(clean)` with no try/catch (home_controller.dart:258); AppGeocoding._forwardFromApi does `api.post(...).timeout(requestTimeout)` and ApiClient._send throws ApiError on HTTP >= 400, NETWORK and TIMEOUT (api_client.dart:98, 123, 131). The exception propagates through _handleDestinationTap -> _runRouteFlow (finally only resets the flag) -> WhereToCard.onTap, which is a VoidCallback, so it becomes an unhandled zone error. Nothing is shown to the rider, nothing is persisted and SelectRide never opens. The picker itself catches onFinish failures (route_picker_page.dart:408-411) but this post-pop step does not. Same unguarded pattern: _useSavedPlaceAsDestination (home.dart:545), _saveAddressFor (home.dart:469, 477), PickupMapController.search used by ConfirmPickupSpot._lookup (confirm_pickup_spot.dart:286) and SetPickupPage._searchAddress (set_pickup_page.dart:702).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider is offline or the geocode endpoint times out. They pick pickup and destination in the route picker (onFinish succeeds because resolvePlace is cached or the point came with the suggestion), the picker closes, the forward geocode of the raw strings throws, the flow aborts: Home shows the old sheet, no error, no SelectRide, Recents not updated. Tapping a saved place (Home/Work card) while offline likewise does nothing.
confirmed.evidence:
home.dart:952-959 `final normaliseBatch = _locationCtl.beginNormalisationBatch(); final normalizedRoute = await Future.wait<String>([ _normaliseAddress(rawPickup, generation: normaliseBatch), ...`
home_controller.dart:258 `final result = await geocoding.forward(clean);` (no try/catch)
api_client.dart:122-123 `if (response.statusCode >= 400) { throw _errorFromResponse(response, requestId); }` and :131 `throw ApiError(code: 'TIMEOUT', ...)`
where_to_card.dart:25 `final VoidCallback onDestinationTap;` (future dropped)
confirmed.suggested_fix: Wrap the post-pop normalisation (and the saved-place / favourite / pickup-search paths) in try/catch; on failure fall back to the raw strings (the draft already carries pickupLat/Lng and destinationLat/Lng) or show homeChooseValidRoute / routeCouldNotReach, instead of letting the exception escape.

verdicts.corrected_title: A failed forward geocode after the route picker closes, or when a saved place is tapped, aborts the flow silently with an unhandled async error
verdicts.reason: _showRouteAddressPicker awaits Future.wait of _normaliseAddress calls (home.dart:953-960). _normaliseAddress has no try/catch (home.dart:433-435), and neither does HomeLocationController.normaliseAddress (home_controller.dart:253-262). AppGeocoding.forward rethrows (app_geocoding.dart:46-64). _forwardFromApi goes through ApiClient._send, which throws ApiError on HTTP 400 or above and on TIMEOUT (api_client.dart:122-123, 131). _request (api_client.dart:155-161) also lets the http ClientException through when the device is offline. _runRouteFlow only resets its flag in finally (home.dart:692-701). The error goes to PlatformDispatcher.onError, which only logs it (bootstrap.dart:102-105), so the rider sees nothing and SelectRide never opens. A pickup or destination that arrived with a point never went through forward() inside onFinish (home.dart:784-788, 841), so it is not in the cache and the post-pop call goes to the network. The saved-place path (home.dart:545) fails the same way. The demo's in-process mock always answers a non-empty query (in_process_mock_client.dart:337-360), so this only happens against a real server. Offline or a server timeout is enough to trigger it there.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: home.dart:933-960, 433-435, 502-521, 538-546, 692-701; home_controller.dart:253-262; app_geocoding.dart:46-64, 94-107; api_client.dart:70-161; bootstrap.dart:102-105. No catch exists anywhere between the geocoder and the VoidCallback.

verdicts.reason: After RoutePickerPage pops, `_showRouteAddressPicker` awaits `Future.wait([_normaliseAddress(rawPickup), _normaliseAddress(rawDestination), ...])` with no try/catch (home.dart:952-959). HomeLocationController.normaliseAddress awaits `geocoding.forward` unguarded (home_controller.dart:258). AppGeocoding.forward rethrows API, timeout and transport errors (app_geocoding.dart:46-64, 94-98). No caller catches: _handleDestinationTap has try/finally only (home.dart:502-519), as does _runRouteFlow (home.dart:692-701). WhereToCard.onDestinationTap is a VoidCallback, so the returned future is dropped (where_to_card.dart:25, 54) and the error goes to the zone as an unhandled exception. The booking ends silently: no message, SelectRide never opens, Recents are not updated. The draft already has pickupLat/Lng and destinationLat/Lng, so the geocode is only cosmetic. In the common case (pickup from GPS, destination from a suggestion) onFinish never calls forward on these strings, so the cache does not save it. Only the in-process demo mock never fails. Staging and production go over HTTP.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway unit test test/_audit_rider45_test.dart (now deleted): HomeLocationController with AppGeocoding(api: ApiClient(client: MockClient(...))) calling normaliseAddress('Sveavägen 12, Stockholm'). Output: `mode=503 threw=ApiError: ApiError(UNAVAILABLE, Request failed, ...)` and `mode=offline threw=ClientException: ClientException: Failed host lookup`. The rest of the chain up to the VoidCallback I traced by hand.

confirmed.title: 'Use current location' row saves the placeholder 'Location off, set pickup' as Home/Work and into Recents
confirmed.description: When location is off/denied, _runDetectCurrentAddress and _resetPickupLabel set _pickupAddress = locationOffPickupLabel. _placeOrNull only filters '' and 'Current location' (home.dart:524-528), so in _showAddressPicker the 'Use current location' row is enabled and pops that placeholder string; _saveAddressFor normalises it and applyResolved stores it as homeAddress/workAddress and calls remember(address), whose own filter also only knows 'Current location' (home_places_controller.dart:86). Home's _rememberAddress guard (isPlaceholderPickupLabel, home.dart:449) is bypassed on this path. Reproduced: applyResolved(target:'home', address: locationOffPickupLabel) -> `home=Location off, set pickup recents=[Location off, set pickup]`.

Rider long-presses the Home card, sees 'Use current location' with subtitle 'Location off, set pickup', taps it: Home address becomes 'Location off, set pickup', it shows on the Home card and in Recents, and tapping the Home card later feeds that text to the geocoder as a destination.

confirmed.title: Zone wall-clock pickup time is stored as a device-local DateTime and compared with DateTime.now()
confirmed.description: Q9 makes every Book-later time the pickup zone's wall-clock time: `ZoneClock.wallTime` returns a plain local `DateTime(local.year, …)` (zone_clock.dart:57-69) and `PickupSchedule` works in those (stockholm_schedule.dart:105-121). The picker returns that wall-clock value (select_date_time.dart:131, 153-158) and it flows unchanged into `ReservationDraft.scheduledPickupAt` (scheduled_ride_checkout.dart:21-32). The backend path converts it to a UTC instant (`PickupSchedule(timezone).toUtc(at)`, scheduled_rides_controller.dart:63-64), but the local reservation path never does: `startLiveIfDue` computes `ride.scheduledPickupAt.difference(currentTime)` with `currentTime = DateTime.now()` (334, 329), the chrono counts down with `DateTime.now()` (home_reservation_chrono.dart:206, 242-249; reservation_format.dart:99,117), `isNoDriverFound` (313-316) and the cancel-fee window (scheduled_ride_rules.dart:93-103) do the same. Whenever the device time zone differs from the pickup zone's (any browser outside CET on the public web build; a Stockholm phone booking a Tunis pickup in summer; a traveller abroad), every one of these is off by the offset. Throwaway test in this UTC container: minimumPickup() for 10:00Z gives wall-clock 12:30 (local, isUtc=false); `pickup.difference(now)` = 2:30:00 and the chrono label reads `2h 30m` for a ride 30 minutes away.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Web rider with browser in UTC (or a Stockholm phone in Tunis zone in summer) books a Stockholm pickup for 12:30 local (30 min ahead). Home chrono shows 2 h 30 m; `startLiveIfDue` reaches T-2 two hours after the real pickup; "No driver found" fires two hours late; free-cancel window shown/charged against the wrong instant.
confirmed.evidence:
zone_clock.dart:57-69 `static DateTime wallTime(...) { ... return DateTime(local.year, local.month, local.day, local.hour, ...); }`
select_date_time.dart:131 `Navigator.pop(context, _selectedDateTime);`
scheduled_ride_checkout.dart:31 `scheduledPickupAt: when,`
reservation_controller.dart:329-334 `final currentTime = now ?? _clock(); ... final untilPickup = ride.scheduledPickupAt.difference(currentTime);`
home_reservation_chrono.dart:206 `DateTime get _now => widget.now?.call() ?? DateTime.now();`
scheduled_rides_controller.dart:63-64 `scheduledAt: switch (scheduledAt) { final at? => WireTime.format(PickupSchedule(timezone).toUtc(at)), ... }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Convert the picked wall-clock time to an instant (`PickupSchedule(timeZone).toUtc(when)`) before building the ReservationDraft, and render it back with `ZoneClock.wallTime` in the reservation screens; or store the IANA zone with the reservation and use it in every comparison.

verdicts.reason: PickupSchedule works in zone wall-clock values. zoneNow returns ZoneClock.wallTime, a plain local DateTime (zone_clock.dart:57-69; stockholm_schedule.dart:29-35). The picker returns that value (select_date_time.dart:131), and it goes unchanged into ReservationDraft.scheduledPickupAt (scheduled_ride_checkout.dart:21-31) and into ReservationPatch on edit (scheduled_ride_booking.dart:62-65). Nothing in the reservation path calls toUtc or PickupSchedule.toUtc. The only conversion is on the backend path, as the finding says. The stored value is then compared with the device clock in three places: startLiveIfDue (reservation_controller.dart:329,334), isNoDriverFound (:313-316) and the home chrono (DateTime.now()). LocalReservationRepository is the live store whenever scheduledRides/bookingLater is on or the build is not release (di.dart:143-146). So any device whose time zone differs from the pickup zone gets the T-2 start, the no-driver timeout, the countdown and the cancel window all off by the offset difference. Q9 makes pickup-zone wall time the intended display and input format, but it does not make the comparison against device-local now correct.
verdicts.repro: Wrote throwaway test test/_audit_r63tz_test.dart (since deleted), run in this UTC container: computed PickupSchedule.stockholm.minimumPickup(DateTime.now()) and its difference from now. Output: `tzOffset=0:00:00.000000 pickup=2026-10-21 04:00:00.000 isUtc=false diff=2:32:55.837967` then `00:00 +1: All tests passed!`. A pickup about 30 minutes away in Stockholm measures as about 2h33m against the device clock.

verdicts.reason: The picked Book-later time is a zone wall-clock value with no offset. ZoneClock.wallTime (lib/core/config/zone_clock.dart:57-69) returns a plain local DateTime, PickupSchedule.minimumPickup builds on it (stockholm_schedule.dart:33), and the picker pops it unchanged (select_date_time.dart:131). It reaches ReservationDraft.scheduledPickupAt unconverted (scheduled_ride_booking.dart:44,82; scheduled_ride_checkout.dart:31). ReservationController then compares it with DateTime.now() as if it were device-local time: isNoDriverFound at reservation_controller.dart:313-316, startLiveIfDue at :329-334, and ReservationFormat.remainingCompact/remainingParts at reservation_format.dart:99,117. Nothing calls PickupSchedule.toUtc on this path. Only the backend scheduled_rides_controller converts. The path is live: demo/dev builds, including the public Pages demo (publish-web-live.yml:45-49, MOVERA_FLAVOR=demo), get LocalReservationRepository plus ReservationController (di.dart:142-176). It only goes wrong when the device zone differs from the pickup zone (a traveller, a browser outside CET, or a Stockholm phone with a Tunis pickup in summer). That makes it an edge path, so medium.

Device in UTC: 'minimumPickup wall=2026-10-21 04:05:00.000 isUtc=false', 'untilPickup=2:30:31', 'true instant=2026-10-21 02:05:00.000Z, true until=0:30:31', 'isNoDriverFound at real+40min: false', 'chrono label: 2h 30m'. Same test with TZ=Europe/Stockholm: 'untilPickup=0:30:23', 'isNoDriverFound at real+40min: true', 'chrono label: 30m'. Both runs: '+1: All tests passed!'.

confirmed.title: Pickup and creation times are persisted as offset-less local ISO strings, so a device time-zone change moves the booked pickup instant
confirmed.original_title: Pickup and creation times are persisted as offset-less local ISO strings, so a device time-zone change moves the booked pickup instant
confirmed.description: toJson writes scheduledPickupAt, createdAt and estimatedDropoffAt with DateTime.toIso8601String(). For a local DateTime (what the booking flow passes) that gives '2026-10-22T10:00:00.000' with no offset. tryParse (DateTime.tryParse) reads it back as local time in whatever zone the device is in at hydrate. cancelledAt is stored as UTC (local_reservation_repository.dart:232), so only some timestamps keep their instant. This is the persistence side, separate from the known zone wall-clock construction issue at line 334: even a booking made correctly in the device zone changes instant after a zone change and an app restart. ARCHITECTURE.md names WireTime (RFC 3339 UTC) as the time contract.
confirmed.failure_scenario: In Stockholm (UTC+2) the rider books 10:00 tomorrow, stored as '...T10:00:00.000' (08:00Z). They fly to London (UTC+1) and relaunch. Hydrate parses 10:00 London time = 09:00Z. The chrono counts down to a pickup an hour late, startLiveIfDue starts assignment and en-route an hour late, and the free-cancel window and fee are worked out against the wrong instant.
confirmed.evidence:
reservation.dart:368-371:
  'createdAt': createdAt.toIso8601String(),
  'scheduledPickupAt': scheduledPickupAt.toIso8601String(),
  if (estimatedDropoffAt != null) 'estimatedDropoffAt': estimatedDropoffAt!.toIso8601String(),
reservation.dart:407-410: DateTime.tryParse(map['createdAt'] ...), DateTime.tryParse(map['scheduledPickupAt'] ...)
confirmed.suggested_fix: Serialize with toUtc().toIso8601String() (WireTime) and convert to local only for display.

verdicts.reason: The pickup time is a local DateTime. select_date_time.dart:284 and :443 build it with `DateTime(...)` and scheduleFor passes it on (select_ride.dart:952, ride_selection_controller.dart:620). It reaches the repository unchanged (local_reservation_repository.dart:167). toJson (reservation.dart:368-371) writes toIso8601String() with no offset, and tryParse (reservation.dart:407-410) reads it back as local time in the device zone at hydrate. No toUtc() is applied on the write path, while cancelledAt is stored as UTC (local_reservation_repository.dart:232). ARCHITECTURE.md:83 names WireTime (RFC 3339 UTC) as the contract. Nothing in DECISIONS.md makes local storage intentional. A device zone change followed by a restart moves the stored instant, and isNoDriverFound and startLiveIfDue (reservation_controller.dart:306-372) then use the shifted time. It needs a device time-zone change, so it is an edge path.
verdicts.repro: Read-only static trace of the booking path from the date picker to the repository, then toJson and tryParse. Worked by hand: '2026-10-22T10:00:00.000' stored at UTC+2 (08:00Z) and parsed at UTC+1 gives 09:00Z.

verdicts.reason: reservation.dart:368-371 serialises createdAt, scheduledPickupAt and estimatedDropoffAt with toIso8601String(). For a local (non-UTC) DateTime, Dart writes no offset or Z. tryParse at reservation.dart:407-410 uses DateTime.tryParse, which reads an offset-less string as local time in the device's zone at hydrate time. cancelledAt, by contrast, is written as UTC (local_reservation_repository.dart:232). Every check that uses the instant (isNoDriverFound at reservation_controller.dart:306-316, startLiveIfDue's untilPickup at :334, the chrono countdown) compares against DateTime.now(), so after a zone change and an app restart the pickup instant moves by the offset difference. ARCHITECTURE.md:83 names WireTime (RFC 3339 UTC) as the contract, and DECISIONS.md does not exempt this. It only happens when a rider with a pending booking changes zone and restarts, so I rate it an edge path (medium).
verdicts.repro: Read only, no run. Dart semantics: DateTime(2026,10,22,10).toIso8601String() gives '2026-10-22T10:00:00.000' with no Z. DateTime.parse of that string in Europe/London (UTC+1 on 22 Oct) gives 09:00Z, versus 08:00Z when written in Stockholm (UTC+2): a shift of one hour.

confirmed.title: Cancelling a reservation from its live screen skips the reservation late-cancel terms, so no fee is recorded
confirmed.description: The Upcoming page computes the terms and passes the agreed fee: `cancelTermsFor(ride)` then `_reservations.cancel(id, reason:, fee: terms.fee)` (upcoming_reservation.dart:131-142). The two other cancel entry points for the same reservation never pass a fee: `ReservationLiveRide.onCancel` calls `reservations.cancel(ride.reservationId, reason: reasonId ?? 'rider_cancelled_live')` (78-85) and `ReservationRideRealtime.cancelRide` does the same (reservation_ride_realtime.dart:255-265). The live screen is exactly where the rider is once the driver is en route (T-2 min, `startLiveIfDue` 383-394 + chrono `_openLiveIfNeeded`), i.e. inside the late-cancel window the rules define (scheduled_ride_rules.dart:86-118, default 60 min / 50 kr). The cancelled ride is then saved with `cancellationFee == null`, History shows plain "Cancelled" (reservation_format.dart:27-33) and no fee is recorded, while the same cancel five minutes earlier from the Upcoming page records 50 kr.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rules: free until 60 min before pickup, 50 kr after. Rider lets the driver start (T-2), the live screen opens, taps Cancel: the ride is cancelled with no fee recorded; History and the receipt show no fee, contradicting the terms the rider was shown.
confirmed.evidence:
reservation_live_ride.dart:78-82 `onCancel: (context, reasonId) async { await reservations.cancel(ride.reservationId, reason: reasonId ?? 'rider_cancelled_live'); ...`
reservation_ride_realtime.dart:259-263 `unawaited(controller.cancel(reservationId, reason: 'rider_cancelled_live'));`
upcoming_reservation.dart:131-142 `final terms = _reservations.cancelTermsFor(ride); ... await _reservations.cancel(ride.reservationId, reason: outcome.reasonId, fee: terms.fee);`

verdicts.corrected_title: Cancelling a reservation from its live screen skips the reservation late-cancel terms, so no fee is recorded
verdicts.reason: The Upcoming page computes the terms and passes them on: cancelTermsFor, then cancel(..., fee: terms.fee) (upcoming_reservation.dart:131-142). The live-screen handler only calls reservations.cancel(ride.reservationId, reason: reasonId ?? 'rider_cancelled_live') (reservation_live_ride.dart:78-82), with no fee. ReservationController.cancel (reservation_controller.dart:208-235) does not compute a fee itself, and LocalReservationRepository.cancelReservation (local_reservation_repository.dart:220-237) stores cancellationFee: null when no fee is passed. The live screen opens when the driver starts, near pickup time (startLiveIfDue, reservation_controller.dart:328). That is always inside the default 60-minute late window, and ScheduledRideRules.cancelTermsFor (scheduled_ride_rules.dart:86-118) would charge there because a driver is assigned (missedByMovera is false). The live sheet's fee note comes from the Book Now live rules (waiting_for_driver.dart:765-799, LiveCancelFeePreview), not from the reservation terms. Per API_V1_MOCK.md:76 the late-cancel fee is only recorded on the device copy and charged nowhere yet. So the effect is a wrong or missing fee record and receipt, not money actually taken, which is why this is medium.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: ReservationLiveRide -> WaitingForDriver(onCancel) -> _confirmCancel (waiting_for_driver.dart:802-830) -> customCancel -> ReservationController.cancel(fee: null) -> LocalReservationRepository.cancelReservation. Compared this with upcoming_reservation.dart:131-142 and the scheduled terms in contracts/CONTRACT.md:133. I did not run a test.

verdicts.corrected_title: Cancelling a reservation from the live (driver en route) screen records no late-cancel fee, while the same cancel from Upcoming records the rule's fee
verdicts.reason: ReservationLiveRide.onCancel (reservation_live_ride.dart:78-82) and ReservationRideRealtime.cancelRide (reservation_ride_realtime.dart:141-150) call reservations.cancel without `fee`. LocalReservationRepository.cancelReservation then stores cancellationFee=null (local_reservation_repository.dart:220-235). UpcomingReservation._cancel computes cancelTermsFor and passes terms.fee (upcoming_reservation.dart:131-142). The live screen opens when the driver is en route, around T-2 min, which is inside the default 60-minute window. There, cancelTermsFor works out a positive fee (scheduled_ride_rules.dart:86-118): minutesBeforePickup=2 < freeMin=60 gives 5000 minor (50 kr), and missedByMovera is false because a driver is assigned. WaitingForDriver._cancelFeeNote (waiting_for_driver.dart:765-800) uses the Book-now LiveCancelFeePreview, not the reservation terms, so the live sheet never states the 50 kr either. History then shows plain resCancelled instead of resCancelledFee (reservation_format.dart:27-32). Reservations are local-only, so nothing is actually charged. The harm is that the recorded and displayed fee contradicts the rules, not a wrong charge, so I rate it medium.
verdicts.repro: Worked by hand with the defaults (ScheduledRideRules: freeCancelMinutesBeforePickup=60, lateCancelFee=Money(5000)): scheduledPickupAt.difference(now).inMinutes = 2, so CancelFeeCalculator.reservation returns 5000 minor, charged=true and terms.fee=50 kr. The live path passes fee=null, and `fee != null && fee.isPositive ? fee : null` stores null. No test was run.

confirmed.title: A leftover suppressRestore from a ride closed earlier makes resumeIfNeeded delete a just-adopted server trip on a push tap, so the ride does not open
confirmed.description: `RideSession.suppressRestore` is set true by every terminal `localTransition`/`backendReconcile` (ride_session.dart 82, 148) and is only reset by a non-terminal transition or `reset()` (sign-out wipe). After the rider closes or cancels a ride on this device the flag stays true indefinitely. `openRideFromNotification` → `_openRide` (notification_navigation.dart 88-125) reads no snapshot, calls `adoptServerActiveTrip(expectedRideId)` which saves the server trip as the snapshot (ride_restore_coordinator.dart 78-100), then calls `resumeIfNeeded()`. `resumeIfNeeded` reads the new snapshot, resyncs, and then hits `if (AppScope.instance.ride.suppressRestore) { unawaited(RideSnapshotStore.clear()); return null; }` (595-598): the just-adopted trip is deleted and nothing opens, although the flag belongs to a different, finished ride. The cold-start path (`_root` → `pageFor`) has no such check, so the same trip is restored after a restart.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Release build (ApiActiveTripRepository): rider finishes ride A on their phone (Done → closed). Later they book ride B on the web; the push for B taps on the phone. `_openRide` adopts B from the server, then `resumeIfNeeded` clears it and returns; the rider sees Home with no ride, and 'This ride has ended.' may be shown by `openNotificationRide`.
confirmed.evidence: ride_session.dart:82 `suppressRestore = status.isTerminal;` and 148 `suppressRestore = backendStatus.isTerminal;` ; ride_restore_coordinator.dart:595-598 `if (AppScope.instance.ride.suppressRestore) { unawaited(RideSnapshotStore.clear()); return null; }` ; notification_navigation.dart:93-96 `await RideSnapshotStore.read() ?? await RideRestoreCoordinator.instance.adoptServerActiveTrip(expectedRideId: expected)` then 123 `await RideRestoreCoordinator.instance.resumeIfNeeded();`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Scope `suppressRestore` to the ride id it was set for (ignore it when the snapshot's rideId differs from `session.rideId`), or clear it in `adoptServerActiveTrip`.

verdicts.reason: Once a ride ends, nothing clears the restore-suppress flag. markClosed/closeCompletedRide (active_ride_controller.dart:442/459) call localTransition(closed), which sets suppressRestore=true (ride_session.dart:82). The only resets are a non-terminal transition or reset() on sign-out wipe (ride_session.dart:210, user_data_wipe.dart:120), and Home calls neither. On a push tap, _openRide (notification_navigation.dart:88-124) adopts the server trip B as the snapshot. resumeIfNeeded then calls _resync(B), which does nothing for a ride the polling transport has no poll for (api_ride_realtime.dart:380-381). It reaches `if (AppScope.instance.ride.suppressRestore) { RideSnapshotStore.clear(); return null; }` (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:595-598), deletes the snapshot it just adopted and opens nothing. The cold path _root -> pageFor has no such check. One detail in the finding is off: openRideFromNotification returns true here, so 'This ride has ended' is not shown. The rider just stays on Home with nothing opened.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_r67_test.dart (since deleted). A RideRestoreCoordinator with an ApiActiveTripRepository over InProcessMockClient holds ride_b=driverAssigned, debugAtRoot=true and onReplaceRoot captured. Without a prior ride: 'page=WaitingForDriver replaced=WaitingForDriver snapshotAfter=ride_b'. After backendReconcile(tripCompleted, id:'ride_a') + localTransition(closed): 'suppress=true ... adopted=ride_b surface=RestoredSurface.waiting / page=null replaced=null snapshotAfter=null'. Both tests passed (the prints are the evidence).
verdicts.corrected_title: A leftover suppressRestore from a ride closed earlier makes resumeIfNeeded delete a just-adopted server trip on a push tap, so the ride does not open

verdicts.reason: suppressRestore is in-memory and only goes back to false on a non-terminal transition or on reset() (ride_session.dart:82,148,210). The only caller of reset() is the sign-out wipe (user_data_wipe.dart:120). So after the rider cancels or closes ride A (finding_driver_controller.dart:969, active_ride_controller.dart:442/459), the flag stays true for the rest of the process. When a push for ride B (booked on another device) is tapped, _openRide (notification_navigation.dart:88-124) finds no local snapshot and adoptServerActiveTrip saves B (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:77-90). resumeIfNeeded then runs into `if (AppScope.instance.ride.suppressRestore) { clear(); return null; }` (595-598) and deletes B before surfaceFor/pageFor runs. Nothing resets the flag on the way. In the release ApiRideRealtime, reconnectAndResync returns early when nothing is subscribed to that ride (api_ride_realtime.dart:380-381), so backendReconcile never runs for B and never sets the flag back to false. One part of the description is wrong: _openRide still returns true (line 124), so the 'This ride has ended.' toast does not appear. The rider just stays on Home with no ride, and B's snapshot is gone until a cold start adopts it again from the server.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_r67_test.dart (now deleted) using the real ApiActiveTripRepository over InProcessMockClient, with the server returning ride_B in findingDriver. Control run with suppressRestore false: 'resume page=FindingDrivers replaced=FindingDrivers snapshotAfter=ride_B showing=RestoredSurface.finding'. Stale run, after backendReconcile(findingDriver, id: ride_A) then localTransition(cancelledByRider): 'suppressRestore before=true rideId=ride_A ... adopted=ride_B surface=RestoredSurface.finding / resume page=Null replaced=Null snapshotAfter=null showing=RestoredSurface.home'. Both tests passed, so the adopted trip was wiped.

confirmed.title: A terminal status (e.g. paymentFailed) reconciled during the Waiting->RideCompleted handoff makes closeCompletedRide throw InvalidRideTransition, so Done and Back both fail with a misleading 'feedback could not be saved' and the rider cannot leave
confirmed.description: `_leave` wraps feedback submission and `closeCompletedRide` in one try/catch; any throw from the latter sets `_submitError = context.l10n.feedbackSaveFailed` and `_leaving = false` (259-265), and both Done and Back route through `_leave`, so the rider can never leave. `closeCompletedRide` can throw after the feedback was accepted: `localTransition(RideStatus.closed)` (active_ride_controller.dart 459) throws `InvalidRideTransition` when the session is already terminal, which happens when a `paymentFailed` (or other terminal) projection is reconciled by the still-live `DriverTrackingController` during the Waiting→RideCompleted `pushReplacement` handoff (RideCompleted's own listener ignores non-completed statuses, 123-127, so the screen keeps showing 'Trip complete'); `archive` can also throw its `StateError` after six lost writes (on_demand_ride_history_store.dart 172-176). The message then blames the rating/tip, which was in fact sent (`_acceptedFeedbackIntent` is set).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Payment fails on the server right as Waiting hands over to the summary. The rider rates the driver and taps Done: the rating is sent, then 'Your feedback could not be saved' appears every time, and neither Done nor Back leaves the screen.
confirmed.evidence: ride_completed.dart:252-265 `await _controller.closeCompletedRide(widget.rideId!); ... } catch (_) { ... _leaving = false; _submitError = context.l10n.feedbackSaveFailed;` ; active_ride_controller.dart:459 `AppScope.instance.ride.localTransition(RideStatus.closed);` ; ride_transition.dart:141-145 `if (from.isTerminal) return false;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Separate the two failure classes: keep the error only for a refused feedback submission, and make leaving tolerant (catch `InvalidRideTransition`/archive errors, clear the snapshot and still navigate Home).

verdicts.corrected_title: A terminal status (e.g. paymentFailed) reconciled during the Waiting->RideCompleted handoff makes closeCompletedRide throw InvalidRideTransition, so Done and Back both fail with a misleading 'feedback could not be saved' and the rider cannot leave
verdicts.reason: waiting_for_driver.dart:713-718 deliberately keeps the DriverTrackingController subscription alive through map parking and the pushReplacement; driver_tracking_controller.dart:118-124 reconciles every event into AppScope.instance.ride, and the resulting terminal tick is dropped by _drainStageNavigation because _completedOpened is already true (waiting_for_driver.dart:520-526). If paymentFailed arrives while the map parks, RideCompleted even opens at tripCompleted (720-723 fall back to `status`). RideCompleted's own listener ignores non-completed statuses (ride_completed.dart:123-127), so the screen still says the trip is complete. On Done or Back, _leave calls closeCompletedRide (ride_completed.dart:252-253), which calls localTransition(RideStatus.closed) (active_ride_controller.dart:459). canTransition refuses any terminal source (ride_transition.dart:141-142, paymentFailed is terminal per ride_status.dart:65), so InvalidRideTransition is thrown. The catch at ride_completed.dart:259-264 resets _leaving and shows feedbackSaveFailed. _store.clear never runs, so every retry throws the same way. PopScope(canPop:false) sends Back through _handleBack and then _leave(submitFeedback:false), which fails too. Unlike RideNavigator.home (ride_navigator.dart:29-39), closeCompletedRide has no canTransition guard.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: Waiting._openCompleted -> markCompleted/_parkMapForStageChange/pushReplacement while tracking stays subscribed -> DriverTrackingController backendReconcile(paymentFailed) -> RideCompleted._leave -> ActiveRideController.closeCompletedRide -> RideSession.localTransition -> transitionRide throws. I read every guard on the path (mounted, _leaving, _completedOpened, _completionRank, isCompletedSurface) and none prevents it. No test was run.

verdicts.corrected_title: A terminal status (e.g. paymentFailed) reconciled into RideSession during the Waiting to RideCompleted handoff makes closeCompletedRide throw InvalidRideTransition, so Done and Back both fail with the feedback/History error and the rider cannot leave
verdicts.reason: ride_completed.dart:252-265 runs closeCompletedRide inside the same try/catch as feedback, and any throw sets _leaving=false and shows feedbackSaveFailed. Back with nothing selected (_handleBack at :185) and Done both go through _leave. closeCompletedRide (active_ride_controller.dart:448-461) calls ride.localTransition(RideStatus.closed). That goes to transitionRide/canTransition (ride_transition.dart:133-145), which refuses any terminal `from`. paymentFailed is terminal (core/contracts/ride_status.dart:65). The bad state can be reached: Waiting._openCompleted (waiting_for_driver.dart:694-745) keeps its DriverTrackingController subscribed through markCompleted, map parking and pushReplacement. That tracker writes every event into the session with backendReconcile (driver_tracking_controller.dart:119-125), and Waiting ignores the terminal because _completedOpened is set (:515). RideCompleted is built with tripCompleted because tracked paymentFailed is not a completed surface (:716-719). Its initState and listener only accept completed-surface statuses (ride_completed.dart:113-127), so the screen shows 'Trip complete' while the session holds paymentFailed. The error text is 'Couldn't save your trip feedback or History' (app_en.arb:931), so it is only partly misleading. Restarting the app restores from the tripCompleted snapshot and lets the rider out, so the trap does not persist. The race window is short (handoff only), which makes this an edge path rather than a main path.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_r72b_test.dart, using the harness from test/ride/ride_completed_leave_without_saving_test.dart. It pushes RideCompleted(status: tripCompleted, persistOnDemandState default), then calls AppScope.instance.ride.backendReconcile(RideStatus.paymentFailed), the same call the live tracker makes, then taps Back twice. Output: 'try 0 home=false err=1 status=RideStatus.paymentFailed' / 'try 1 home=false err=1 status=RideStatus.paymentFailed'. The rider never reaches Home and the error shows every time. File deleted.

confirmed.title: Wallet is offered as the full payment method even when the fare is above the balance, and completing the ride drives the local wallet ledger negative (demo/dev builds, where the local wallet is enabled)
confirmed.description: The wallet row is listed whenever `walletBalance > 0` with no comparison against the fare (ride_selection_controller.dart:265-268), PayWithPage pops `'wallet'` on tap with no check (pay_with_page.dart:224-232), and `walletSplitFor` returns `WalletSplit.none` for the wallet method (200-202) so `walletAmountMinor` is 0 and the server-side range check in the mock (`walletMinor > serverTotal`) cannot catch it. At completion `RideCompleted._maybeChargeWallet` → `chargeCompletedRideById` → `chargeCompletedRide` charges `amount = snapshot.price` (wallet_controller.dart:282-283) and `LocalWalletRepository._apply` subtracts with no floor (wallet_repository.dart:215-218), so the stored balance becomes negative and WalletHome shows e.g. '-209 kr'. Reproduced: `brand=wallet walletMinor=0 remainderMinor=25900` and `balance after wallet-paid 259 kr ride from 50 kr: -209.0`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider has 50 kr in the wallet, picks a 259 kr ride, opens Pay with, taps the Movera Wallet row ('Balance: 50 kr'), books. Ride completes: wallet balance shows -209 kr, the wallet disappears from Pay with (balance not > 0), and the next 100 kr top-up shows -109 kr.
confirmed.evidence: ride_selection_controller.dart:265-268 `if (item.brand == 'wallet') { return _flags.enableWallet && walletBalance > 0 && walletMatchesTrip; }`; pay_with_page.dart:226-232 `_row(... title: context.l10n.walletBalance(...), onTap: () => Navigator.of(context).pop('wallet'),)`; wallet_controller.dart:282-283 `if (paidByWallet) { amount = snapshot.price;`; wallet_repository.dart:215-218 `final nextMinor = Money.fromLegacyMajor(current, currency).amountMinor + Money.fromLegacyMajor(deltaKr, currency).amountMinor; final next = Money(nextMinor, currency).major; await _source.saveBalance(next);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Offer the wallet as a full method only when `walletBalance >= fare` of the selected ride (or show it disabled with 'Balance too low'), and clamp `debitRide` to the available balance / refuse the charge with a logged error.

verdicts.reason: `payments()` lists the wallet whenever `walletBalance > 0` (ride_selection_controller.dart:265-268). PayWithPage pops 'wallet' on tap with no fare check (pay_with_page.dart:226-231). `walletSplitFor` returns `WalletSplit.none` for the wallet method (200-202), so the mock booking range check on `walletAmountMinor` (in_process_mock_client.dart:2247-2252) never sees it. verdicts.reason:
The steps chain with no guard:
- `RideSelectionController.payments()` lists the wallet whenever `walletBalance > 0` (ride_selection_controller.dart:265-268), with no comparison against the fare.

confirmed.title: Saved 'wallet' default payment is silently replaced by Cash on every Select Ride open (load-order race)
confirmed.description: `SelectRide.initState` starts `_loadSavedCards(paymentName)` (line 353) and `_loadWalletBalance()` (line 361) concurrently. `_loadSavedCards` → `restoreDefaultPayment()` reads the saved brand and, because `payments()` only lists the wallet when `walletBalance > 0` (ride_selection_controller.dart:267) and the balance has not loaded yet, hits `if (saved == null || !list.any((item) => item.brand == saved)) { _selectDefaultPayment(); }` and selects Cash. `_loadWalletBalance` resolves later (`loadUseWalletFirst` → `WalletStore.loadPayments` performs four `prefs.remove` platform calls plus possible writes before returning) and calls `setWalletBalance`, which only re-selects the *current* brand (`if (current != null) selectPaymentByBrand(current);`, 598-602), i.e. Cash. The remembered wallet default (persisted by `selectPayment` → `_persistSelectedBrand` and by WalletScreen `_selectMethod('wallet')`) is therefore never restored, contradicting the R10 note in default_payment_store.dart ('the choice survives relaunch'). A return ride whose origin was paid with 'Movera Wallet' loses it the same way (`selectPaymentNamed` runs before the balance is known). Reproduced with a throwaway test driving the same sequence on the controller: `afterRestore=cash walletOffered=true afterBalance=cash savedDefault=wallet`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider with 500 kr in the wallet chooses Movera Wallet in Pay with (persisted as default). Next time they open Select Ride the footer shows Cash; if they do not notice, the ride is booked as Cash and the driver asks for cash.
confirmed.evidence: ride_selection_controller.dart:572-582 `final saved = store == null ? null : await store.read(); final list = payments(); if (saved == null || !list.any((item) => item.brand == saved)) { _selectDefaultPayment(); }`; ride_selection_controller.dart:265-268 `if (item.brand == 'wallet') { return _flags.enableWallet && walletBalance > 0 && walletMatchesTrip; }`; ride_selection_controller.dart:598-602 `void setWalletBalance(double balance) { final current = selectedPaymentItem()?.brand; walletBalance = balance; if (current != null) selectPaymentByBrand(current); }`; select_ride.dart:353 `unawaited(_loadSavedCards(paymentName));` and :361 `unawaited(_loadWalletBalance());`. Throwaway test output: `afterRestore=cash walletOffered=true afterBalance=cash savedDefault=wallet`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Remember the saved brand in the controller (e.g. `_pendingDefaultBrand`) when it is not yet offered, and re-apply it in `setWalletBalance`/`setZonePaymentMethods` once it appears; or have SelectRide await the wallet balance before `restoreDefaultPayment`.

confirmed.title: After a confirmed pickup-pin move, other categories (and the selected one when its pin re-quote failed) are booked with quotes priced at the original pickup
confirmed.description: Set pickup only re-quotes the selected category, and only when the pin moves (set_pickup_page.dart:493-507 `if (_isAwayFrom(_center, _routeStart)) { ... unawaited(_requote()); }`). When the rider confirms a moved pin, `_bookNow` stores the new position (`_pickupAddress = spot.address; _pickupPosition = spot.position; _pickupConfirmed = true;`, 1487-1489) but never reloads the list quotes. If the rider then declines the 'Price updated' dialog (1515-1520 returns after `setState`), or returns from Finding Drivers, every other category still holds `authoritativeQuotes` priced from the old pickup, and the tiles show those prices. Tapping Book on such a category passes `_book`'s `quoteIsAvailable` check (the quote is fresh for up to 2 min), opens Set pickup at the NEW position showing `fare: SetPickupFare(totalKr: _priceFor(ride) ...)` (1307-1309, the old-pickup quote), and because the pin does not move nothing re-quotes; `_quoteAfterPickup` returns `_bookableQuote(ride.id)` as long as it is not expired (559-560), so `submitFinding` sends `pickupLat/Lng` of the new point with `quoteId`/`quoteSignedPayload` of the old point. The same happens for the selected category itself when its pin re-quote timed out: `_requoteNow` keeps the old fare (set_pickup_page.dart:534-541), `shown == quote.totalMinor` so no dialog, and the old-point quote is booked. The in-process mock's `_validateQuoteBinding` (in_process_mock_client.dart:2188-2230) checks id, signature, expiry, total and category but not the pickup, so the booking is accepted at the wrong price. `_bookScheduled` has the same shape: it never awaits `_pinQuote`, so a pin re-quote still in flight when Set pickup pops (it waits at most 3 s) leaves `ScheduledRideCheckout.draftFrom` → `quotedPrice` on the old-point quote.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider picks Economy, taps Book, drags the pin 1.5 km in Set pickup, confirms, gets 'Price updated 310 kr (was 259 kr)', taps Not now. List now shows Comfort at the price quoted for the original pickup. Rider taps Comfort → Book → Set pickup opens at the new pin showing the old-pickup price → Confirm and search → ride is created at the new coordinates with the old-pickup quote and price; Finding/Waiting then show that price.
confirmed.evidence: select_ride.dart:1487-1489 `_pickupAddress = spot.address; _pickupPosition = spot.position; _pickupConfirmed = true;` (no `_loadQuotes()`); select_ride.dart:1515-1520 `if (shown != null && _selection.moneyOf(shown).amountMinor != quote.totalMinor && !await _acceptNewPrice(shown, authoritativePrice)) { if (mounted) setState(() {}); return; }`; select_ride.dart:559-560 `final current = _bookableQuote(ride.id); if (current != null) return current;`; select_ride.dart:1307-1309 `fare: SetPickupFare( totalKr: _priceFor(ride),`; set_pickup_page.dart:493-507 requote only inside `if (_isAwayFrom(_center, _routeStart))`; in_process_mock_client.dart:2188-2230 `_validateQuoteBinding` has no pickup check.
confirmed.suggested_fix: After a confirmed pin move (and on 'Not now'), call `_loadQuotes()` so every category is re-priced from `_pickupPosition`; in `_quoteAfterPickup`, treat a quote whose pickup point differs from the confirmed one (or a failed pin re-quote) as unavailable and re-quote before booking; have `_bookScheduled` await `_pinQuote` the way `_bookNow` does.

confirmed.title: Trip-share contact checkbox (trip_share_page.dart:167-188): a failed save gets no rider feedback, editContact's error escapes unhandled, and a partial failure leaves the preference list and shareTrips inconsistent
confirmed.description: The checkbox value is `prefs.tripShareContactIds.contains(id) || contact.shareTrips` (581-585). Its `onChanged` first calls `_ctl.setTripShare(contactIds: selected)` (612-614) and then `_ctl.editContact(contact.copyWith(shareTrips: value == true))` (615-619). `setTripShare` swallows failures into `controller.error` (safety_controller.dart:277-295) and this page never shows `error`; `editContact` has no generic catch, so a transport failure in `SafetyStore._write` (safety_store.dart:92-101 rethrows after restoring the cache) escapes the async callback as an unhandled exception. Because the two writes are independent, one can succeed while the other fails: unchecking a contact may remove the id from `tripShareContactIds` while `shareTrips` stays true, and the `||` keeps the box checked with no message.

confirmed.title: A restored trip loses its pickup distance (and bags), so the waiting terms change after the app is killed and reopened: far-pickup free wait and no-show fee are replaced by the defaults
confirmed.description: _waitTerms is computed from widget.pickupKm (WaitingRules.termsFor applies the farPickup rule when pickupKm > 5: freeMinutes 1, noShowFee 85 kr). Home, Radar and Ride requests pass offer.pickupKm into AcceptRide. PersistedActiveRide has no pickupKm field, so _buildSnapshot cannot save it, and AcceptRide.fromPersisted does not pass it. After a crash, reload or PWA resume, the same trip gets base terms: 5 free minutes and a 65 kr no-show fee. The waiting clock, the paid seconds, the cash to collect, the driver's earnings and the no-show threshold all change in the middle of the trip. bags is also not saved or restored, so the island's bag notice disappears.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A driver accepts an offer 7 km away and waits at pickup for 4 minutes (3 paid minutes under the far-pickup rule). Safari kills the tab, and Home restores the trip. The island now shows those 4 minutes as included free wait, so the paid wait and the waiting fee drop to 0. The no-show fee the driver is promised falls from 85 kr to 65 kr.
confirmed.evidence:
accept_ride.dart:989-996 `late final WaitingTerms _waitTerms = WaitingRules.current.termsFor(category: widget.category, type: ..., pickupKm: widget.pickupKm);`
accept_ride.dart:253-291 fromPersisted passes no pickupKm and no bags.
waiting_rules.dart `if (pickupKm != null && pickupKm > farPickupKm) { ... terms = terms._with(farPickup, ...); }` with farPickup freeMinutes 1, noShowFee 8500 ore.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Save pickupKm (and bags) in PersistedActiveRide.toJson/fromJson/stamped, write them in _buildSnapshot, and pass them through AcceptRide.fromPersisted. Better still, save the resolved WaitingTerms so the trip keeps the terms it was accepted under.

verdicts.reason: PersistedActiveRide (lib/core/ride/active_ride_repository.dart:136-180) has no pickupKm field, and AcceptRide.fromPersisted (accept_ride.dart:240-291) passes no pickupKm. So after a restore, _waitTerms (accept_ride.dart:989-996) runs WaitingRules.termsFor with pickupKm == null and skips the farPickup rule (waiting_rules.dart:226-231: 1 free minute, 85 kr no-show fee). The trip falls back to base terms: 5 free minutes, 65 kr. On first accept the offer's pickupKm is passed in (home_offer_radar.dart:133/982/1064, ride_requests.dart:167). Nothing reachable sets pickupKm above 5 in demo mode, because every demo offer is under 5 km. But ApiDispatchRepository builds pickupKm from pickupMeters/1000 (api_dispatch_repository.dart:73), so live offers over 5 km reach this path. The no-show threshold, waiting fee and cash total then change mid-trip after a restore. Nothing in DECISIONS.md or LOCAL_DATA.md documents dropping these terms.

PersistedActiveRide has no pickupKm field (active_ride_repository.dart:138-188), _buildSnapshot does not save one (accept_ride_trip.dart:23-73), and AcceptRide.fromPersisted (accept_ride.dart:253-291) does not pass one. Cancelling a secured next trip archives it in history with that id (accept_ride_sheet.dart:270-286). Radar then returns to scanning and the next offer reuses the same id. If the driver secures it, finishes A and completes B, the journal's non-authoritative archive finds an existing row with that tripId and returns without writing (prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:201-202).

accept_ride.dart:963-964 `_NextTripRadarOffer get _uniqueDemoNext => _NextTripRadarOffer(

confirmed.title: On any cash trip with a Movera bonus, the app tells the driver to collect the full fare, bonus included, from the rider (API offers never carry cashToCollect)
confirmed.description: RideOffer.driverBonus is 'Movera-paid extra… [fare] already includes it', and WaybillPayment says of the bonus 'the rider never pays it'. On a cash trip whose offer has no explicit cashToCollect (null means 'the fare'), `_cashToCollect` falls back to `widget.fare`, which includes the bonus. That amount (plus the waiting fee) is what the Collect cash sheet shows in the big 'Collect … in cash' tray, and it is journaled as cashCollected. api_dispatch_repository parses driverBonus and paymentMethod independently, so a cash + bonus offer is a valid input.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An admin radar-group trip with fare 152,40 kr including a 40 kr Movera bonus, paid in cash, with no cashToCollect from the server. At drop-off the sheet says 'Collect 152,40 kr in cash', so the rider is charged Movera's 40 kr bonus. The cash balance then shows 'Settled' instead of Movera owing the driver the bonus.
confirmed.evidence:
accept_ride.dart:1007-1009 `String get _cashToCollect => WaitingTerms.addFee(widget.cashToCollect ?? widget.fare, _waitTerms.waitingFee(...));`
dispatch_repository.dart: `/// Movera-paid extra for this driver ... [fare] already includes it`
waybill.dart:288-290 `[bonus] ... is Movera's extra already in [fare]: the rider never pays it`
cash_collect_sheet.dart:75 `final amount = _short(cash);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: When cashToCollect is null, default the cash to fare − driverBonus (plus the rider's waiting fee), so the balance shows the bonus as owed by Movera.

verdicts.reason: The contract (contracts/contract.json:626) says driverBonus is included in Offer.fare and that the rider never pays it. WaybillPayment (waybill.dart, _riderOre = fare - bonus) does the same. The finding understates how wide this is. api_dispatch_repository.dart:59-95 never parses a cashToCollect field (the contract has none), so every live API offer has cashToCollect == null. _cashToCollect (accept_ride.dart:1007-1009) then falls back to widget.fare, which includes the bonus. That amount is shown on the Collect cash sheet (accept_ride_trip.dart:841) and journaled as cashCollected (accept_ride_trip.dart:335, 945). The parser reads paymentMethod (line 88) and driverBonus (line 65) independently, and nothing in the contract or docs forbids a bonus on a cash trip.
verdicts.repro: I traced the path statically: API offer JSON -> ApiDispatchRepository builds RideOffer with no cashToCollect -> home_offer_radar.dart:143/964 passes cashToCollect: null and driverBonus -> AcceptRide._cashToCollect = fare (bonus included) + waiting fee -> cash sheet and journal. I checked contract.json for cashToCollect and found nothing, and found no cash-specific bonus rule in docs/*.md.
verdicts.corrected_title: On any cash trip with a Movera bonus, the app tells the driver to collect the full fare, bonus included, from the rider (API offers never carry cashToCollect)

verdicts.reason: accept_ride.dart:1040-1042 `_cashToCollect => WaitingTerms.addFee(widget.cashToCollect ?? widget.fare, ...)` falls back to the full fare. The contract (contracts/openapi.yaml:5458 'fare ... driverBonus included', :5470 'already in fare and driverEarnings. The rider never pays it') and the app's own WaybillPayment (lib/core/waybill/waybill.dart:288-290, `_riderOre => _fareOre - _bonusOre`) both say the rider's share is fare minus bonus. The contract Offer has no cashToCollect field, so api_dispatch_repository.dart:64-88 parses fare, driverBonus and paymentMethod but never sets cashToCollect. On every API cash offer the fallback is therefore taken. home_offer_radar.dart:971-973 passes offer.fare and offer.driverBonus through to AcceptRide, and nothing subtracts the bonus. The result is used as both the Collect-cash amount (accept_ride_trip.dart:848) and the journaled cashCollected (accept_ride_trip.dart:337/952). CashBalance (lib/core/earnings/cash_balance.dart:32, fare - cashCollected) then shows 0 ('settled'), when Movera actually owes the driver the bonus.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand. An API offer with fare = 15240 öre (includes a 4000 öre bonus), paymentMethod = cash and no cashToCollect gives cashToCollect null, so _cashToCollect = '152,40 kr' plus any waiting fee. WaybillPayment.fromFare('152,40 kr', bonus: '40 kr').fare gives 112,40 kr as the rider's share, so the rider is overcharged by 40 kr. Nothing in the contract or the admin bonus endpoint (openapi.yaml:3601) excludes cash trips.

confirmed.title: On-trip next-trip offer card floats over the web map without PointerInterceptor or the map-gesture block that every other overlay uses
confirmed.description: When `_incomingOfferOpen` is true, the sliding panel collapses to 0 height (minHeight 0 / maxHeight 1), so the full-screen map (an HtmlElementView on web) lies under the card. Every other overlay on this screen goes through `_mapOverlay` (PointerInterceptor plus `_setMapGesturesBlocked`): the sheet, the island, the map controls and the Ride check layer. Home's equivalent offer sheet is also wrapped in PointerInterceptor, with the comment 'Opaque to touches: nothing under the sheet (dock, map) gets them'. The incoming ride card is added bare, so on web the map's DOM element receives pointer events in the card's area, and `_blockMapGestures` is never set while the driver touches it.
confirmed.failure_scenario: In the Safari/PWA build, during a trip an Exclusive next-trip offer appears in the bottom card. When the driver taps Accept or Decline, the touch reaches the Google map, which pans or ignores it, instead of the card button. The offer can run out unanswered.
confirmed.evidence:
accept_ride.dart:1347-1354
```
if (offerOpen)
  Positioned(
    key: const ValueKey<String>('on-trip-radar-layer'),
    ...
    child: _AcceptRidePanel(this)._buildIncomingRideCard(),
  ),
```
versus accept_ride.dart:1177/1279/1342/1359 `_AcceptRidePanel(this)._mapOverlay(...)`; accept_ride_panel.dart:13-22 `_mapOverlay` = `PointerInterceptor(child: Listener(onPointerDown: (_) => _setMapGesturesBlocked(true) ...))`; home_offer_sheet.dart:291-292 `// Opaque to touches: nothing under the sheet (dock, map) gets them. final sheet = PointerInterceptor(`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Wrap the card in `_AcceptRidePanel(this)._mapOverlay(child: ...)`, as the other overlays are.

verdicts.reason: The incoming next-trip card is placed directly in the outer Stack (accept_ride.dart:1347-1354), above the full-screen map. Unlike every other overlay on this screen (sheet 1177, map controls 1342, Ride check 1359), it is not wrapped in _mapOverlay, which is PointerInterceptor plus the map-gesture block (accept_ride_panel.dart:13-22). While offerOpen is true the panel is collapsed to height 0 (1148-1149), so the card sits only over the map. The map comes from google_maps_flutter (pubspec:50), which is an HtmlElementView on web. The pointer_interceptor README (0.10.1+2) documents this exact case: clicks over an HtmlElementView are taken by it and not relayed to Flutter, for example a FAB over a full-screen map. The app depends on that behaviour everywhere else, and home_offer_sheet.dart:291-292 wraps the equivalent Home offer sheet for that reason. The card's AbsorbPointer flag _blockMapGestures is also never set while it is touched.
verdicts.repro: I traced this statically: the Stack layout in accept_ride.dart:1144-1366, the _mapOverlay definition, the PointerInterceptor usages across lib/, and the pointer_interceptor README in the pub cache. Not reproduced in a browser: flutter test cannot exercise web platform-view hit-testing.

verdicts.reason: In accept_ride.dart:1380-1387 the on-trip offer card is placed as a bare `Positioned(... child: _AcceptRidePanel(this)._buildIncomingRideCard())`. _buildIncomingRideCard (accept_ride_panel.dart:192-200) returns a plain Material/Container with no PointerInterceptor. Every other overlay on this map goes through `_mapOverlay` (accept_ride_panel.dart:13-22: PointerInterceptor plus Listener for _setMapGesturesBlocked): the panel at 1210, the island at 1312, the controls at 1375 and Ride check at 1392. While the offer is open, the sliding panel collapses to 0/1 height (1181-1182), so only the full-screen map lies under the card. On web the map is google_maps_flutter's HtmlElementView (DECISIONS.md:79-81 names Safari/PWA as a supported target). Without PointerInterceptor, DOM pointer events over a platform view go to the map element, not to Flutter widgets drawn above it. AbsorbPointer(_blockMapGestures) at 1226 cannot help: it only blocks Flutter-side events, and the flag is never set by this card.
verdicts.repro: Static trace, since flutter test cannot run the web platform-view DOM. Compared the card against the four `_mapOverlay` call sites and the PointerInterceptor in home_offer_sheet.dart. Confirmed pointer_interceptor ^0.10.1+2 and google_maps_flutter are in pubspec.yaml, and that test/widget_test.dart:1076/2346 assert PointerInterceptor around map overlays as the house convention.

confirmed.title: System Back on the 'Unresolved trip' dialog closes the saved trip and marks it terminal
confirmed.description: For a stale snapshot (older than 6 h) or one without verified endpoints, Home shows an AlertDialog with 'Close trip' and 'Resume trip'. barrierDismissible: false only blocks taps outside the dialog. The Android or browser Back button still pops the DialogRoute with a null result, because there is no PopScope in the builder. The code treats any result other than true as 'Close trip' (`if (resume != true)`). It then writes a terminal marker (driver cancel, or released to dispatch) and clears the saved ride. So Back, which the driver expects to dismiss the dialog, silently cancels a trip that could have been resumed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver's phone restarts during a long trip, and the saved ride is more than 6 h old or the app is reopened late. Home shows 'Unresolved trip' with Resume enabled. The driver presses Android Back (or browser Back on the PWA) to get rid of the dialog. The trip is marked cancelled by the driver or released to dispatch, and its recovery record is deleted, with no confirmation.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Wrap the AlertDialog in PopScope(canPop: false), or treat a null result as 'ask again' rather than 'close'.

verdicts.reason: home.dart:530-537 (now ~535-541 in the working tree) shows the 'Unresolved trip' AlertDialog with only barrierDismissible:false. No PopScope wraps the dialog builder. Home's own PopScope (home_back.dart:39-44) sits on Home's route, not on the DialogRoute, so system Back pops the dialog with a null result. The next line, `if (resume != true)`, treats null the same as 'Close trip'. It calls markTerminal(... cancelledByDriver / released) and then clearForTrip, so a trip the driver could have resumed (Resume is enabled when hasVerifiedEndpoints) is ended with no confirmation. The reachable case is a stale snapshot (isFresh false, older than 6 h) with verified endpoints, so this is an edge path. Nothing in DECISIONS.md makes Back mean 'close'.
verdicts.repro: I wrote a throwaway widget test (test/_audit_u113_test.dart, since deleted) that copies the exact pattern: showDialog<bool>(barrierDismissible:false, AlertDialog) and then binding.handlePopRoute(). Output: 'DIALOG POPPED BY BACK, result=null' and '+1: All tests passed!'. In home.dart I traced that a null result goes into the `resume != true` branch, which calls markTerminal and clearForTrip.

verdicts.reason: home.dart:535-539 calls showDialog with barrierDismissible: false. That flag only stops taps on the barrier. The AlertDialog builder has no PopScope, so system Back pops the DialogRoute with a null result. The Home PopScope in home_back.dart:39 sits on the Home route below the dialog and does not apply to it. home.dart:541 then runs `if (resume != true)`, which calls markTerminal (driver cancel, or release to dispatch) and clearForTrip/clear. Nothing in DECISIONS.md or LOCAL_DATA.md says Back should close the trip.
verdicts.repro: Wrote throwaway test/_audit_u113_test.dart: showDialog<bool>(barrierDismissible:false) with Close/Resume actions, then tester.binding.handlePopRoute() to simulate Android Back. Output: `done=true result=null resume!=true -> true`, `+1: All tests passed!`. The file was deleted afterwards.

confirmed.title: _hasRideOffers set from the Radar list on close is never cleared when those offers leave dispatch: the orb says 'Trip found', 'Finding trips' never shows and Exclusive offers are held back
confirmed.description: Closing the full Radar list sets `_hasRideOffers = hasOffers || _radarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty`, where hasOffers comes from the list's own dispatch offers. _hasRideOffers is reset only by _dismissRadarHomeOffer, _refreshRadarHomeOffers (which needs pending Home offers), _openOfferTrip, go online and go offline. The dispatch watcher (_watchDispatchRadar) updates _latestDispatchOffers but never recomputes _hasRideOffers. Suppose the Home deck was emptied while the list was open, for example when a card was withdrawn or taken and removed after 2.8 s, and the list still had other trips. The flag then stays true after those trips expire. While it is true: _buildTripRadarButton shows 'Trip found / NEW / Tap for all' with zero trips (totalTrips = max(0, 0)); _waitingForTrips is false, so the island never says 'Finding trips'; and _showOutsideRadarOffer returns early for every non-reservation Exclusive offer (`!offer.reservation && (_pendingRadarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty || _hasRideOffers)`).
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver opens the Radar list. Meanwhile the only Home card is taken by another driver and removed, and the list still shows two other trips. The driver closes the list, and those two trips then expire in dispatch. Home keeps showing 'Trip found · NEW · Tap for all' with nothing to take, never shows 'Finding trips', and no Exclusive offer can rise until the driver taps the orb again.

confirmed.title: 'Open settings' in the push primer calls Geolocator.openAppSettings, which throws UnsupportedError on web
confirmed.description: `_openSettings` defaults to `Geolocator.openAppSettings`. geolocator_web implements it as `throw _unsupported('openAppSettings')`. The primer is reachable on web in release-like builds (gate `enabled = !allowsMockTransport`): when the browser's `Notification.requestPermission()` answers 'denied' (or 'default'), `FlutterFirebasePushGateway.requestPermission` maps it to `PushAuthorizationStatus.denied`, `PushPermissionGate._register` stores `blockedBySystem`, and both the sheet (`_blocked`) and the Notifications screen banner then offer 'Open settings'. Tapping it throws inside the button callback; nothing opens, the rider gets no feedback, and the error is recorded as a crash by the zone handler. The location notice already handles this case correctly via `locationSettingsOpenerFor(isWeb: ...)` returning null, so the web branch was simply missed here.

confirmed.title: Backup and device-transfer rules leave out the root domain, so ride-check audio under app_flutter is not excluded, and the test only checks that the tags exist
confirmed.description: The test 'Android excludes app data from backup and device transfer' only asserts that `<cloud-backup>` and `<device-transfer>` are present. It never checks what they exclude. The rules exclude the `sharedpref`, `database` and `file` domains only. Ride-check audio is written under `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()`, which on Android is `context.getDir("flutter")`, i.e. `<dataDir>/app_flutter`. That is in the `root` domain, not `file`. For apps targeting Android 12+, `allowBackup="false"` does not stop device-to-device migration, so the recordings leave the phone when the driver moves to a new device. The rules file's own comment says driver data stays on this device, and the ride-check UI says the recording is saved only on this phone. The test cannot catch this, or any rule that includes data.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A driver records audio in a Ride check, then sets up a new Android phone with device transfer. The .m4a files under app_flutter/ride_check_audio are copied to the new device. A rules file containing `<include domain="root" path="."/>` would also pass this test. Worked from the Android backup-domain rules and path_provider_android behaviour; nothing was run.
confirmed.evidence:
test/audit/privacy_storage_test.dart:61-63 `final rules = File('android/app/src/main/res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml').readAsStringSync(); expect(rules, contains('<cloud-backup>')); expect(rules, contains('<device-transfer>'));`
android/app/src/main/res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml: `<device-transfer> <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="." /> <exclude domain="database" path="." /> <exclude domain="file" path="." /> </device-transfer>` (no `root`)
lib/core/safety/ride_check_recorder_native.dart:31-32 `final directory = Directory('${(await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()).path}/ride_check_audio');`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add `<exclude domain="root" path="."/>` to cloud-backup, device-transfer and full-backup-content (or store recordings under getFilesDir). Make the test parse the XML and assert every domain the app writes to is excluded in both sections.

On Android, path_provider puts that directory at context.getDir('flutter'), i.e. <dataDir>/app_flutter, which belongs to the 'root' backup domain. The 'file' domain covers only getFilesDir(). data_extraction_rules.xml excludes only sharedpref, database and file in both <cloud-backup> and <device-transfer>, and backup_rules.xml has the same gap. For apps targeting Android 12+ (targetSdk = flutter.targetSdkVersion), allowBackup="false" (AndroidManifest.xml:13) does not stop device-to-device transfer, so files outside the excluded domains can be copied to a new phone. On Android, path_provider_android 2.3.1 implements that directory as `context.getDir('flutter', MODE_PRIVATE)` (path_provider_android_real.dart:36-45), which is <dataDir>/app_flutter. That folder is in Android's `root` backup domain, not `file` (getFilesDir). android/app/src/main/res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml and backup_rules.xml exclude only sharedpref, database and file, so the folder is not excluded. targetSdk is flutter.targetSdkVersion (31 or higher), and for those apps allowBackup="false" (AndroidManifest.xml:13) does not stop device-to-device transfer. The app tells the driver the audio is 'saved only on this phone' (app_localizations_en.dart:1342), so the recordings can be copied to a new phone despite that promise. Grep found no other lib/ code using that directory. The cloud-backup/device-transfer behaviour of the Android domains was worked by hand from the platform rules, not run on a device.
