confirmed.title: Web auth-preview: a wrong OTP while an earlier session's tokens are still in sessionStorage expires the session and re-roots Sign in instead of showing 'wrong code'
confirmed.description: `_send` enters the refresh/retry/expire path for any 401 whose request carried an access token (line 89); the comment relies on OTP verify never carrying one. `RideRestoreCoordinator` returns `SignIn()` when `AppEnv.current.authPreview && snapshot == null` (ride_restore_coordinator.dart lines 432-434, 449-452) without clearing tokens, and on web the tokens live in this tab's sessionStorage, so a reload with `?auth_preview=1` after an earlier sign-in reaches `PhoneVerify` with tokens present. A wrong code -> mock `401 invalid_otp` -> `_refreshAccess` (mock accepts any `mock-refresh-*`) -> retry -> 401 again -> `_expireSession` clears tokens, calls `onSessionExpired` (`LocationRepository.clearLastGoodFix()` + `showMoveraRoot(SignIn())`), then throws; `PhoneVerify` is unmounted so its `_error` is never shown.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Web demo with `?auth_preview=1`: rider who signed in earlier in the tab types one wrong OTP digit; instead of 'wrong code' the screen jumps back to the first Sign in step, the stored session is gone and the last good location fix is wiped.
confirmed.evidence:
api_client.dart:89-113 `if (response.statusCode == 401 && access?.isNotEmpty == true) { // An OTP rejection is not an expired session. Only requests that carried an access token enter the refresh/retry path. final refresh = await _refreshAccess(access!); ... if (replacement == null || response.statusCode == 401) { await _expireSession(replacement ?? access); } }`
ride_restore_coordinator.dart:449-452 `if (snapshot == null && AppEnv.current.authPreview) { reportRestoreSurface('signInPreview'); return const SignIn(); }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Exclude `/api/v1/auth/*` paths from the refresh/expire path (or let callers opt out), or clear tokens before showing the preview Sign in.

verdicts.reason: api_client.dart:89 enters the refresh, retry and expire path for any 401 on a request that carried an access token, and that includes /api/v1/auth/otp/verify. The case is reachable on the web demo with ?auth_preview=1. env.dart:67-69 enables the preview, ride_restore_coordinator.dart:449-452 roots SignIn without checking or clearing tokens, the tokens persist in this tab's sessionStorage (secure_token_store.dart:9-17), and AuthRepository and PhoneVerify never clear them before verifying. A wrong code gets a mock 401 invalid_otp (in_process_mock_client.dart:433-435). The refresh succeeds because the mock accepts mock-refresh-*, the retry gets 401 again, and _expireSession (api_client.dart:220-226) clears the tokens and runs onSessionExpired, which calls clearLastGoodFix and showMoveraRoot(SignIn()) (di.dart:104-116, app.dart:15-17). PhoneVerify is replaced, so its 'wrong code' error is never shown. Production and staging are not affected, because SignIn shows there only when hasSession() is false.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_r6_otp_test.dart (deleted afterwards): MemoryTokenStore pre-seeded with mock-access/mock-refresh, ApiClient(client: InProcessMockClient()), OTP request, then verify with code 9999. Output: `AUDIT R6: err=ApiError(unauthenticated, invalid_otp, ...) expired=1 access=null` -- onSessionExpired fired once and the tokens were cleared.
verdicts.corrected_title: Web auth-preview: a wrong OTP while an earlier session's tokens are still in sessionStorage expires the session and re-roots Sign in instead of showing 'wrong code'
In the web demo with ?auth_preview=1 after an earlier sign-in in the tab, one wrong OTP is treated as session expiry: tokens are cleared and Sign in is re-rooted instead of showing 'wrong code'
verdicts.reason: api_client.dart:89 decides whether to refresh only by whether a stored access token exists, not by path. ride_restore_coordinator.dart:449-452 (and :433) returns SignIn whenever `authPreview && snapshot == null` and does not clear tokens. No code in the sign-in flow clears them either (the only callers of `_tokens.clear` are signOut and clearLocalSession, auth_repository.dart:135-141). On web, tokens live in tab sessionStorage (secure_token_store.dart:17), so they survive the reload. A wrong code gives mock 401 invalid_otp (in_process_mock_client.dart:433-435). The mock refresh accepts any `mock-refresh-*` token (:479-491), the retry gets 401 again, and `_expireSession` clears the tokens and calls onSessionExpired (di.dart:104-116: clearLastGoodFix plus showSignInOnSessionExpired). That unmounts PhoneVerify, so its 'wrong code' error is never shown. This path exists only in the web demo flavor's auth-preview mode (env.dart:67-69), so severity is low.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_vq7c1b3_test.dart: ApiClient(InProcessMockClient, MemoryTokenStore pre-filled with mock-access/mock-refresh tokens, onSessionExpired counter), then AuthRepository.requestOtp, then verifyOtp(code '9999'). Output: `AUDIT6 error=ApiError(unauthenticated, invalid_otp, ...) expired=1 access=null refresh=null`. The session was expired and both tokens were wiped by one wrong code. Test file deleted.

confirmed.title: `PATCH /rides/{id}` offer raise / searching edit changes the fare, pickup and destination without `_touch`, so version, updatedAt, sequence and eventId stay unchanged
confirmed.description: The non-routeChange PATCH branch (lines 947-1011) calls `_setFare(ride, fare + increase)` and rewrites `pickupAddress/pickupLat/pickupLng/destination*` but never calls `_touch(ride)`, unlike every other mutation (route change line 895, cancel via `_apply`, feedback line 646). The mock's own rule (lines 1351-1361) is 'one committed change: version + 1, new updatedAt, next sequence/eventId' and CONTRACT.md §1 requires a stale `expectedVersion` to be refused. After a raise the trip still reports the old `version`/`updatedAt`/`eventId`, so a second screen's `expectedVersion` from before the raise is accepted, `ApiRideRealtime` dedupes the projection by the unchanged eventId, and `updatedAt` misreports when the trip last changed. Reproduced: `AUDIT B2: fare 29100 -> 34100; version 1 -> 1; eventId ev_..._1 -> ev_..._1; updatedAt unchanged`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Demo flavor: rider raises the offer by 50 kr while searching; the projection's `version`, `updatedAt` and `eventId` do not move. A command sent from another tab/screen with the pre-raise `expectedVersion` is not refused as stale, and a polling consumer never sees a new event for the change.
confirmed.evidence:
in_process_mock_client.dart:989-1010 `final increase = _offerIncreaseMinor(body, rideCurrency); final fare = _fareMinor(ride); if (increase != null && fare != null) { _setFare(ride, fare + increase); ride['offerIncrease'] = _money(increase, rideCurrency); } if (body['pickupAddress'] != null) { ride['pickupAddress'] = body['pickupAddress']; } ... payload = {'code': 'OK', 'ride': ride, 'requestId': requestId};` (no `_touch`)
in_process_mock_client.dart:1351-1361 `/// One committed change: version + 1, new updatedAt, and the next server-assigned realtime sequence ... static void _touch(`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Call `_touch(ride)` after applying the offer raise / pickup / destination edit in that branch.

verdicts.reason: In the searching-edit branch of PATCH /rides/{id} (lib/core/api/in_process_mock_client.dart:986-1010), _setFare and the pickup/destination rewrites are never followed by _touch(ride). _setFare (:1942-1945) changes only the fare. Every other committed change goes through _touch (:1354-1362), which bumps version, updatedAt and sequence/eventId. As a result, a later command carrying the pre-raise expectedVersion passes _versionMismatch (:1448-1456), against R-O2 and CONTRACT.md §1. Realtime events with the unchanged sequence/eventId are dropped by RealtimeGate as duplicates (finding_driver_controller.dart:359-367). Impact is limited: the rider who raised the offer updates its own snapshot from the PATCH response (finding_driver_controller.dart:828-860), so the fare it shows is right. Raises are also additive and keyed, so there is no money harm, only broken stale-write protection and an unchanged change marker in the demo backend.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_r89_test.dart (since deleted) against InProcessMockClient: booked a ride, then PATCHed offerIncrease 10 kr with expectedVersion 1. Output: `R8 fare {amountMinor: 30100, currency: SEK} version 1 -> 1 eventId ev_ride_..._1 -> ev_ride_..._1 updatedAt same=true`. A second PATCH (pickupAddress) with the pre-raise expectedVersion 1 was accepted: `R8 stale-version edit accepted: OK`. Test passed: `+1: All tests passed!`.

verdicts.reason: The non-routeChange PATCH branch in lib/core/api/in_process_mock_client.dart:989-1010 calls _setFare and rewrites pickup/destination but never calls _touch (defined at :1351-1361 as 'one committed change: version + 1, new updatedAt, next sequence/eventId'). The route-change branch does call it at :895. The real caller is FindingDriverController's offer raise (lib/features/finding_driver/application/finding_driver_controller.dart:820-829), which PATCHes {offerIncrease, expectedVersion}. After the raise the version does not move, so _versionMismatch (:1448-1465) still accepts the pre-raise expectedVersion. The rider's own screen takes the fare from the response, so the visible effect is limited to stale-version protection and realtime dedupe by eventId. That is a contract deviation, not a main-path failure.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_c3b1_rider_test.dart (since deleted) quoted and booked through the mock, then sent PATCH /api/v1/rides/{id} with offerIncrease 1000 öre and expectedVersion=1. Output: 'AUDIT r8 status=200 fare {amountMinor: 22800} -> {amountMinor: 23800}; version 1 -> 1; eventId ev_ride_..._1 -> ev_ride_..._1; updatedAt same=true'. A second raise sent with the pre-raise version was accepted: 'status=200 code=OK', not 409.

confirmed.title: PickupSchedule.zoneNow builds the zone wall-clock as a device-local DateTime: for a Tunis pickup on an EU-DST phone, during 02:00-02:59 Tunis on the EU spring-forward day, the earliest legal pickup is pushed an hour late
confirmed.description: `wallTime` computes the correct zone wall-clock components and then constructs `DateTime(year, month, day, hour, ...)` with the local-time constructor. Dart resolves a non-existent local time (the device's spring-forward gap) by shifting it, so when the device time zone differs from the zone's (RiderZones has Europe/Stockholm, Europe/Paris, Africa/Tunis; Tunis has no DST) the picker shows the wrong hour. `toUtc` (lines 74-86) uses `DateTime.utc`, so the round trip is asymmetric. Also the doc comment on `toUtc` says the summer offset is used in the non-existent hour, but the two-step guess yields the winter offset: wall 02:30 Stockholm on 2026-03-29 -> asUtc 02:30Z -> offsetAt = +2 -> guess 00:30Z -> offsetAt(00:30Z) = +1 -> 01:30Z (= 03:30 wall), not 00:30Z.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider with a Swedish phone books a reservation in the Tunis zone for 2026-03-29 02:30 Tunis time (instant 01:30Z): `wallTime('Africa/Tunis', instant)` -> `DateTime(2026,3,29,2,30)` in Europe/Stockholm does not exist -> shows 03:30. The reverse mapping of the shown value then lands on a different instant than the one stored.
confirmed.evidence: lib/core/config/zone_clock.dart:57-69 `static DateTime wallTime(String timeZone, DateTime instant) { ... return DateTime(local.year, local.month, local.day, local.hour, local.minute, local.second, local.millisecond); }` ; :71-73 doc `In the hour that does not exist (spring forward) the summer offset is used` vs :84-85 `final guess = asUtc.subtract(offsetAt(timeZone, asUtc)); return asUtc.subtract(offsetAt(timeZone, guess));`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Return `DateTime.utc(local.year, ..., local.millisecond)` (a UTC-flagged carrier of wall components, which never shifts) and have the pickers treat it as offset-free; fix the toUtc doc comment or the algorithm to match.

verdicts.reason: zone_clock.dart:60-68 rebuilds the zone's wall-clock time with the local DateTime constructor, so the device's DST rules apply to it. PickupSchedule.zoneNow (stockholm_schedule.dart:29-30) feeds this value to minimumPickup and the pickers, and scheduled_rides_controller.dart:64 maps the chosen value back with toUtc. With the device in Europe/Stockholm, 01:30Z on 2026-03-29 in the Tunis zone gives 03:30 instead of 02:30. The round trip then lands on 02:30Z, not 01:30Z. This is real but very narrow: once a year, a one-hour night window, and only when the device time zone differs from the pickup zone's and has DST.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_rc2b2_tz_test.dart, run with TZ=Europe/Stockholm (deleted afterwards). Output: 'wallTime tunis @01:30Z => 2026-03-29 03:30:00.000 hour=3', 'toUtc of that => 2026-03-29 02:30:00.000Z', 'zoneNow tunis => 2026-03-29 03:30:00.000', 'All tests passed!'.

verdicts.corrected_title: PickupSchedule.zoneNow builds the zone wall-clock as a device-local DateTime: for a Tunis pickup on an EU-DST phone, during 02:00-02:59 Tunis on the EU spring-forward day, the earliest legal pickup is pushed an hour late
verdicts.reason: zone_clock.dart:57-69 rebuilds the zone wall-clock with the local DateTime constructor, so a wall time inside the device zone's spring-forward gap is moved forward an hour. The only caller is PickupSchedule.zoneNow (stockholm_schedule.dart:29-30), which feeds minimumPickup, isLegalPickup and timePickerMinFor. The finding's own scenario (wallTime applied to a chosen reservation instant) does not occur, because wallTime is only ever applied to 'now'. The real effect is limited to a mismatched device and pickup zone (Stockholm/Paris phone, Tunis pickup, since Tunis has no DST) during one hour a year. The toUtc doc comment at 71-73 is also wrong: Stockholm 02:30 on 2026-03-29 resolves to 01:30Z, which uses the winter offset, not the summer one it claims.
verdicts.repro: I ran a throwaway test under TZ=Europe/Stockholm. ZoneClock.wallTime('Africa/Tunis', 2026-03-29 01:30Z) returned 03:30 (correct is 02:30). toUtc of that value returned 02:30Z, not the original 01:30Z. ZoneClock.toUtc(DateTime(2026,3,29,2,30), 'Europe/Stockholm') returned 01:30Z. PickupSchedule('Africa/Tunis') at now=01:15Z (02:15 Tunis): 'zoneNow=03:15 min=03:45'. A 03:15 Tunis pickup is reported not legal, although the correct minimum is 02:45.

confirmed.title: docs/QA_HOOKS.md still lists moveraOpenSafety as absent from release builds, but code and CI intentionally expose a navigation-only bridge
confirmed.description: docs/QA_HOOKS.md:3-11 states public release builds do not expose `moveraOpenSafety` and that hooks install only under kDebugMode or MOVERA_QA. `installSafetyNavigationBridge` sets exactly that global without any gate, and bootstrap calls it unconditionally (lib/app/bootstrap.dart:76-78) outside the `if (moveraQaHooksEnabled)` block (lines 82-85). The gated `installSafetyQaOpener` (line 52) writes the same property name, so in QA builds whichever runs last wins. The code comment says this is intentional, so either the record or the code is wrong; per the audit rules a place where code does not do what the decision document says is reportable.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On the public GitHub Pages build any page script (or the Maps JS SDK) can call `window.moveraOpenSafety()` and navigate the rider to the Safety hub; QA_HOOKS.md promises this surface is absent.
confirmed.evidence: lib/core/debug/web_qa_hooks_web.dart:67-81 `void installSafetyNavigationBridge(bool Function() open) { // This bridge is intentionally available in public web builds. ... globalContext.setProperty('moveraOpenSafety'.toJS, ...` ; lib/app/bootstrap.dart:76-78 `installSafetyNavigationBridge(() => pushPageOnce(() => const SafetyHub(), AppRoutes.safety));` (before the `if (moveraQaHooksEnabled)` at :82); docs/QA_HOOKS.md:3-9 `Public GitHub Pages **release** builds do **not** expose: ... - moveraOpenSafety`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Either gate the bridge with moveraQaHooksEnabled (and use the gated installSafetyQaOpener only), or correct docs/QA_HOOKS.md / ARCHITECTURE.md to state that moveraOpenSafety is a public navigation-only hook.

verdicts.corrected_title: docs/QA_HOOKS.md still lists moveraOpenSafety as absent from release builds, but code and CI intentionally expose a navigation-only bridge
verdicts.reason: The mismatch with the document is real. docs/QA_HOOKS.md:3-11 says release builds do not expose moveraOpenSafety. But bootstrap.dart:74-78 calls installSafetyNavigationBridge without a gate, and web_qa_hooks_web.dart:67-81 sets window.moveraOpenSafety unconditionally. This is clearly intentional: the code comments at web_qa_hooks_web.dart:68-70 and bootstrap.dart:74-75 say so, and qa-live-rider-flow.yml:115-141 asserts the bridge exists on public release. So the document is stale, not the code. The security effect is nil: the bridge only pushes the SafetyHub, which the rider can already open from the drawer, via pushPageOnce. It does not mutate state. The claim that whichever install runs last wins is moot, because registerWebQaHooks runs after the bridge only in QA builds, and both open the same screen.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: bootstrap.dart:73-85 runs the bridge before the `if (moveraQaHooksEnabled)` block. Grep for moveraOpenSafety across docs, lib and .github: the docs say absent, while the CI workflow requires it to be present.

verdicts.corrected_title: docs/QA_HOOKS.md:9 still lists moveraOpenSafety as absent from public release builds, but the code (on purpose) exposes it as a public navigation-only bridge
verdicts.reason: The finding is accurate. bootstrap.dart:76-78 calls installSafetyNavigationBridge with no gate, before the `if (moveraQaHooksEnabled)` block, and web_qa_hooks_web.dart:67-81 sets window.moveraOpenSafety unconditionally. The gated installSafetyQaOpener (:52) has no callers, so the overwrite race the finding describes cannot happen. The exposure is deliberate. The code comment (:68-70), the bootstrap comment (:74-75) and the CI workflow qa-live-rider-flow.yml:114-120 all say so, and the workflow even fails if the bridge is missing on public Pages. The behaviour is harmless: it only pushes the same SafetyHub the drawer already opens, via pushPageOnce. QA_HOOKS.md was edited later (ee9f4c1, 2026-10-17) than the bridge was added (2026-10-14) and still says it is not exposed, and ARCHITECTURE.md says window.movera* hooks are gated. So this is a real documentation contract mismatch, but the impact is a stale doc, not a security hole.
verdicts.repro: Traced callers: grep shows the only caller of installSafetyNavigationBridge is bootstrap.dart:76, which runs unconditionally, and installSafetyQaOpener has no callers. qa-live-rider-flow.yml:118-120 expects `window.moveraOpenSafety()` to return 'ok' on the public release Pages build. Checked docs/QA_HOOKS.md:3-11 and the dates in git log (read-only). No runtime test was needed.

confirmed.title: A web JS flight stopped by a tap leaves MapView.pose at the flight's starting pose, so the next stepped glide starts from the wrong place
confirmed.original_title: A web JS flight stopped by a tap leaves MapView.pose at the flight's starting pose, so the next stepped glide starts from the wrong place
confirmed.description: While a JS flight runs, view.easing is true, so CustomGoogleMap._onMove ignores every camera report and view.pose stays at the pose from before the flight. On the web, Dart only learns where the camera is when the flight lands (_jsGlide sets pose = goal). If the flight is cancelled, interrupt() calls RiderMapBridge.cancelFlight and clears easing. _jsGlide's finally block skips its work because the generation changed. view.pose is never refreshed. A tap without a drag (pointerdown on .gm-style sets touching=true and interrupts) produces no further camera report. It also does not set movedByHandAt, so follow updates are not held. The next follow glide or 450 ms fitBounds ease runs on the Dart loop from view.pose, which is the pre-flight origin.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On the web Home map, the rider taps recenter and taps the map (for example a marker) halfway through the 1 s flight. The camera stops mid-way, but pose still holds the pre-recenter view. The next follow update (a GPS fix) starts a Dart glide whose first frame jumps the camera back toward the old view before gliding to the target.
confirmed.evidence: map_camera_motion.dart:86-89 `if (_jsFlight) { _jsFlight = false; final id = mapId; if (id != null) RiderMapBridge.cancelFlight(id); }` with no pose refresh; :364-375 `if (view.generation == generation) { if (arrived && view._goal != null) { view.pose = view._goal; ...` (skipped after interrupt). custom_google_map.dart:202 ignores reports while `view.easing`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: When a JS flight is cancelled, read the live camera into view.pose, for example by having cancelFlight return the current pose or by calling controller.getVisibleRegion/zoom, or mark pose unknown so the next report is accepted.

verdicts.reason: interrupt() (map_camera_motion.dart:80-94) cancels the JS flight and clears easing, but it does not touch pose. _jsGlide's finally (:364-375) is skipped because the generation changed, and arrived is false anyway, since JS endFlight(false) runs on cancel (web/rider_map_camera.js:137-145). During the flight, CustomGoogleMap._onMove dropped every echo because easing was true (lib/shared/widgets/custom_google_map.dart:202). The only things that write pose are _onMove, _send and _jsGlide (grep). A tap without a drag sets touching through the map_touch_web pointerdown (lib/core/web/map_touch_web.dart:40). It does not call release(): the gesture layer only releases on a move of 6 px or more, a dblclick or a native zoom control (rider_map_camera.js:218-235). So movedByHandAt stays null. The next follow update through animateCamera(follow:true) passes _mayMove, and easeCameraTo steps _glide from view.pose, which is the pre-flight origin. Its first _approach frame (about a 5% share) lands next to the old view. One thing could save it: a trailing bounds_changed from the flight's last rAF frame arriving after pointerdown. That frame normally renders and dispatches within its own frame, before the input event, so nothing reliably refreshes pose.
verdicts.repro: Static trace only (read-only run, no flutter/dart executed). Traced easeCameraTo -> RiderMapBridge.flight -> _jsGlide, interrupt -> cancelFlight -> JS endFlight(false), all pose writers (grep '\.pose = '), the touch watcher in map_touch_web.dart and the release() conditions in rider_map_camera.js. No document records this as intentional.

verdicts.reason: On the web, a pointerdown on .gm-style goes through map_touch_web.dart to _fingerDown, which sets touching=true (custom_google_map.dart:173). That calls interrupt() (map_camera_motion.dart:80-90): generation goes up, easing becomes false and the JS flight is cancelled (rider_map_camera.js:145, endFlight(false)). The pose is not refreshed. After that, _jsGlide's finally block is skipped because the generation no longer matches (:364), so view.pose is not set to the goal. While the flight ran, every report was dropped because easing was true (custom_google_map.dart:202). So view.pose still holds the pose from before the flight. A tap without a drag never calls release() in the JS layer: pointerdown only stores pointerOrigin (rider_map_camera.js:222), and single-finger touchstart does not call releaseTouch. So movedByHandAt stays null and heldByRider is false once the finger lifts. onCameraIdle carries no pose. The next follow easeCameraTo calls interrupt() and then starts from view.pose (map_camera_motion.dart:324-325). Its first _approach frame is computed from the stale origin and sent with moveCamera, so the camera jumps back toward the old view. The only thing that could rescue it is timing: a trailing bounds_changed after the cancel. The web plugin reads the live map pose for each CameraMoveEvent (google_maps_controller.dart:279-288), so such an event would fix pose. But nothing guarantees one arrives.
verdicts.repro: Read-only, no run. Traced pointerdown, then map_touch_web onDown, _fingerDown, the touching setter, interrupt() and cancelFlight. Then traced _jsGlide's finally block (generation mismatch, so it is skipped) and _onMove's easing filter. Checked google_maps_flutter_web 0.5.14+2: onBoundsChanged gives CameraMoveEvent(_gmViewportToCameraPosition(map)) and onIdle gives no pose. Then followed the next animateCamera(follow:true) path: _mayMove, easeCameraTo, interrupt, from = view.pose, _glide frame 0 and _send.

confirmed.title: A recenter that joins a running follow glide is stepped on the Dart timer on the web and keeps the old glide's 240-frame cap, which can cut the flight short
confirmed.original_title: A recenter that joins a running follow glide is stepped on the Dart timer on the web and keeps the old glide's 240-frame cap, which can cut the flight short
confirmed.description: When easeCameraTo gets a flight-length goal (>= 600 ms, for example animateCamera(follow:false) from a recenter) while a damped follow glide is running, it converts that glide in place: it sets _flight and resets _flownMicros to 0. It never hands the flight to RiderMapBridge.flight, although the comment at lines 336-338 says web flights run on the browser frame clock so they do not stutter on a Dart timer in Safari. The loop variable `frame` in _glide also keeps counting from the start of the old glide, and the flight branch ends with `last = after >= 1 || frame >= _maxEaseFrames`. If the follow glide had already run about 180 frames (it was retargeted repeatedly without settling), the new 1 s flight is cut off after the remaining frames and snaps to its goal.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On web Safari, the Home map is gliding after a stream of GPS follow fixes when the rider taps recenter. The 1 s locate flight runs on the Dart 16 ms timer (the stutter the JS path exists to avoid). If the follow glide was already near frame 240, the flight lands with a jump after a fraction of a second.
confirmed.evidence: map_camera_motion.dart:318-321 `if (view._flight == null && duration >= _flightThreshold) { view._flight = duration; view._flownMicros = 0; }` then `return running.future;` with no JS hand-off; :388 `for (var frame = 0; ; frame++)` and :404 `last = after >= 1 || frame >= _maxEaseFrames;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: When a flight-length goal arrives during a follow glide, interrupt and start a fresh flight (JS on the web), or reset the frame counter when converting to a flight.

verdicts.reason: A recenter calls animateCamera(follow:false) with cameraFlightDuration of 1000 ms (google_map_provider.dart animateCamera). While a follow glide runs (easing true, _goal set, _done set, _jsFlight false because follow glides always step in Dart), easeCameraTo takes the join branch at map_camera_motion.dart:306-322. It sets _flight and _flownMicros=0 and returns without calling RiderMapBridge.flight. So the flight is stepped by _glide on the Dart 16 ms timer, the case the comment at :336-338 says the JS path exists to avoid. _glide's loop counter `frame` (:388) is not reset, and the flight branch ends with `last = after >= 1 || frame >= _maxEaseFrames` (:404). A 1 s flight needs about 62 frames. If the follow glide had already run more than about 178 frames (about 3 s of continuous retargets without settling), the flight snaps to its goal early. The comment at :316-317 makes joining intentional, but neither the missing JS hand-off nor the inherited frame cap is addressed there.
verdicts.repro: Static trace only (read-only run). Followed animateCamera -> easeCameraTo join branch -> _glide flight branch and worked the frame budget by hand: 1000 ms / 16 ms is about 62 frames, against a 240-frame cap counted from the start of the original glide.

verdicts.reason: animateCamera(follow:false) (google_map_provider.dart:96-107) calls _mayMove, which only clears movedByHandAt and does not interrupt. So a recenter during a running follow glide takes the join branch (map_camera_motion.dart:308-322). That branch sets _flight=1000ms and _flownMicros=0 and returns, without RiderMapBridge.flight. The flight is therefore stepped on the Dart 16 ms timer on the web too. In _glide the frame counter is a loop local (:388) that is never reset. The flight branch ends at `frame >= _maxEaseFrames` (:404), and then next=goal, a snap. A follow glide that keeps being retargeted can reach high frame counts: each GPS fix moves the goal, and with the 315 ms position time constant it needs about 77+ frames to settle within 2 m. So a recenter at frame 200 gets only 40 frames, about 640 ms. flightEase(0.64) is about 0.62 progress, so it jumps the last ~38%. The comment at :316-317 makes the join intentional, but the frame cap carry-over and the missing JS hand-off are not covered by it.
verdicts.repro: Read-only, no run. Traced the recenter path: animateCamera, _mayMove(follow:false), then the easeCameraTo join branch. Worked the frame budget by hand. A 1000 ms flight needs about 62 frames of 16 ms. A carried-over frame count of 180 or more cuts it short and snaps it at frame 240.
verdicts.evidence: map_camera_motion.dart:318-322 converts the glide in place with no JS hand-off; :388 `for (var frame = 0; ; frame++)`; :404 `last = after >= 1 || frame >= _maxEaseFrames`.

confirmed.title: MotionEngine lerp window is anchored at the previous fix's timestamp, so with fixes 420 ms or more apart t clamps to 1 and the home puck snaps between raw smoothed fixes (pose heading is unused)
confirmed.description: ingest() is called once per delivered fix (HomeController._deliverFix, lib/features/home/application/home_controller.dart:518) and passes `startedAt: _from!.timestamp` with a 420 ms window. `_from` is the previous accepted sample, whose timestamp is at least one fix interval (typically >= 1 s) old, so `now - startedAt` always exceeds 420 ms and the interpolator clamps to t=1, returning `_to` verbatim. There is no ticker that calls lerp between fixes, so the 'interpolation' is a no-op and the rider marker snaps to each raw smoothed point; heading likewise jumps. Not a crash, but the animation math does not do what the component is for.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On the home map the blue rider dot and heading cone jump between 1 Hz fixes rather than easing across the 420 ms window.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Record `startedAt = clock` when a new sample arrives and expose a `poseAt(now)` used by a frame ticker; or drop the interpolator if snapping is intended.

verdicts.corrected_title: MotionEngine lerp window is anchored at the previous fix's timestamp, so with fixes 420 ms or more apart t clamps to 1 and the home puck snaps between raw smoothed fixes (pose heading is unused)
verdicts.reason: motion_engine.dart:39-48 sets `_from = _to`, then calls lerp with `startedAt: _from!.timestamp` (the previous sample's GPS time), `now: DateTime.now()` and a 420 ms window. interpolator.dart:26-28 clamps `elapsed/total` to [0,1]. At the usual ≥1 Hz geolocator cadence, elapsed is at least the fix interval, so t=1 and the result is exactly `_to`. The only caller is HomeController._deliverFix (home_controller.dart:518), once per fix, and no ticker re-samples between fixes. home.dart:259-262 and _updateLocationVisuals (home.dart:1569-1585) paint the marker straight at that point without animating it. The finding's heading claim is moot: _deliverFix takes heading from position.heading/compass (home_controller.dart:531-536), not from pose.heading. The effect is cosmetic, but the component does not do what it exists for.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: MotionEngine.ingest -> PositionInterpolator.lerp math -> HomeController._deliverFix -> home.dart onFix -> _updateLocationVisuals/paintUserPuck. There is no frame ticker or animation controller on the puck position.

verdicts.corrected_title: MotionEngine starts its 420 ms window at the previous fix's GPS timestamp and nothing ticks between fixes, so the puck position snaps to each fix and the interpolator never animates
verdicts.reason: lib/core/motion/motion_engine.dart:41-49 calls lerp with `startedAt: _from!.timestamp`, the previous accepted fix's timestamp, and `now: DateTime.now()`. lib/core/motion/interpolator.dart:24-26 clamps `elapsed/420` to at most 1, so with fixes 420 ms or more apart t=1 and `_to` comes back unchanged. The only caller is HomeController._deliverFix (home_controller.dart:518), once per fix, and no frame ticker re-samples. The output therefore equals the raw fix and the interpolation does nothing. If fixes arrive less than 420 ms apart, it returns a partial point that stays put until the next fix. The heading part is misdescribed: pose.heading is never used for the puck. _deliverFix takes `heading` from the compass or position.heading (lines 532-537) and uses only pose.position and pose.cone.accuracy, so heading behaviour does not depend on this math.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_c2b3v_test.dart, since deleted. It fed fix A (t0) and then fix B (t0+1 s, 0.001 deg north, heading 90), with now = B's time + 50 ms. Output: `AUDIT20 progress=1.0 pos=59.001 heading=90.0`. The pose is exactly fix B, with no intermediate value.

confirmed.description: An interrupted CompletionJournal (app killed between writing the journal and finishing the handoff, or a storage failure) is replayed by Home on the next cold start (home.dart:508). handoff() writes next.stamped().toJson(), and stamped() sets savedAt = DateTime.now(). Neither handoff nor _replay compares the journal's completedAt with PersistedActiveRide.freshnessWindow. Home then reads a snapshot that is always isFresh and pushes AcceptRide.fromPersisted(B) directly, skipping the 'older than 6 hours' dialog that a normal snapshot of the same age would get.

confirmed.title: Ride check fired-trigger set and trip start are not restored after a reload, so an answered check can reopen and the 'longer trip' timer restarts
confirmed.description: _fired lives in the detector, which AcceptRide recreates in didChangeDependencies (accept_ride.dart:664). AcceptRide.fromPersisted after a reload or PWA resume therefore starts with no fired triggers, and checks the driver already answered on this trip can open again. The restore path also passes the restore time instead of the saved start (accept_ride_trip.dart:108 `startTrip(_rideCheckNow)`), although the detector's doc says 'Restored trips pass their saved start'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver answers a long-stop check ('Traffic'), Safari kills the tab, and the trip is restored while the car is still stuck. A couple of minutes later, the same long-stop check opens again on the same trip.
confirmed.evidence:
ride_check_detector.dart:10 'Each trigger opens at most once per trip.'; :17 `final Set<RideCheckTrigger> _fired = <RideCheckTrigger>{};`; :27-29 '/// Restored trips pass their saved start.'
accept_ride_trip.dart:107-108 `case ActiveRideStage.onTrip: _rideCheckDetector.startTrip(_rideCheckNow);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Persist the fired triggers (and the trip start) in the active-ride snapshot, or seed them from the trip's saved RideCheckRecords on restore. Pass restored.startedAt to startTrip.

A trip restored after a reload goes through home.dart:571 AcceptRide.fromPersisted, and nothing seeds the detector's fired triggers. _resumeStageSideEffects calls _rideCheckDetector.startTrip(_rideCheckNow) (accept_ride_trip.dart:117-118), although restored.startedAt is available and is already copied into _onTripStartedAt (accept_ride.dart:608). The detector doc (ride_check_detector.dart:27) says restored trips pass their saved start. After a restore, a longStop or offRoute check the driver already answered can open again: _stillSince starts fresh and _fired is empty. The 'longer than expected' check is also measured from the restore time, so it fires late. Effect: a repeated safety prompt on an edge path.

confirmed.title: After a pause or an open card, a 20 s ride-check tick that lands before the first observe() uses the old stop clock and can fire a false long stop
confirmed.description: _stillSince is only refreshed by observe(). The trip screen stops calling observe while the app is paused (_pauseLiveUpdates) and while any card is open (_rideCheckWatching is false). After resume, the first fix sets _hasLiveLocation = true (accept_ride_trip.dart:661) but calls _rideCheckObserve only after `await _refreshRoadRoute(force: true)` (up to the 8 s routing timeout, line 683-686). A 20 s ticker tick in that window calls tick(gps: true), which computes `at - _stillSince` from the old timestamp and fires longStop. Nothing resets _stillSince when observation resumes.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver switches to another navigation app for 5 minutes while driving, then returns. On resume, the routing request takes a few seconds. A ride-check tick lands in that window and opens 'Your car has stopped for 5 min', even though the car has been moving the whole time. The longStop trigger is then used up for the rest of the trip.
confirmed.evidence:
ride_check_detector.dart:81-82 `if (!gps) return _longer(at); return _longStop(at, place) ?? _longer(at);`
ride_check_detector.dart:132-133 `final stopped = at.difference(since); if (stopped <= Duration(minutes: rules.longStopMinutes)) return null;`
accept_ride_trip.dart:661 `_hasLiveLocation = location.isUsableAt(DateTime.now());` ... 683 `await _refreshRoadRoute(force: forceRoute);` ... 686 `_rideCheckObserve();`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Reset the stop clock (_stillAt = null / _stillSince = now) whenever observation resumes after a pause or after a card closes, or call observe before the awaited route refresh.

verdicts.reason: _stillSince is only refreshed in observe() (ride_check_detector.dart:57-63) or by tick at a planned stop (:77-79). Nothing resets it when observation resumes. _pauseLiveUpdates (accept_ride_trip.dart:126-145) clears _hasLiveLocation, and _rideCheckTick returns early while paused (:1519). On resume the first fix sets _hasLiveLocation = true (:689) but reaches _rideCheckObserve (:714) only after `await _refreshRoadRoute(force: true)` (:708), which awaits a forced ensureRoute network request (navigation_controller.dart:302ff). The 20 s Timer.periodic ticker (accept_ride.dart:667) can fire inside that window and call tick(gps: true) -> _longStop with the pre-pause _stillSince (:129-138), and longStop then cannot fire again (_fired, :172). The same happens after a card closes, because observe is skipped while _rideCheck.active (:1482-1484). The window is narrow: the position stream is subscribed before routing (:633-645), and its next fix goes through ensureRoute's non-forced early return (_routeInFlight, navigation_controller.dart ~345) to observe. That resets _stillSince if the car has moved more than 30 m. So the window is about one GPS interval, unless GPS is sparse.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _startLiveLocation -> _applyDriverPosition -> _refreshRoadRoute -> ensureRoute, of _rideCheckTick and the ticker setup, and of every writer of _stillSince. No guard resets the clock on resume or when a card closes. Not reproduced with a test, because the race involves widget timing.

verdicts.corrected_title: After a pause or an open card, a 20 s ride-check tick that lands before the first observe() uses the old stop clock and can fire a false long stop
verdicts.reason: ride_check_detector.dart:57-63 updates _stillSince only inside observe(), and tick() (:81-82) runs _longStop on whatever value is there. _pauseLiveUpdates (accept_ride_trip.dart:128-147) stops all observation, and _rideCheckWatching (:1489) blocks observe while a card is open. Nothing resets the clock when observation starts again. On resume, the first fix sets _hasLiveLocation=true (:695) before `await _refreshRoadRoute(force: true)` (:714), and _rideCheckObserve (:720) runs only after that await. A tick from accept_ride.dart:697 that lands in that gap calls tick(gps:true) and fires. The 8 s window in the finding is too wide, though. The stream subscription is set up before routing (:636-641) at 1 s intervals (driver_location_service.dart:72). The next fix's ensureRoute(force:false) returns at once while _routeInFlight is set (navigation_controller.dart ~343-349), so its observe resets the clock about 1 s later because the car has moved past the still radius. Real window: about 1 s out of each 20 s tick, so roughly a 5% chance per resume after a pause longer than the admin long-stop time (default 2 min, ride_check_admin_config.dart:10). The trigger then stays used up for the rest of the trip.

confirmed.title: Ride check reason is stored and sent to Movera in the driver's UI language, contrary to the 'record and alert keep English' rule
confirmed.description: ride_check_l10n.dart states that the topic, trigger and question values 'stay in English: they are what the trip record and the alert to Movera keep'. The reason, however, is built from tr.* (rcStoppedLead, rcMinutes, rcEndedLead, rcOffRouteLead, rcLongerLead, rcCrashLead…) at detection time. confirmed.title: ARCHITECTURE.md and the cancelSearch doc comment still describe the old offline cancel (commit locally); the code implements RC-03 (queued, not committed), so the docs are out of date
confirmed.description: ARCHITECTURE.md lines 13-17 state that on Finding, Cancel request commits the ride as `cancelledByRider`, archives it and clears the snapshot 'on its OK — or when it cannot be reached, leaving the outbox entry to retry'. The method doc of `cancelSearch` repeats it (1089-1091: 'unreachable: the same local commit, with the outbox entry kept'). The implementation does the opposite: `if (result == SearchCancelResult.queued) { _cancelInFlight = false; _cancelQueued = true; ... return result; }` (1123-1137) commits nothing, keeps the search listening and shows 'Cancelling…'. confirmed.title: `_refreshRoadRoute` has no request generation, so an older road-route answer can overwrite the route drawn for a changed destination
confirmed.description: `_adoptRoute` (line 395-406) and `_applyRouteChange` (line 700-711) update `_pickupPosition`/`_destinationPosition`, clear `_roadRoutePoints`, redraw, and then call `unawaited(_refreshRoadRoute())`. `_refreshRoadRoute` awaits `roadRoutePolyline(from: _pickupPosition, to: _destinationPosition)` (a network call via `RoutingService.roadLine`) and on return only checks `mounted` and `route.points.length < 2` before assigning `_roadRoutePoints = route.points` and redrawing. There is no check that the answer is for the route currently adopted. When a route change happens while the previous road request is still in flight (or a slow first request is beaten by the second), the older polyline lands last and is drawn between the new pickup/destination markers.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider changes the destination from the Finding screen (or the server's route-change event arrives) right after the screen opened. The new destination marker appears, then the road line for the OLD destination is drawn on the map and stays until another route change or ride stage.
confirmed.evidence: finding_drivers.dart:506-519 `Future<void> _refreshRoadRoute() async { if (_stops.isNotEmpty) return; final route = await roadRoutePolyline( id: 'route', from: _pickupPosition, to: _destinationPosition, color: RiderRouteStyle.color, ); if (!mounted || route.points.length < 2) return; _roadRoutePoints = route.points; _loadMapBits(); setState(() {}); }` | :403-405 `_roadRoutePoints = null; _loadMapBits(); if (_mapReady) unawaited(_refreshRoadRoute());` | :709-711 same in `_applyRouteChange`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Capture `from`/`to` (or a `++_routeGeneration`) before the await and discard the result when `_pickupPosition`/`_destinationPosition` changed (or the generation moved on) in the meantime.

verdicts.reason: finding_drivers.dart:506-519 `_refreshRoadRoute` only checks `mounted` and `points.length < 2` after awaiting `roadRoutePolyline`. Nothing ties the answer to the pickup and destination in effect when the request was sent. `_applyRouteChange` (701-711) and `_adoptRoute` (397-406) change the endpoints and start a new request, but a request started earlier by onMapCreated (852) is never cancelled. `RoutingService.roadLine` (core/maps/routing_service.dart:37-83) is a network POST with a 15s timeout (api_client.dart:42). On failure it falls back to a 2-point straight line, which also passes the `< 2` check, so even a timed-out old request overwrites the new route. It is worse when the new route has stops: `_refreshRoadRoute` returns early, and a late old answer sets `_roadRoutePoints`, which `_loadMapBits` (441-449) draws in preference to the stops line. The sibling screen guards this: waiting_for_driver.dart:2368-2378 checks `_routeKey != requestKey`. Finding has no such guard. The window is narrow: the first request has to still be pending when the rider finishes the route-change flow, which is plausible on a slow network.
verdicts.repro: Static trace. Followed the writers of `_pickupPosition`, `_destinationPosition` and `_roadRoutePoints` (lines 163-165, 399-405, 705-711, 516) and the callers of `_refreshRoadRoute` (405, 711, 852), through `roadRoutePolyline` (route_polyline.dart:43) into `roadLine` (timeout, straight-line fallback, cache keyed by endpoints). Compared with the requestKey guard in waiting_for_driver.dart:2378. `_applyRouteChange` is reached only from the rider's own route-change flow (line 683), not from a server event, so that part of the scenario is wrong but the race holds.

verdicts.reason: finding_drivers.dart:506-518 `_refreshRoadRoute` awaits `roadRoutePolyline` and then only checks `mounted` and `route.points.length < 2` before assigning `_roadRoutePoints`. Nothing ties the answer to the `_pickupPosition`/`_destinationPosition` it was requested for. Two requests can be in flight at once: the first starts in `onMapCreated` (:852), and `_applyRouteChange` (:701-711) starts another after a rider edit (:683). `RoutingService.roadLine` (routing_service.dart:37-80) goes to the network. With a 15 s ApiClient timeout (api_client.dart:42), it falls back to a straight line for the OLD points on timeout or error, so the old request can land after the new one. `_loadMapBits` (:441-449) prefers `_roadRoutePoints` over everything, so the stale line replaces the new route. It also replaces the stops path: when the new route has stops, the new call returns at once (:508) and the late old answer still overwrites. The old line then stays until the next route change. One correction: the finding mentions a 'server route-change event', but `_applyRouteChange` is only called from the rider's own edit at :683.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand. A starts in onMapCreated with (P, D1). The rider edits the destination: _applyRouteChange sets D2, clears _roadRoutePoints and starts B with (P, D2). B returns first (cache hit, fast reply, or the stops early return). A then returns after up to 15 s (timeout gives line(P, D1)) and sets _roadRoutePoints to the P to D1 polyline, which _loadMapBits draws between the P and D2 markers. Needs the first request to still be pending when the edit finishes, so it only happens on slow or stalled networks. No widget test was run because FindingDrivers needs the full AppScope.

confirmed.title: normaliseAddress forward-geocodes placeholder pickup labels, contrary to its own contract
confirmed.description: isPlaceholderPickupLabel's doc says a placeholder 'must not be forward-geocoded or saved' (home_controller.dart:62-69), but normaliseAddress only short-circuits '' and 'Current location'. _showRouteAddressPicker normalises draft['pickup'] unconditionally (home.dart:954), and that value is locationOffPickupLabel when _prefillPickup fell back (home.dart:818-822) or pickupLocationFallbackLabel ('Pickup location') / a 'Dropped pin …' label when the pin was placed on the map (confirmedPickupAddress, pickup_address.dart:46-49). Reproduced with a recording geocoder: forward() was called with 'Location off, set pickup' and 'Pickup location'. With the in-process mock the text comes back unchanged (in_process_mock_client.dart returns `'address': normalized`), but any real geocoder that fuzzy-matches returns some place name, which then becomes the pickup label shown in SelectRide and sent with the booking while pickupLat/Lng stay at the pin or the Stockholm default.

After the picker pops, forward('Pickup location') returns e.g. a business called 'Pickup Location AB' in another city; SelectRide and the booking carry that label with the pin's coordinates.

home_controller.dart:254-258 `Future<String> normaliseAddress(String input, {int? generation}) async { final clean = input.trim(); if (clean.isEmpty || clean == 'Current location') return clean; final scope = generation ?? _normaliseGuard.next(); final result = await geocoding.forward(clean);`

home.dart:954 `_normaliseAddress(rawPickup, generation: normaliseBatch),`

It ignores isPlaceholderPickupLabel (home_controller.dart:62-69), whose doc says placeholders 'must not be forward-geocoded', and it also ignores needsDroppedPinLabel (pickup_address.dart:41-43). _showRouteAddressPicker always normalises draft['pickup'] (home.dart:954). confirmed.title: Location permission is requested again immediately after the rider denies it, and again on every app resume
confirmed.description: _awaitCurrentFix loops two attempts; if the first detectCurrent returns quickly with permissionDenied (target == null), the second attempt starts a fresh detectCurrent, which calls location.requestPermission() again (home_controller.dart:369-371) — a second system prompt right after the first 'Deny'. didChangeAppLifecycleState(resumed) also calls _detectCurrentAddress() whenever _currentLatLng == null (home.dart:266-267), so an Android rider who denied once gets the prompt on each return to the app until Android auto-blocks it. iOS/web report deniedForever after one refusal, so only Android (and 'denied' on older Android indefinitely) is affected.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Android rider taps Where to with location not yet granted, denies the prompt; within the same tap the prompt appears a second time (attempt 2). Later, every time they switch apps and come back, the prompt is shown again.
confirmed.evidence:
home.dart:343-350 `for (var attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt++) { ... await _detectCurrentAddress().timeout(left, onTimeout: () {}); if (!mounted) return null; final fix = _tripPickupLatLng ?? _currentLatLng; if (fix != null) return fix; }`
home_controller.dart:368-371 `var permission = await location.checkPermission(); if (permission == LocationPermission.denied) { permission = await location.requestPermission(); }`
home.dart:266-267 `} else if (_currentLatLng == null) { _detectCurrentAddress(); }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Stop retrying when the first attempt ended in a permission failure (track the last DetectedLocation.failure), and on resume only re-detect when the last state was not permissionRequired.

verdicts.reason: home_controller.dart:368-371 calls location.requestPermission() whenever checkPermission() returns `denied`. Nothing stops it from running again after a fresh refusal. location_repository.dart:24-25 calls Geolocator directly and nothing caches the answer. In _awaitCurrentFix (home.dart:343-350) attempt 1 runs whenever attempt 0 got no fix. It never checks the failure reason, even though the comment says the retry is only meant to start 'once permission is granted'. The resume handler (home.dart:266-267) also re-detects whenever _currentLatLng == null and never checks HomeLocationState.permissionRequired. When Home's startup detect has already ended in 'denied', both attempts in the onFinish path (home.dart:807) start a new detectCurrent, so an Android rider is asked again within the same tap. On Android 11+ the OS turns a second refusal into deniedForever, so the extra prompts stop. On Android 10 and older they keep coming until 'Don't ask again' is ticked. iOS and web return deniedForever after one refusal, so they are not affected.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: home.dart:332-357 (_awaitCurrentFix retry loop), home.dart:324-328 (the in-flight join is cleared on completion, so the retry starts a new detect), home_controller.dart:357-399 (detectCurrent permission branch), home.dart:250-268 (resume handler), core/location/location_repository.dart:24 (direct Geolocator call). Nothing returns early on a permission failure. No runtime test: the OS permission dialog cannot be driven from flutter test.

verdicts.reason: detectCurrent() calls requestPermission() whenever checkPermission() is `denied` (home_controller.dart:368-371). On Android, geolocator_android's checkPermission never reports deniedForever: a not-granted permission always comes back as `denied` (PermissionManager.java:64). Nothing remembers that the rider already said no. The resume handler re-detects whenever `_currentLatLng == null` (home.dart:266-267), and `_awaitCurrentFix` makes a second fresh attempt when the first returns quickly with permissionDenied (home.dart:343-350). On Android the permission dialog itself pauses the activity (inactive) and resumes it when closed. So right after the rider taps Deny, the resume handler asks again at once. On Android 10 and older the prompt keeps coming back until the rider ticks "Don't ask again". On Android 11+ the OS stops it after the second refusal. iOS and web report deniedForever and are not affected.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_rider43_46_test.dart (now deleted). It pumped the real Home with GeolocatorPlatform.instance set to a fake whose checkPermission and requestPermission both return denied, then sent inactive followed by resumed three times. Output: `after mount requests=1`, `after resume #1 requests=2`, `after resume #2 requests=3`, `after resume #3 requests=4`. Every resume calls requestPermission again. The two-attempt loop in _awaitCurrentFix I traced by hand (home.dart:343-350) and did not run.

confirmed.title: Recenter button is hidden after a recenter that was interrupted or blocked, leaving the map off the rider with no way back
confirmed.description: _recenterOnUser unconditionally ends with `setState(() => _showRecenterButton = false)`. The flight future completes early when a finger touches the map (MapView.touching -> interrupt() completes _done, map_camera_motion.dart:76-94), and the refinement glide `_flyToUser(fresh, follow: true)` is a no-op when heldByRider (google_map_provider.dart:81, 102). In both cases the camera is not on the rider, any 'show' decision made by _handleMapCameraMove during the rider's pan is overwritten with false, and the button only returns after the next camera move event.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider taps recenter; while latestFix() runs (up to 9 s) they pan the map elsewhere (button correctly shows). latestFix returns a point >15 m away, the follow glide is refused because the map is held, then _showRecenterButton = false: the map stays where they panned and the recenter button is gone until they move the map again.
confirmed.evidence:
home.dart:1664-1668 `await _flyToUser(fresh, follow: known != null); } else { await flight; } if (mounted) setState(() => _showRecenterButton = false);`
map_camera_motion.dart:306 `if (view.touching) return Future<void>.value();`
google_map_provider.dart:102 `if (map == null || !_mayMove(map, follow)) return;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Only clear _showRecenterButton when the glide actually landed (e.g. re-evaluate with AppScope.instance.camera.showRecenter against the last camera pose), or leave it to _handleMapCameraMove.

verdicts.reason: _recenterOnUser always ends with setState(() => _showRecenterButton = false) (home.dart:1668), whether or not the camera reached the rider. The first glide uses follow:false (home.dart:1639). A finger on the map calls interrupt(), which completes the flight early (map_camera_motion.dart:71-94). A fresh fix that would move the camera is sent with follow:true (home.dart:1663), and _mayMove refuses it while heldByRider (google_map_provider.dart:79-81; followHold is 12 s, map_camera_motion.dart:55). latestFix is a bestForNavigation getCurrentPosition that can take up to 9 s (home_controller.dart:613-622). If the rider pans and lets go before it returns, the 'show' value that _handleMapCameraMove set during the pan (home.dart:1615-1628) is overwritten with false. The map is left away from the rider and the recenter button (home.dart:1943) is hidden. It comes back on the next camera move, so the effect is minor.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: home.dart:1631-1684, 1615-1629 and 1943; map_camera_motion.dart:44-94; google_map_provider.dart:79-108; home_controller.dart:613-622. The final hide does not depend on whether the camera reached the rider.

verdicts.reason: `_recenterOnUser` always ends with `setState(() => _showRecenterButton = false)` (home.dart:1668), whether or not the camera reached the rider. Only _handleMapCameraMove turns the button back on (home.dart:1615-1629), so it needs another camera-move event. Suppose the rider touches the map during the 1 s flight: touching=true calls interrupt(), which completes the flight's future (map_camera_motion.dart:71-94). They pan away and lift their finger while latestFix (bestForNavigation, up to 9 s, home_controller.dart:613-622) is still running. When latestFix returns, either `await flight` resolves at once (fix within 15 m), or the follow:true refinement is refused because heldByRider is true (google_map_provider.dart:81, 102). Either way the button is set to false while the map sits where the rider panned it. It stays hidden until they move the map again. The effect is minor and the rider can recover with one more pan.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand (needs a real map controller): tap → _flyToUser(known, follow:false) → finger down → interrupt() completes _done → pan, onCameraMove sets the button to shown → finger up, no more camera events → latestFix resolves → `await flight` (already complete) or a refused follow glide → `_showRecenterButton = false`. Nothing between those steps checks the camera pose.

confirmed.title: Chat message times use the Material 12/24-hour locale default instead of the app's 24-hour rule
confirmed.description: _messageTime formats with `TimeOfDay.fromDateTime(sentAt.toLocal()).format(context)`, which follows MaterialLocalizations.timeOfDayFormat: for the 'en' locale that is 'h:mm a' (12-hour, '3:05 PM') unless MediaQuery.alwaysUse24HourFormat is set. confirmed.title: A push sent the day before is labelled with no day (as today) when it is ingested on the day after spring-forward, because Duration.inDays between local midnights is 0 (23h)
confirmed.description: _formatTime computes `today.difference(day).inDays` where both are local midnights built with DateTime(y,m,d). On the day after a spring-forward transition the two midnights are 23 hours apart (verified by throwaway test under TZ=Europe/Stockholm: DateTime(2026,3,30).difference(DateTime(2026,3,29)) == 23:00:00), so inDays == 0 and the function returns only the clock, dropping the 'Yesterday' prefix the FLOW-18 comment promises. More generally, any day count across a DST change is one short (a notification from 3 days ago reads as 2 days -> still fine, but 2 days ago reads as 1 -> 'Yesterday').
confirmed.failure_scenario: Sunday 29 Mar 2026 (Europe/Stockholm) at 23:10 a 'Driver arrived' push arrives. On Monday 30 Mar the Notifications list shows it as '23:10' (today) instead of 'Yesterday 23:10'; a push from Saturday 28 Mar shows as 'Yesterday'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Compare calendar days with UTC-constructed midnights: `DateTime.utc(now.year, now.month, now.day).difference(DateTime.utc(time.year, time.month, time.day)).inDays`.

verdicts.corrected_title: A push sent the day before is labelled with no day (as today) when it is ingested on the day after spring-forward, because Duration.inDays between local midnights is 0 (23h)
verdicts.reason: notifications_repository.dart:92-97: today.difference(day).inDays is computed from local midnights, and on 30 Mar 2026 in Stockholm the gap is 23h, so inDays is 0 and only the clock is returned. The finding's scenario is misdescribed, though. The label is worked out once, at ingest (line 53, time: _formatTime(at)), and the UI shows the stored string (notifications.dart:190), so a push that arrived Sunday already reads '23:10' because it was 'today' then. The bug only shows when a push whose sentAt (firebase_push_service.dart:151, message.sentTime) is the previous day is ingested on that Monday. That happens, for example, when the rider taps yesterday's tray notification (push_coordinator.dart:56-58, 73-74) or a push is delivered late.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway probe under TZ=Europe/Stockholm printed 'days 0' for DateTime(2026,3,30).difference(DateTime(2026,3,29)).inDays. Traced ingest callers in push_coordinator.dart and the display at notifications.dart:190.

verdicts.corrected_title: Notification day label uses Duration.inDays between local midnights; a notification ingested the day after spring-forward with a sentAt on the previous day is labelled as today
verdicts.reason: notifications_repository.dart:92-96 computes DateTime(today).difference(DateTime(day)).inDays. Across the spring-forward night the two local midnights are 23 hours apart, so inDays is 0 and line 96 returns only the clock. Note the label is computed once, at ingest (line 53, time: _formatTime(at)), using _now() at ingest. The bug therefore needs a push whose sentAt falls on the previous day but which is ingested on the day after the transition (for example a late delivery, or one opened from the tray the next morning). The finding's scenario (arrives Sunday, is shown Monday) is really the separate issue that labels are frozen at ingest, not the DST problem.
verdicts.repro: I ran a throwaway test under TZ=Europe/Stockholm with NotificationsRepository(now: 2026-03-30 09:00). Output: 'diff=23:00:00.000000'. A push with sentAt 2026-03-29 23:10 got 'label=23:10' instead of 'Yesterday 23:10'. A push with sentAt 2026-03-28 14:00 got 'label=Yesterday 14:00' instead of '28 Mar 14:00'. The control case, now 2026-10-14 with sentAt 2026-10-13 23:10, got 'control=Yesterday 23:10'.

confirmed.title: Notification time label is frozen at ingest, so items never become "Yesterday …"
confirmed.description: FLOW-18 says only today's items show just the time and older ones name the day. `_formatTime(at)` is evaluated once when the item is ingested (206-213) and stored in `AppNotification.time`; `_formatTime` compares against `_now()` at that moment (248-261). The screen renders `notification.time` (notifications.dart:630) and never recomputes from `at`. The feed is in-memory for the process, so any app/tab left open across midnight shows yesterday's pushes with a bare clock.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Push at 23:50 shows "23:50"; the next morning the same row still says "23:50" instead of "Yesterday 23:50".
confirmed.evidence:
notifications_repository.dart:206-213 `final at = (payload.sentAt ?? _now()).toLocal(); _items.insert(0, AppNotification(... time: _formatTime(at), at: at, ...`
notifications.dart:630 `text: notification.time,`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Format from `notification.at` at build time (or recompute labels on emit).

verdicts.reason: lib/features/notifications/data/notifications_repository.dart:46-53 computes `time: _formatTime(at)` once inside ingest(), and _formatTime (lines 88-101) compares against `_now()` at that moment. AppNotification.time is a final String (domain/notifications.dart:19), copyWith keeps it (line 31), and the row renders `notification.time` (presentation/notifications.dart:190); nothing reformats from `at`. The feed is an in-memory singleton (NotificationsRepository.shared), so a session left open across midnight keeps a bare clock on yesterday's items, which breaks the FLOW-18 rule written in the comment at lines 86-87. The line numbers in the finding are stale, but the code it describes is accurate.
verdicts.repro: Static trace. Followed ingest -> _formatTime -> AppNotification.time -> the notifications.dart:190 render. The only other write is markRead/copyWith, which copies `time` unchanged. No timer, rebuild or locale hook recomputes the label.

verdicts.reason: The audit's line numbers are out of date, but the code does what it says. lib/features/notifications/data/notifications_repository.dart:46-53 computes `time: _formatTime(at)` once, when the item is ingested. `_formatTime` (lines 88-101) compares against `_now()` at that moment, and the result is stored as a String in AppNotification.time (domain/notifications.dart:16). The screen renders `text: notification.time` (presentation/notifications.dart:190) and never reformats from `at`. The feed is an in-memory singleton (`NotificationsRepository.shared`) with no recompute anywhere, so a process that stays alive past midnight keeps showing a bare clock. That contradicts the FLOW-18 comment at lines 86-87.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_c2b3v_test.dart, since deleted. It injected now=2026-10-20 23:50, ingested a push, then moved the clock to 2026-10-21 08:00 and read all().first.time. Output: `AUDIT51 before=23:50 after=23:50 at=2026-10-20 23:50:00.000`. After midnight FLOW-18 expects "Yesterday 23:50".

confirmed.title: `_idle` turns a superseded (null) reverse-geocode into the 'Pickup location' fallback and can overwrite the newer resolved address
confirmed.description: Every `onCameraIdle` (line 345-349) calls `_idle()`, which awaits `_pickup.reverse(_center)`. `PickupMapController.reverse` (pickup_controller.dart:53-74) deliberately returns `null` for a call that was superseded by a newer one (`if (!_stale.isCurrent(generation)) return null;`). `_idle` does not distinguish 'superseded' from 'no address': `isUnusablePickupLabel(null)` is true, so it does `setState(() { _address = pickupLocationFallbackLabel; _search.text = label; })`. The two lookups are independent HTTP requests (AppGeocoding dedupes only identical keys), so when the newer request B completes before the older request A, B's continuation writes the real street and A's continuation then overwrites it with 'Pickup location'. `_confirmPosition` (line 296-305) books `confirmedPickupAddress(_address, position)`, which keeps that fallback string. Contrast set_pickup_page.dart:550-570 `_resolveAddressNow`, which guards with its own `_resolveGeneration` and `_isAwayFrom(at, _center)` before applying.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider drags the pin, lets go (request A starts), nudges it once more and lets go (request B starts). B answers first and shows 'Klockarvägen 37'; A then answers (as null, superseded) and the card flips to 'Pickup location'. The rider confirms and the booking/driver gets the neutral label 'Pickup location' although the street had been resolved.
confirmed.evidence: confirm_pickup_spot.dart:222-233 `Future<void> _idle() async { if (_moving) return; final address = await _pickup.reverse(_center); if (!mounted) return; final label = isUnusablePickupLabel(address) ? pickupLocationFallbackLabel : address!.trim(); setState(() { _address = label; _search.text = label; }); }` | pickup_controller.dart:61 `if (!_stale.isCurrent(generation)) return null;` | pickup_address.dart:18-23 `bool isUnusablePickupLabel(String? label) { final clean = label?.trim() ?? ''; return clean.isEmpty || ...` | confirm_pickup_spot.dart:300 `final address = confirmedPickupAddress(_address, position);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give `_idle` its own generation counter (or read `_pickup`'s) and return without touching state when the lookup was superseded or when `_isAwayFrom(at)`; only apply the fallback label when the current lookup genuinely returned no address.

verdicts.reason: PickupMapController.reverse (pickup_controller.dart:53-74) returns null for any call superseded by a newer one, because the StaleGuard generation is no longer current. _idle (confirm_pickup_spot.dart:222-233) checks only `mounted` after the await, then maps null to pickupLocationFallbackLabel and calls setState. Nothing compares against a generation, against _center or against _moving. So whenever an older lookup A completes after a newer lookup B, A overwrites B's resolved street with 'Pickup location'. This ordering is realistic. AppGeocoding.reverse (app_geocoding.dart:68-86) serves B from its cache keyed at 5 decimal places, or from a quicker HTTP or Nominatim reply, while A is still on the network. _confirmPosition (:296-305) then books confirmedPickupAddress(_address), so the booking and the driver get 'Pickup location' even though a street had been resolved. Compare _refreshCurrentFix (:174), which does guard with _isAwayFrom.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the onCameraIdle -> _idle -> PickupMapController.reverse -> StaleGuard.isCurrent path, plus the AppGeocoding cache and in-flight dedupe, which only merges identical keys, so a cache hit for B returns immediately while A is pending. No widget test was run.

verdicts.reason: `PickupMapController.reverse` returns null when a newer call has superseded it (pickup_controller.dart:61). `_idle` (confirm_pickup_spot.dart:222-233) cannot tell that apart from 'no address': `isUnusablePickupLabel(null)` is true, so it sets `_address`/`_search.text` to 'Pickup location' with no generation check and no `_isAwayFrom` check. Compare `_refreshCurrentFix` at :175, which has that check. AppGeocoding.reverse (app_geocoding.dart:66-85) answers a cached or in-flight key at once, so out-of-order completion is realistic: the rider drags back to a spot already resolved (B comes from cache) while an earlier lookup A is still on the network. `_confirmPosition` then books `confirmedPickupAddress('Pickup location')`, which keeps the label (pickup_address.dart). Home's `bookingPickupAddress` does not count 'Pickup location' as unusable, so it is never re-resolved. Even when answers arrive in order, the card shows 'Pickup location' for a moment. Impact is limited: the coordinates still travel with the booking, so only the label is wrong.

Output: `AUDIT57 idle(2.0) -> Klockarvagen 37`, then `AUDIT57 idle(1.0) -> Pickup location`, then `AUDIT57 final display=Pickup location confirmed=Pickup location`. Test file deleted.

verdicts.corrected_title: Set pickup address search has no try/catch (a failed geocode shows no feedback) and no staleness guard against a pin moved while it was pending
verdicts.reason: set_pickup_page.dart:702 awaits _pickup.search(text) with no try/catch. pickup_controller.dart:113-120 and AppGeocoding.forward/_forwardFromApi (app_geocoding.dart:46-65, 94-106) do not catch either, and they apply an 8 s .timeout. So when the rider is offline or the request times out, the future started from InkWell onTap (:1121) ends as an uncaught async error and the 'addressNotFoundMoveMap' snackbar never shows. Nothing marks the page busy during the search, and _glideTo (:576-623) unconditionally rewrites _center/_routeStart/_address. Unlike the reverse lookups, it has no generation check on entry. A pin drag or chip tap made while the search is pending is therefore overwritten when the search returns. Impact is limited: the pin then goes to the address the rider explicitly searched for, the jump is visible before Confirm, and the mock geocoder answers almost at once. Hence low, not medium. The finding's claim that the rider 'confirms a pickup they did not choose' overstates it.

confirmed.description: `PromotionDetailsSheet.open` defaults `categories` to `AppScope.instance.rideCatalog.rides()`. In di.dart:337 `rideCatalog` is `RideSelectionRepository()`, whose `builtInRides` is the 14-item fallback list that explicitly includes seven 'Categories the admin may switch on later' (van, wheelchair, business, airport, kids, women, delivery; ride_selection_repository.dart:84-162). The live catalog is `AppScope.instance.catalog.current` (di.dart:341, RideCatalogController), which SelectRide uses for its own `_openPromotionDetails`. PayWithPage (pay_with_page.dart:271 `PromotionDetailsSheet.open(context, promo)`) and the default `onTap` of PromotionTicket (promotion_ticket.dart:54) use the default, so the 'Prices with promotion' section lists categories the rider cannot book and, when `rideTypes` is empty, marks each 'Included'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Server catalog has the 7 seed categories. Rider opens Pay with → taps the promotion row → sheet lists Van, Wheelchair, Business, Airport, Kids seat, Women driver and Delivery as 'Included', none of which exist on Select Ride.
confirmed.evidence: promotion_details_sheet.dart:74-79 `final list = categories ?? [ for (final ride in AppScope.instance.rideCatalog.rides()) PromotionCategory(id: ride.id, name: ride.name), ];`; di.dart:337 `late final RideSelectionRepository rideCatalog = RideSelectionRepository();` vs di.dart:341 `late final RideCatalogController catalog = RideCatalogController(api: api);`; ride_selection_repository.dart:84-85 `// Categories the admin may switch on later; the pictures ship with the // app, the admin decides what is shown.`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Default to `AppScope.instance.catalog.current` (the server/cached catalog) instead of `rideCatalog.rides()`.

That is `RideSelectionRepository.builtInRides` (ride_selection_repository.dart:4-9: 'the last fallback when neither the server nor the cache can answer'): 14 items, including 7 'Categories the admin may switch on later' (84-85). The live list is `RideCatalogController.current` (di.dart:341; ride_catalog_controller.dart:39). pay_with_page.dart:271, side_menu.dart:505 and the home ticket (home.dart:2211 → promotion_ticket.dart:54 default onTap) all use the fallback. confirmed.description: resolveNoDriverFound records reason 'no_driver_found', and the live-ride cancel records 'rider_cancelled_live' (reservation_live_ride.dart:81, reservation_ride_realtime.dart:148). confirmed.title: ReservationPriceChange treats any change under 0.5 major units as unchanged, so EUR/TND edits under half a unit show a zero difference and a 'price unchanged' summary
confirmed.original_title: ReservationPriceChange treats any change under 0.5 major units as 'unchanged', so euro and dinar edits show a 0 difference between two different prices
confirmed.description: ReviewChangesPage builds ReservationPriceChange(previous: original.price, next: draft.price, currency: original.currency). It shows the previous and new prices, then a difference of kr(0) whenever `unchanged`. The 0.5 threshold suits whole-kronor SEK display only. EUR is formatted with cents and TND with millimes (formatMoney), so a real change of up to 0.49 EUR or 0.499 DT is shown as a zero difference. The class also holds a single currency, so when the edited pickup is priced in another currency (draft.currency = selection.currency) the two amounts are subtracted across currencies.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A Paris (EUR) reservation was booked at 12.35 €, and the edit re-quotes it at 12.70 €. Review changes shows Previous '12,35 €', New '12,70 €', Difference '0,00 €'. The rider confirms an edit that costs 0.35 € more while being told the difference is zero.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Compare in minor units with Money.fromLegacyMajor(next, currency) != Money.fromLegacyMajor(previous, currency), or set the threshold at half a displayed unit per currency. Refuse, or show separately, a change across currencies.

verdicts.reason: reservation.dart:178 sets `unchanged => delta.abs() < 0.5`. review_changes.dart:23-27 builds the change from original.price and draft.price, and review_changes.dart:110-112 shows kr(0) when unchanged. ReservationFormat.kr (reservation_format.dart:95) calls formatMajor(whole: true). In shared/formatters/money.dart:24-37 `whole` rounds only SEK; EUR and TND keep their minor digits. The EUR and TND markets exist in rider_app_config.dart:490 and :529. So a 0.35 EUR change shows as '0,00 €', and change.summary (reservation.dart:181) says resPriceUnchanged. The cross-currency half is weaker: the class uses original.currency for both amounts, but an edit that moves the pickup into another market is an edge case. The rider still sees both real prices on the cards above.
verdicts.repro: Read-only static trace (no flutter/dart run). Worked by hand: previous 12.35, next 12.70, delta 0.35 < 0.5 so unchanged; kr(0,'EUR') -> formatMoney(Money(0,'EUR'), whole:true) -> '0,00 €'.

verdicts.reason: reservation.dart:178 `unchanged => delta.abs() < 0.5` is a whole-krona threshold, and review_changes.dart:110-111 then shows kr(0, currency) as the difference. EUR and TND fares are not whole units: mock_catalog_fares.dart sets EUR stepMinor 5 (0.05 €) and TND stepMinor 100 (0.1 DT), and money.dart:34-37 always prints EUR and TND to the minor unit. So 12.35 -> 12.70 € gives delta 0.35 < 0.5: the row shows '0,00 €' and the summary says resPriceUnchanged, while the Previous and New rows show different prices. The cross-currency part is speculative: it needs an edit whose pickup moves into another zone, and I did not trace that path.
verdicts.repro: Read only, no run. Worked by hand: 12.70 - 12.35 = 0.35 (double, about 0.35000000000000142), abs < 0.5, so unchanged is true. That leads to formatMajor(0,'EUR'), which prints '0,00 €'. The 0.05 € fare step comes from MockZoneCurrency.eur in lib/core/api/mock_catalog_fares.dart.
