confirmed.title: An unresolved 'No driver found' ride stays the chrono's next ride and stops a later ride's live screen from auto-opening
confirmed.original_title: An unresolved 'No driver found' ride stays the chrono's next ride and stops a later ride's live screen from auto-opening
confirmed.description: _nextRide always returns the earliest upcoming reservation. A no-driver-found ride is still `upcoming` (driverAssignmentPending) until the rider resolves it. If they swipe the sheet away, _promptedNoDriverId stops it reappearing, but the ride stays first. _openLiveIfNeeded and _promptNoDriverIfNeeded only look at _nextRide(), so a later reservation that gets a driver and goes en route is never auto-opened, and tapping the chrono opens the stale no-driver sheet again.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Demo build: ride A (09:00) timed out without a driver and the rider dismissed the sheet. Ride B (11:00) gets a driver, and at 10:58 its driver goes en route. Home keeps showing A's red badge and never opens B's live ride. The rider only finds B through History > Upcoming.
confirmed.evidence:
home_reservation_chrono.dart:199-204: final upcoming = [..._reservations.upcoming()]..sort(...); return upcoming.first;
home_reservation_chrono.dart:132-136: final ride = _nextRide(); if (ride == null || !ride.revealsDriver) return;
confirmed.suggested_fix: For live auto-open, pick the first ride that reveals a driver. For the chrono, skip rides already prompted as no-driver when a later actionable ride exists.

verdicts.reason: _nextRide (home_reservation_chrono.dart:199-204) returns the earliest isUpcoming ride. A no-driver ride is still scheduled or driverAssignmentPending, both of which count as upcoming (reservation_status.dart:15-21). Nothing cancels it automatically: startLiveIfDue (reservation_controller.dart:328-395) never cancels, and isNoDriverFound is only a predicate. If the rider dismisses the sheet, choice is null and the code returns without resolving (line 119). _openLiveIfNeeded (lines 132-136) checks only _nextRide().revealsDriver, so a later ride B that goes en route is never auto-opened. The only other caller of ReservationLiveRide.open is upcoming_reservation.dart:102, which is reached manually. Tapping the chrono calls _openRide(A) and opens the no-driver sheet again (lines 156-160).
verdicts.repro: Read-only static trace of _nextRide, _openLiveIfNeeded, _promptNoDriverIfNeeded and isUpcoming, plus a grep for other ReservationLiveRide.open callers.

verdicts.reason: _nextRide (home_reservation_chrono.dart:199-204) always returns the earliest upcoming ride. A no-driver ride keeps the scheduled or driverAssignmentPending status (isNoDriverFound, reservation_controller.dart:306-316, is derived and nothing changes the status), so it stays in upcoming() (:141-142) until resolveNoDriverFound runs. Dismissing the sheet (choice == null at :119) only sets _promptedNoDriverId. _openLiveIfNeeded (:132-136) checks only _nextRide().revealsDriver, so a later ride that reveals its driver is never auto-opened, and tapping the chrono reopens the no-driver sheet (:158-163). Reachable in demo or mock dispatch when ride A gets no driver but ride B does.
verdicts.repro: Read only, no run. Traced it by hand with A at 09:00 (no driver, dismissed) and B at 11:00 (driver en route at 10:58): _nextRide() returns A, A.revealsDriver is false, so the function returns early and B is never opened.

confirmed.title: cardDate 'Tomorrow' label breaks on the spring-forward day because today.add(Duration(days:1)) is not the next local midnight
confirmed.description: cardDate compares `day == today.add(const Duration(days: 1))` where today is a local midnight. Dart's add() works in absolute time, so on the DST switch day the result is 01:00 of the next day, not midnight (verified by throwaway test: DateTime(2026,3,29).add(Duration(days:1)) == 2026-03-30 01:00:00 under Europe/Stockholm). The equality then fails and the reservation card falls through to weekdayDate instead of 'Tomorrow, 30 Mar'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On Sunday 29 Mar 2026 a Stockholm rider with a reservation on Monday 30 Mar sees 'Mon, 30 Mar' on the upcoming card instead of 'Tomorrow 30 Mar'. Same for Tunisia or any zone with DST on its switch day.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Build tomorrow as `DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day + 1)` (calendar arithmetic) instead of adding a Duration.

verdicts.reason: reservation_format.dart:143 compares day == today.add(const Duration(days: 1)). On a DST change day that sum is not the next local midnight, so the equality fails and cardDate (used at :205 for the reservation card line) falls through to weekdayDate instead of 'Tomorrow'. This happens on both the spring and the autumn switch. The Tunisia example in the finding is wrong because Tunisia has no DST, but Sweden and France are affected.
verdicts.repro: Wrote test/_audit_r64dst_test.dart and ran `TZ=Europe/Stockholm flutter test test/_audit_r64dst_test.dart`. Output: 'add=2026-03-30 01:00:00.000 eq=false' and 'fall add=2026-10-25 23:00:00.000 eq=false', then 'All tests passed!'. The file was deleted afterwards.

verdicts.reason: reservation_format.dart:139-145 compares the calendar day `day` with today.add(const Duration(days:1)). DateTime.add adds absolute time, so on a DST switch day the result is not the next local midnight, the equality fails, and cardDate falls through to weekdayDate. It is reached through historyWhen (:204-205), which is used by the upcoming/reservation cards (reservation_widgets.dart:382) and the History detail (ride_history.dart:546). This affects both switch days, not only spring. The Tunisia example is wrong because Tunisia has no DST; Stockholm, the primary market in DECISIONS.md:42, does.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test run with TZ=Europe/Stockholm. Output: 'today=2026-03-29 00:00 add1d=2026-03-30 01:00 calendarTomorrow=2026-03-30 00:00 equal=false' and 'today=2026-10-25 00:00 add1d=2026-10-25 23:00 calendarTomorrow=2026-10-26 00:00 equal=false'. Control: 'today=2026-06-01 ... equal=true'. So on 29 Mar and 25 Oct 2026, a ride the next day gets the weekday label instead of 'Tomorrow'.

confirmed.title: Editing a reservation keeps its dispatch status: a searching or no-driver ride moved to a later day stays 'searching'
confirmed.original_title: Editing a reservation keeps its dispatch status: a searching or no-driver ride moved to a later day stays 'searching'
confirmed.description: canEdit covers driverAssignmentPending (and the no-driver-found state), so the Upcoming page offers Edit. The edit goes through ScheduledRideBooking.confirm -> ReservationController.update with a patch that changes the time and route but not status. confirmed.title: Scheduled booking does not re-quote a quote that expired during the date picker and Set pickup; booking fails with a no-price toast and needs two more taps
confirmed.description: `_book` checks `quoteIsAvailable` once, then `_bookScheduled` opens the date-time picker and Set pickup (and possibly the picker again for return rides) before `ScheduledRideCheckout.run` → `draftFrom` → `ScheduledRideBooking.quotedPrice`, which throws `ScheduledQuoteRequiredException` as soon as `authoritativePriceFor` is null. Quotes expire after 2 minutes (in_process_mock_client.dart:2173 and catalog_quote_repository.dart:35), so a rider who spends more than two minutes choosing a time and pickup spot gets the `resErrNoPriceBook` toast and nothing is booked; Book now handles the same situation by re-quoting in place (`_quoteAfterPickup`, RIDE-2) but the scheduled path has no equivalent. Tapping Book again then shows 'price unavailable, refreshing' and the rider must repeat the picker and pickup steps.

Quotes expire 120 s after they are issued (in_process_mock_client.dart:2173). confirmed.title: SwedishPhone.toE164 accepts a trunk zero after +46 and stores an invalid contact number
confirmed.description: After normalising, the function only checks that the part after `+46` is 7–10 digits (116-119). Input like `+46 070 123 45 67` (a very common way to write a Swedish mobile) becomes `+46070…`, which passes (10 digits) and is stored as the emergency contact's `phoneE164` and sent to the share/alert backend, but is not a dialable E.164 number.

confirmed.evidence: phone_e164.dart:115-119 `if (!value.startsWith('+46')) return null; final rest = value.substring(3); if (rest.length < 7 || rest.length > 10) return null; if (!_digits.hasMatch(rest)) return null; return '+46$rest';`

verdicts.reason: lib/features/safety/domain/phone_e164.dart:4-18 (the file is 29 lines, so the cited line 116 is wrong). After '+46' is detected, `rest` is only checked for length 7-10 and all digits, so a trunk '0' is kept. The emergency contact form is a free-text TextField (emergency_contacts_page.dart:327-330, keyboardType phone, no formatter), and SafetyStore.addContact (safety_store.dart:136-155) saves whatever toE164 returns as phoneE164. Its duplicate check also misses '+4670...' against '+46070...'. The auth path (auth_navigation.dart:68-71) is safe because it only adds +46 when the input has no leading 0.

confirmed.title: `_ContactEditorState._save` calls setState in its catch block without a mounted check; the editor is a dismissible sheet
confirmed.description: `_ContactEditor` is shown through `MoveraSheet.show` (line 42-46) with the defaults `swipeDismissible = true, barrierDismissible = true` (movera_sheet.dart:22-23), so the rider can swipe it away while `await widget.controller.addContact/editContact` is in flight. The success branch guards with `if (mounted) Navigator.pop(context);` but the catch branch does `setState(() { _error = ...; _saving = false; })` unconditionally. If the save fails after the sheet was dismissed, `setState` runs on a disposed State: an assertion error in debug ('setState() called after dispose()'), a null-check error on `_element` in release, surfacing as an unhandled async error from the button's unawaited `_save()` future.

verdicts.reason: emergency_contacts_page.dart:284-291: the success branch checks `if (mounted)`, but the catch branch calls setState(...) and reads `context.l10n` without a check. The save awaits a remote call: SafetyStore.createContact -> _write(() => _remote.createContact(...)) (safety_store.dart:165), so the rider has time to dismiss the sheet. SafetyController.addContact rethrows failures (safety_controller.dart:228-233). onPressed is `_saving ? null : _save` (:396), which does not await the Future. So a remote failure after dismissal throws 'setState() called after dispose()' (or a null-check error on _element in release), and it escapes as an unhandled async error. The rider sees nothing; the only effect is a spurious crash report.

confirmed.title: Trip camera approach loop and 33 ms car-marker ticker keep updating the hidden trip map while another route covers AcceptRide
confirmed.description: AcceptRide pauses live updates only on app lifecycle changes (didChangeAppLifecycleState -> `_pauseLiveUpdates` -> `_camera.suspend()`). Unlike Home (didPushNext -> `_pauseHomeUpdates`), it is not RouteAware. When the driver opens a full-screen route from the trip, for example `onHistory: () => pushSingle(context, MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => const DriverRideHistory()))` (accept_ride.dart:1307), the chat, destination picker or safety screens, GPS keeps arriving and `_camera.update` keeps retargeting. GoogleDriverCameraPort's loop paces itself with `Timer`-based `_sleep(16 ms)`, not vsync, so it keeps calling `controller.moveCamera` about 60 times a second on the hidden map. Each frame's `onFrame` snaps the vehicle pose, so the 33 ms `_ThrottledVehicleMap` timer keeps pushing marker updates. On web each of those pushes also leaks a Blob URL (see the first finding).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Mid-trip, the driver opens Ride history from the island and reads it for 2 minutes while driving. The invisible trip map gets about 7,200 camera moves and about 3,600 marker pushes, which wastes CPU and battery on native and grows memory on web. Worked out from the code; not run.
confirmed.evidence:
accept_ride.dart:715-724 only lifecycle states call `_rideLifecycle.persistNow(); _AcceptRideTrip(this)._pauseLiveUpdates();`
google_driver_camera_port.dart:328-329 `await _sleep(Duration(milliseconds: settled ? 50 : 16));` (Timer-based, lines 557-563)
accept_ride.dart:1257-1260 `onFrame: (position) { ... _vehicle.snapTo(position.target, _camera.vehicleCourse); }`
home.dart:174 `void didPushNext() { _routeVisible = false; _pauseHomeUpdates(); }` (Home has the guard, AcceptRide does not)
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make AcceptRide RouteAware (or check TickerMode/ModalRoute.isCurrent). On didPushNext suspend the camera and stop the 33 ms ticker, keeping GPS and the trip logic running. On didPopNext resume and recenter.

It has no RouteAware/didPushNext hook, unlike Home. Routes pushed over the trip, such as onHistory pushSingle(DriverRideHistory) at accept_ride.dart:1307, leave GPS, the camera and the ticker running. Two details in the finding are overstated. The camera loop in google_driver_camera_port.dart:276-335 is not a constant 60 Hz: it runs 16 ms steps only until the pose settles, then breaks. And the _ThrottledVehicleMap ticker (accept_ride.dart:1458-1467) pushes a marker only when the pose changed. While driving, GPS updates keep both busy on an invisible map. That wastes CPU and battery but breaks nothing functionally.

confirmed.title: Phone sign-in and create-account screens show a US flag by default in the Swedish (SE) market; the selected code is never used
confirmed.description: The sign-in phone screen and both create-account screens set the default country to US/+1 in initState, after first declaring '+92' as the field initialiser. DECISIONS.md P2 fixes the market as SEK/Stockholm, and the rest of the app (documents 'Stockholm trips', SEK money) is Swedish. Every Swedish driver has to change the country before typing a number, and a number typed without changing it would be read as a US number.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A Swedish driver opens 'Sign in with phone' and sees the US flag. They type 0701234567, which would be read as +1 0701234567.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Default to 'SE' / '+46', or to the market country from DriverAccountRules.current.country.

confirmed.title: When browser storage is blocked outright, recovery never resolves, so the driver can never go online and is told about a saved trip that does not exist
confirmed.description: _restoreActiveRideIfNeeded runs CompletionJournal.reconcile() and repo.read(). Both call SharedPreferences.getInstance(), which throws when the browser blocks localStorage (Safari 'Block all cookies', some private modes). Any non-ActiveRideUnreadable error lands in the generic catch, which shows 'The saved trip could not be opened' and leaves _recoveryResolved false. _goOnline refuses while !_recoveryResolved and shows 'Finish or close the saved trip before going online' with 'Open saved trip', which only retries the same failing read. On a first launch with no storage there is no saved trip, yet the driver is blocked from going online for the whole session.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Fresh install opened in a browser with site storage blocked: Home shows 'The saved trip could not be opened'. Every radar tap answers 'Finish or close the saved trip before going online', and 'Open saved trip' fails again. The driver can never go online.
confirmed.evidence: home.dart:519-525 `} catch (_) { _didAttemptActiveRideRestore = false; if(mounted) { _HomeMapSheet(this)._tripProblem(HomeIslandNotices.recoveryFailed, tr.savedTripCouldNotBeOpened); } return; }`; home.dart:890-895 `if(!_recoveryResolved) { _HomeMapSheet(this)._tripProblem(HomeIslandNotices.recoveryPending, tr.finishOrCloseSavedTripBefore, action: tr.openSavedTrip); return; }`; prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:71 `final prefs = await _load();`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Tell 'storage unavailable' apart from 'a saved trip exists but failed'. When the store cannot be opened, nothing can be recovered: resolve recovery (with a warning) instead of blocking going online.

verdicts.reason: PrefsActiveRideRepository.read (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:69-72) lets SharedPreferences.getInstance errors propagate on purpose ('A failing storage plugin is transient: let it propagate for Retry'). home.dart:519-525 catches them, shows savedTripCouldNotBeOpened and leaves _recoveryResolved false, and _goOnline (home.dart:890-895) then refuses to go online. Failing closed is intentional for transient faults. However, when storage is permanently unavailable, the getter itself throws SecurityError: on web, Chrome with site data blocked or Safari with 'Block all cookies'. In that case every retry fails the same way. Startup does not stop the app before Home (main.dart:46-50 catches errors, and the session store is in memory), so the driver reaches Home and is blocked for the whole session, told about a 'saved trip' that does not exist. The path is real but needs a non-default browser setting, hence low.
verdicts.repro: I traced this statically: main.dart startup, which tolerates storage errors -> DriverHome post-frame _restoreActiveRideIfNeeded -> CompletionJournal.reconcile / repo.read -> _load() throws -> generic catch at home.dart:519 -> _goOnline gate at home.dart:890. I found no doc entry covering permanently unavailable storage (LOCAL_DATA.md, DECISIONS.md). Not reproduced in a browser.
verdicts.corrected_title: When browser storage is blocked outright, recovery never resolves, so the driver can never go online and is told about a saved trip that does not exist

verdicts.reason: In home.dart:505-528, _restoreActiveRideIfNeeded calls CompletionJournal.reconcile() and repo.read(), and both load SharedPreferences.getInstance (completion_journal.dart:39, prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:71, which has the comment 'A failing storage plugin is transient: let it propagate for Retry'). On web, shared_preferences_web 2.4.3 reads html.window.localStorage with no guard. That access throws SecurityError when site data is blocked, and shared_preferences resets _completer on error, so every retry throws again. The generic catch at home.dart:519-526 shows savedTripCouldNotBeOpened and leaves _recoveryResolved false. _goOnline (home.dart:896-900) then refuses with 'finish or close saved trip', and its 'Open saved trip' action (home_map_sheet.dart:1286) only reruns the same failing restore. Home is reachable without storage, because the session store is MemoryDriverSessionRepository (main.dart:86) and DriverLanguage.restore is in a try/catch (main.dart:46-47). The driver is therefore locked offline for the whole session, and is told about a saved trip that does not exist.
verdicts.repro: Static trace through home.dart restore, the _goOnline guard, the _tripProblem retry action and the shared_preferences_web/legacy getInstance source in the pub cache (completeError, then _completer = null; no catch around localStorage). Not run, since a browser with storage blocked cannot be simulated in flutter test. The premise is that the browser throws on window.localStorage access when site data is blocked, which is standard Chrome/Firefox/Safari behaviour. No document in docs/ makes the storage-unavailable case intentional.

confirmed.title: A restored trip's waybill shows the time of the last background save as its issue time, not when the trip was accepted
confirmed.description: _waybillFromSnapshot sets issuedAt: snapshot.savedAt. savedAt is re-stamped on every save (GPS every 2 minutes, lifecycle, stage changes), while the snapshot also carries acceptedAt. After any crash or reload the current waybill's Time row (waybill_sheet.dart:74 formatWaybillTime(record.issuedAt)) shows the last-save time instead of when the trip was accepted. AcceptRide's own path uses DateTime.now() at accept time.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A trip accepted at 14:02 is restored after a reload at 14:40 whose last GPS snapshot was at 14:38. The waybill shown to the driver (and to an inspector) says the trip was issued at 14:38.
confirmed.evidence:
home.dart:627 `issuedAt: snapshot.savedAt ?? DateTime.now(),`
active_ride_repository.dart:212 `savedAt: at ?? DateTime.now(),` (stamped on every save)
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use snapshot.acceptedAt (falling back to savedAt) for the restored waybill's issuedAt.

verdicts.reason: _waybillFromSnapshot sets `issuedAt: snapshot.savedAt ?? DateTime.now()` (home.dart:627, now 631). savedAt is re-stamped on every write: prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:156 writes ride.stamped(), and active_ride_repository.dart:212 sets `savedAt: at ?? DateTime.now()`. The original waybill takes issuedAt from DateTime.now() at accept time (accept_ride_trip.dart:191), and the snapshot keeps acceptedAt (active_ride_repository.dart:143, read back by AcceptRide at accept_ride.dart:610). The waybill repository is in memory only, and beginCurrent (waybill.dart:169-173) replaces the record for the same trip. AcceptRide does not rebuild the waybill because current.tripId already matches (accept_ride.dart:621). So after a restore, the Time row (waybill_sheet.dart:74) shows the last background-save time, not the accept time.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the stamped() writers, the beginCurrent and replace semantics, and the accept_ride.dart:621 guard that skips rebuilding the waybill. No test was run.

verdicts.reason: home.dart:631 sets `issuedAt: snapshot.savedAt ?? DateTime.now()`. savedAt is re-stamped on every save (active_ride_repository.dart:220 `savedAt: at ?? DateTime.now()` in stamped()). The snapshot also has acceptedAt (active_ride_repository.dart:145, written from accept_ride_trip.dart:52), but this code does not use it. After a restore, AcceptRide keeps that record: accept_ride.dart:649 only rebuilds it when the tripId differs. waybill_sheet.dart:74 then shows formatWaybillTime(record.issuedAt), which is the time of the last save, not the accept time. On the live path, accept_ride_trip.dart:193 uses DateTime.now() at accept.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand: accept at 14:02, so acceptedAt=14:02. A GPS save at 14:38 stamps savedAt=14:38. Reload at 14:40: _waybillFromSnapshot gives issuedAt=14:38, and AcceptRide.fromPersisted keeps it because the tripId matches. No test was run.

confirmed.title: An Exclusive offer that arrives while the side menu is open is shown under the drawer, keeps its timeout and counts as missed (Q16)
confirmed.description: The drawer is not a route, so opening it does not trigger didPushNext or pause. The Exclusive sheet sits under the drawer's 90%-wide panel and its scrim, where the driver cannot see it or tap Accept, and its _outsideOfferTimeoutTimer keeps running. When it fires, the offer is dismissed with missed: true, which feeds ExclusiveAnswers (Q16), and enough misses in a row take the driver offline. The same offer hidden by a pushed route is paused and, per R13-3, 'ran out while the driver could not see it: not a miss'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An Exclusive offer rises and the driver opens the side menu from the island to check Notifications, reading the menu for 15 s. The offer runs out under the drawer and counts as a missed Exclusive. At the admin's limit, the driver is taken offline.
confirmed.evidence:
home.dart:712-716 `drawer: DriverSideMenu(isOnline: _isOnline, ...)` (no drawer-open handling)
home_offer_radar.dart:275-281 `_outsideOfferTimeoutTimer = Timer(lifetime, () { ... // Ran out without Accept: it counts as missed (Q16). _dismissOutsideRadarOffer(missed: true); });`
home_exclusive.dart:110-112 `// It ran out while the driver could not see it: not a miss.`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pause the Exclusive timeout while the drawer is open (Scaffold.onDrawerChanged), or do not count a timeout as a miss while the drawer covers the offer.

verdicts.corrected_title: An Exclusive offer that arrives while the side menu is open is shown under the drawer, keeps its timeout and counts as missed (Q16)
verdicts.reason: The finding's exact path, opening the menu from the island while the Exclusive is up, is blocked. While _exclusiveOnIsland is true the island is `tucked`, and the menu button sits under IgnorePointer(ignoring: tucked) (home_map_sheet.dart:969-1030). The bug is still reachable two ways. First, an offer can arrive while the drawer is already open: _showOutsideRadarOffer (home_offer_radar.dart:209-248) has no isDrawerOpen or visibility gate, and the drawer is not a route, so _routeVisible stays true and didPushNext never fires. Second, the Scaffold's default edge-swipe can open the drawer over a live offer. In both cases _outsideOfferTimeoutTimer (home_offer_radar.dart:275-281) fires _dismissOutsideRadarOffer(missed:true). A pause behind a hidden tab or route, by contrast, does not count as a miss (home_exclusive.dart:110-112). Effect: a false miss that feeds the auto-offline count.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: the island tuck and IgnorePointer, the show-gate conditions (no drawer check), the only isDrawerOpen use (home_back.dart:53), and the timeout callback. No test was run.

verdicts.corrected_title: An Exclusive offer that rises while the side menu is already open (or the menu is edge-swiped open) counts down under the drawer and is counted as missed
verdicts.reason: The finding's own trigger is blocked: while an Exclusive is on the island, the island's menu button is tucked and wrapped in IgnorePointer (home_map_sheet.dart:1019-1031, `tucked = ... || exclusive != null`). Other paths still reach the failure. _showOutsideRadarOffer (home_offer_radar.dart:228-247) never checks whether the drawer is open, so an offer can arrive while the driver is already reading the menu. Home's Scaffold also leaves the default edge-swipe drawer gesture on, unlike accept_ride.dart:1153 which disables it. The drawer is not a route, so didPushNext/_pauseHomeUpdates (home.dart:174) never runs, and nothing uses onDrawerChanged. The timer at home_offer_radar.dart:275-281 fires _dismissOutsideRadarOffer(missed: true), which reaches _exclusiveMissed (line 320). The hidden-by-route case in home_exclusive.dart:110-112 is treated as not a miss.
verdicts.repro: Traced callers: grep finds no onDrawerChanged/isDrawerOpen handling apart from Back (home_back.dart:53), no drawer check in _showOutsideRadarOffer, and no drawerEnableOpenDragGesture:false on Home. No widget test was run, because Home needs the full dependency graph.

confirmed.title: Matching from the full Radar list leaves Home's copy of the card live: it is marked 'unavailable' at match time and the driven trip briefly reappears as 'Taken' after the trip
confirmed.description: When the driver matches from the Home deck, _openOfferTrip clears all Home offer state in a post-frame callback (_outsideRadarOffer, _radarHomeOffers, _pendingRadarHomeOffers, _hasRideOffers = false). When the driver matches from the embedded RideRequests list (shown when showRideRequests is true), Home only receives onCloseRides and the session callbacks, and nothing clears Home's deck. The sequence is as follows. (1) RideRequests claims the offer. The demo dispatch _removeOffer emits the new offer list to Home's still-live _watchDispatchRadar listener, which calls _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost(offer, unavailable) on Home's copy of the same trip and marks it claimedElsewhere. (2) Within 500 ms AcceptRide is pushed, and didPushNext -> _cancelAllOfferTimers(preserveClaim: true) cancels the 2.8 s cleanup but keeps every list and deadline. (3) After the trip, endTrip sets resumeHomeAfterTrip, and _onDriverSessionChanged only sets showRideRequests = false. didPopNext -> _resumeOfferTimers shows the driven trip as a 'Taken' card for 1.2 s. Other cards have old deadlines and come back already expired (Match faded), and _hasRideOffers stays true.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver is online with three Radar cards on Home, taps the orb to open the full Radar list, and taps Match on the first trip. They drive it and complete it 20 minutes later. Back on Home, the deck still holds the pre-trip cards: the trip just completed is shown as 'Taken', and the rest have Match faded. If that card was the expanded front card, the island also posted 'Trip unavailable' at the moment of the match.
confirmed.evidence:
home.dart:746-766 `RideRequests(... onCloseRides: (hasOffers) { setState(() { showRideRequests = false; _hasRideOffers = hasOffers || _radarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty; }); }, )`. No match callback exists.
home.dart:664-668 `if (_driverSession.consumeResumeHomeAfterTrip()) { setState(() { showRideRequests = false; }); return; }`
Compare home_offer_radar.dart:983-990 (Home-deck accept): `_rebuild(() { _outsideRadarOffer = null; _radarHomeOffers.clear(); _pendingRadarHomeOffers.clear(); _hasRideOffers = false; ...`
home_offer_radar.dart:604-610 `if (!ids.contains(offer.id) && _homeRadarStateFor(offer.id) == available) { _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost(offer, _RadarOfferGone.unavailable); }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give RideRequests an onMatched callback, or clear Home's deck in _onDriverSessionChanged when a trip begins, in the same way as the Home-deck accept path.

verdicts.reason: _openRideOffers (home.dart:979-986) keeps Home's deck while the full list is open. On a list Match, DemoDispatchRepository.claimOffer calls _removeOffer (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:565), which emits to Home's still-live watcher. The watcher calls _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost(unavailable) (home_offer_radar.dart:604-610, 672-707). That sets claimedElsewhere, posts 'Trip unavailable' if the card was the front card, and starts a 2.8 s cleanup. AcceptRide is pushed about 520 ms later, and didPushNext calls _pauseHomeUpdates, which calls _cancelAllOfferTimers(preserveClaim:true) (home.dart:192-203, home_offer_radar.dart:791-818). That cancels the cleanup but keeps the deck, the match states and the deadlines. No RideRequests callback clears the deck; only onCloseRides exists. _onDriverSessionChanged only sets showRideRequests=false (home.dart:664-668). RideCompleted uses popUntil(isFirst) (ride_completed.dart:79), which brings back the same Home State. didPopNext then calls _resumeOfferTimers, which shows the driven trip as 'Taken' for 1.2 s and restarts pick windows against old deadlines, so those cards come back expired. The re-subscribed watcher replays a snapshot (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:505) that marks the others unavailable. The Home-deck accept path clears all of this (home_offer_radar.dart:1005-1007).
verdicts.repro: Static trace of claimOffer, _removeOffer, the Home watcher, didPushNext/didPopNext, and popUntil(isFirst). I tried a widget test that matched from the list, ended the trip and popped back. It would not compile because files were being edited at the same time (home_offer_radar.dart:995 passed scheduledPickupAt, which AcceptRide does not accept). I deleted the test, so this verdict rests on static tracing.

verdicts.corrected_title: Matching from the full Radar list leaves Home's copy of the card live: it is marked 'unavailable' at match time and the driven trip briefly reappears as 'Taken' after the trip
verdicts.reason: RideRequests has no match callback (home.dart:751-771), so Home's deck is not cleared the way the Home-deck accept does it (home_offer_radar.dart ~1000-1007). Home's dispatch listener is still live when the claim removes the offer. It calls _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost(unavailable) (home_offer_radar.dart:604-610), which marks the card claimedElsewhere and, if it was the front card, shows 'Trip unavailable' (line 689). The pause cancels the 2.8 s cleanup (_cancelAllOfferTimers, preserveClaim keeps the states). After the trip, _resumeOfferTimers (762-789) shows the driven trip as Taken for 1.2 s before removing it. The effect is short-lived, not a lasting stale deck: _resumeHomeUpdates calls _scheduleVisibleOffers, then _watchDispatchRadar. The demo stream replays a snapshot on listen (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:504-505), so any card gone from dispatch is resolved and removed after 2.8 s. Cards still in dispatch with a used-up pick window keep Match faded, which matches the D-04 pause rule for any covering route.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand: claim, then the watcher marks the card claimedElsewhere, then the AcceptRide push pauses Home with states kept. On pop: _scheduleVisibleOffers resubscribes and the snapshot resolves gone cards (2.8 s), and _resumeOfferTimers removes the Taken card after 1.2 s. No test was run.

confirmed.title: HorizontalSwipe keeps the drag origin in build-local variables, so a rebuild mid-drag resets start to 0: a leftward drag is swallowed or read as a right swipe
confirmed.description: `start` and `last` are plain locals declared inside `build()` and captured by the three drag closures. GestureDetector re-syncs recognizer callbacks on every rebuild (RawGestureDetectorState.didUpdateWidget -> _syncAll re-initialises onStart/onUpdate/onEnd), so if the widget rebuilds while a finger is down, onUpdate/onEnd run with a fresh `start = 0`. `distance = last - start` then equals the absolute x position of the finger (always > 56 on a phone), so `right` is true regardless of direction. Callers: lib/features/home/presentation/home.dart:2177 wraps the Home sheet inside an AnimatedBuilder (rebuilds on every sheet tick and on every Home setState, e.g. each GPS fix delivered by HomeLocationController._deliverFix) with only onSwipeLeft -> a slow left swipe is swallowed and a fast one is cancelled because both `left` and `right` are true; lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/home_tab_page.dart:42 sets both callbacks, so a rebuild during a leftward drag pops the page with `HomeTabs.previousOf(tab)` (the wrong neighbour). Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (deleted): a 100 px leftward drag with one setState mid-drag printed `left=0 right=1`; the identical drag without the rebuild gave `left=1 right=0`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Rider on Home drags the sheet left to open Payment while a location fix arrives (Home rebuilds ~1 Hz): nothing opens, or on a bottom-bar page the app pops to the previous tab instead of the next one.
confirmed.evidence: lib/shared/widgets/horizontal_swipe.dart:22-23 `double start = 0; double last = 0;` (inside build) ... :26 `onHorizontalDragStart: (d) => start = last = d.globalPosition.dx,` :30 `final distance = last - start;` :32 `final right = velocity > _minVelocity || distance > _minDistance;` ; lib/features/home/presentation/home.dart:2177 `child: HorizontalSwipe(` under `AnimatedBuilder` (~home.dart:2105); lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/home_tab_page.dart:42-45. Test run: `left=0 right=1 ... Expected: <1> Actual: <0>`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make HorizontalSwipe a StatefulWidget (or keep start/last in a ValueNotifier/record owned outside build) so the drag origin survives rebuilds; alternatively use DragStartDetails/DragEndDetails only (d.velocity + accumulated delta from onHorizontalDragUpdate stored in State).

verdicts.corrected_title: HorizontalSwipe keeps the drag origin in build-local variables, so a rebuild mid-drag resets start to 0: a leftward drag is swallowed or read as a right swipe

After a rebuild, the recognizer gets the new closures (start=0), so distance at :30 becomes the finger's absolute x and `right` is true. On Home the swipe sits inside the sheet's AnimatedBuilder (home.dart:2105-2131, 2177), which rebuilds on every sheet-controller tick and on any Home setState. The finding's main trigger is wrong, though: GPS fixes do not setState Home. The onFix handlers (home.dart:382-387) only repaint the puck through _locationCtl, and _refreshPickupLabelIfMoved rebuilds only after 75 m. So the realistic triggers are a sheet still settling, a promotion or saved-places change, or the recenter button toggling mid-drag. HomeTabPage (home_tab_page.dart:40-46) rebuilds only when its route rebuilds the cached page, which is rare. The mechanism is real, but on an edge path.

confirmed.title: Transition builders allocate an undisposed CurvedAnimation on every transition frame, leaking status listeners on the route controller for the route's lifetime and losing curve-direction continuity on mid-animation reversal
confirmed.original_title: Transition builders create a new CurvedAnimation on every frame and never dispose it, so status listeners pile up on long-lived routes
confirmed.description: Each transitionsBuilder (TopToBottomTransition:28, RideStageTransition:61, SwitchTransition:99, _sheetCover:169, _sideCover:193) constructs a CurvedAnimation. In this Flutter SDK the CurvedAnimation constructor always calls parent.addStatusListener(_updateCurveDirection), and only dispose() removes it. _ModalScopeState rebuilds buildTransitions through a ListenableBuilder on Listenable.merge(animation, secondaryAnimation) (flutter routes.dart:1101-1102, 1204-1208), so the builder runs on every tick of the route's own animation and of every route pushed or popped above it. Each tick leaves one more status listener on the route's AnimationController for the route's lifetime. Flutter's own CurvedAnimation docs (animations.dart:410-411) say not to recreate it on every build because it leaks. A fresh CurvedAnimation per frame also drops the curve-direction memory, so a pop that starts mid-push jumps to the reverse curve.
confirmed.failure_scenario: SelectRide or FindingDrivers (RideStageTransition) stays in the stack while many pages and sheets are pushed and popped above it. Each transition frame (about 20 per 360 ms push) adds another dead status listener to that route's controller. Memory grows with every navigation over the route, and every later status change iterates the whole list.
confirmed.evidence: navigation_transition.dart:28 `final curved = CurvedAnimation(parent: animation, curve: MoveraCurves.open, reverseCurve: MoveraCurves.close);` (and :61, :99, :169, :193). /opt/flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/animation/animations.dart:389-392 `CurvedAnimation(...) { ... parent.addStatusListener(_updateCurveDirection); }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use `CurveTween(curve: ...)` chained on the animation, for example `animation.drive(CurveTween(curve: MoveraCurves.open))`, or move the curves into a StatefulWidget that owns and disposes its CurvedAnimation.

verdicts.reason: navigation_transition.dart:28,61,99,169,193 each build a new CurvedAnimation inside transitionsBuilder, and nothing disposes it. The Flutter SDK constructor at animations.dart:389-392 calls parent.addStatusListener(_updateCurveDirection), and only dispose() removes that listener. The parent is route.animation, which is _controller!.view (routes.dart:247-250), meaning the AnimationController itself. _ModalScopeState wraps _buildFlexibleTransitions in a ListenableBuilder on Listenable.merge(animation, secondaryAnimation) (routes.dart:1101-1102, 1204-1208). So every tick of the route's own animation, and every tick of a route pushed or popped above it, adds one more status listener to that controller. The value listeners used by FadeTransition and SlideTransition are removed correctly in didUpdateWidget, so only the status listeners pile up. The direction-memory part is also real: a fresh CurvedAnimation starts with _curveDirection null and takes parent.status (animations.dart:430), so a route that reverses mid-push switches to reverseCurve at once (SwitchTransition, _sideCover, _sheetCover and TopToBottom all set reverseCurve), which makes a visible jump. No guard prevents either effect. Impact is small: the listeners are tiny, they are freed when the route's controller is disposed, and they only grow during animation frames, never while idle.
verdicts.repro: Static trace only, no flutter/dart run (read-only). Read the app file, then /opt/flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/animation/animations.dart:389-435 and /opt/flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/routes.dart:247-250, 328, 1101-1102, 1204-1235. Nothing in DECISIONS.md or ARCHITECTURE.md mentions this pattern.

verdicts.reason: navigation_transition.dart:28, 61, 99, 169 and 193 each build a new CurvedAnimation inside transitionsBuilder, and nothing disposes it. In this SDK the constructor calls parent.addStatusListener(_updateCurveDirection) (animations.dart:389-392), and only dispose() removes that listener. _ModalScopeState wraps _buildFlexibleTransitions in a ListenableBuilder on Listenable.merge(animation, secondaryAnimation) (routes.dart:1101-1102, 1204-1208), so the builder runs again on every tick of the route's own animation and of its secondaryAnimation. No guard exists. The extra listeners live until the route's controller is disposed with the route, so the leak is bounded by how long the route stays in the stack. The cost per tick is small, which is why it rates low. The direction claim also holds: each new instance reads parent.status, so once a pop reverses a push mid-flight, every new CurvedAnimation picks reverseCurve (the reversal case animations.dart:404-407 avoids) and the curve jumps. RideStageTransition has no reverseCurve and a zero reverse duration, so this part does not apply to it. The leak still does.
verdicts.repro: Read-only run: no flutter or dart commands. I traced routes.dart:1098-1250, where the ListenableBuilder over the merged animations calls buildTransitions -> transitionsBuilder on every animation tick, and the CurvedAnimation constructor and its doc warning at animations.dart:389-416. Worked by hand for a 360 ms push at 60 fps: about 21 builder calls, so about 21 status listeners added and never removed, plus about the same again for each push or pop above the route through secondaryAnimation.

confirmed.original_title: Screen readers announce the connection banner twice: an explicit Semantics label is set and the child Texts are still read
confirmed.description: The banner wraps its content in Semantics(liveRegion: true, label: '<title>. <body>'), but the title and body Text widgets below it are not excluded. Neither is a semantics boundary, so their labels merge into the same node and the live-region announcement reads the title and body twice. Text(spec.title ...), Text(spec.subtitle ...)` where spec.semantics = '${L10n.current.rtReconnecting}. ${L10n.current.rtReconnectingBody}'. movera_empty_state.dart:29-31 `Semantics(container: true, label: '$title. $message', child: ... Text(title) ... Text(message)`

verdicts.reason: realtime_connection_banner.dart:34-38 sets Semantics(liveRegion: true, label: spec.semantics) with no container and no excludeSemantics. Its descendants (DecoratedBox, Padding, Row, Column, two Text widgets) contain no semantics boundary and no ExcludeSemantics. The Texts' labels therefore merge into the same semantics node as the explicit label 'title. body', and the node reads that label followed by title and body again. The banner is used on ride-critical screens: waiting_for_driver.dart:1518, finding_drivers.dart:903 and ride_completed.dart:331. MoveraEmptyState is at lib/shared/design_system/movera_empty_state.dart:29-31, not under widgets/ as the finding says. Its Semantics(container: true, label: '$title. $message') sits above Text(title) and Text(message) with no exclusion. Its SingleChildScrollView may put the Texts in a child scroll node instead of merging them, but the screen reader still reads the title and message twice. The decision documents do not record any accessibility choice that would make this intentional.

confirmed.title: screenHorizPadding is computed once (lazy top-level), so after a web/desktop window resize side gutters stay at the first scale (e.g. 16 px vs 20 px) while ResSize-scaled layout rescales
confirmed.description: `double screenHorizPadding = ScreenUtil().setWidth(16);` is evaluated on first read and never again. lib/app/screen_scale.dart:45-47 deliberately rebuilds ScreenUtilInit with new bounds on a window resize so widths rescale, but every consumer of this global (lib/features/messages/presentation/chat.dart:107-314, lib/features/home/presentation/home.dart:1990-2002, lib/features/ride_complete/presentation/trip_detail.dart:28, driver_info.dart:40) keeps the padding computed for the first window size while the rest of the layout (ResSize.w, which is a getter) rescales. If the first read happens before ScreenUtilInit has run (any host that builds one of those widgets directly) the value is derived from ScreenUtil's uninitialised defaults for the rest of the process.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Desktop/web rider resizes the browser window from phone width to 1280 px: everything scaled through ResSize.w grows to the 1.25 bound, but the side gutters in Chat, Home's location card and Trip detail stay at the old 16 x (old scale) value, leaving misaligned edges.
confirmed.evidence: lib/shared/widgets/responsive_size.dart:3 `double screenHorizPadding = ScreenUtil().setWidth(16);` ; lib/app/screen_scale.dart:45-47 `// The root View provides this MediaQuery, so a window resize rebuilds // ScreenUtil with new bounds.` ; home.dart:1990 `left: screenHorizPadding,`

verdicts.reason: responsive_size.dart:3 is a top-level variable with an initializer, so Dart evaluates it lazily once and caches it. MoveraScreenUtilInit (screen_scale.dart:44-53) re-inits ScreenUtil with new bounds on resize, so ResSize.setWidth changes while screenHorizPadding stays fixed. Consumers mix the two: home.dart:1990-2002 uses screenHorizPadding next to ResSize.h, and chat.dart, trip_detail.dart, driver_info.dart and others (18 uses) use it too. On mobile the orientation is locked (bootstrap.dart:69), so this is limited to resizing on web or desktop. The finding's second claim is wrong. Reading the variable before ScreenUtilInit throws a LateError, it does not compute and keep default values, and Dart re-runs a lazy initializer that threw on the next read. So the value does not stay at 'uninitialised defaults'.

confirmed.title: The camera's coasted chase point reaches the car marker through onFrame, so between fixes the car icon moves in a straight line along the camera bearing (up to 21° off course) and overshoots by up to 22 m when the driver brakes
confirmed.description: Each loop frame aims at _at(goal, _coasted(goal)). _coasted extrapolates up to 1.1 s / 22 m along goal.bearing, which is the smoothed camera heading blended up to 21° toward the route ahead, not the car's course. _move calls onFrame(logical) whenever _trackCar is true (target within 25 m of goal.target, which a 22 m coast always is). AcceptRide's onFrame calls _vehicle.snapTo(position.target, …) every frame while following, which overrides the route-snapped _vehicle.moveTo(camera.vehiclePoint). The car marker is therefore drawn at the damped, coasted camera target. DriverCameraPose.speedMetersPerSecond is documented as 'Used only to coast the chase point between GPS fixes. Never the car marker.'
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver brakes hard for a light, or makes a turn while the camera bearing lags. Between fixes, the car icon keeps sliding up to 22 m along the old or look-ahead bearing, beyond the stop line or off the road at the corner, then rubber-bands back when the next fix arrives.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Publish the un-coasted vehicle point (goal.target, or the policy's vehiclePoint) to onFrame, and keep the coasted target only for the camera.

verdicts.reason: google_driver_camera_port.dart:281 aims each frame at `_at(goal, _coasted(goal))`. _coasted (:118-139) moves the point up to 1.1 s / 22 m along goal.bearing. During guidance that bearing is the course blended up to 21 degrees toward the road ahead and then smoothed (driver_camera_controller.dart:276-310), so it is not the road. _move publishes that logical frame through onFrame whenever _trackCar holds (:217-219, :184-193: follow durations of 450 ms are 600 ms or less, and the target is within 25 m). accept_ride.dart:1257-1260 then calls `_vehicle.snapTo(position.target, ...)` every frame while following in guidance. That replaces the route-snapped moveTo(camera.vehiclePoint) from accept_ride_trip.dart:696. The car marker therefore coasts off the snapped polyline between fixes, which contradicts 'Never the car marker' (driver_camera_controller.dart:33) and the 'on-route snapped' car in docs/driver-camera-architecture.md. The effect is visual: a few metres of overshoot or off-road drift, corrected at the next fix.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: the coast path (:118-139, :281), the onFrame publish in _move (:217-219), the _trackCar guard (:184-193), the snapTo consumer (accept_ride.dart:1257-1260), and how the policy builds bearing and the coast flag (driver_camera_controller.dart:276-337). No guard leaves the coast offset out of the marker.

verdicts.corrected_title: The camera's coasted chase point reaches the car marker through onFrame, so between fixes the car icon moves in a straight line along the camera bearing (up to 21° off course) and overshoots by up to 22 m when the driver brakes
verdicts.reason: During following guidance, the policy sets coast: onRoute && speed>=1 (driver_camera_controller.dart:337). On-route, the pose bearing is course + clamp(roadDelta,±30)*0.7, then smoothed (lines 279-317), so it can sit up to 21° off the car's course. In the port, _coasted moves the target up to min(v*1.1 s, 22 m) along goal.bearing (google_driver_camera_port.dart:117-139). The loop aims at _at(goal, _coasted(goal)) (line 281). For a 450 ms pose, _trackCar returns true because the frame is under 25 m from goal.target (lines 183-193). _move then calls onFrame(logical) (line 218). accept_ride.dart:1290-1293 calls _vehicle.snapTo(position.target, ...) on every frame while following in guidance. snapTo stops the animator (live_vehicle_animator.dart:47-48), so the coasted, damped camera target replaces the route-snapped moveTo(vehiclePoint) (accept_ride_trip.dart:702). This contradicts the doc comment at driver_camera_controller.dart:33 ('Never the car marker'). No guard drops the coast for the marker.
verdicts.repro: Worked by hand. Last fix at 15 m/s, then the driver brakes to a stop: the coast runs 15*1.1 = 16.5 m past the real position before the next fix pulls it back. Bearing 21° off the road direction with a 22 m cap: lateral offset 22*sin(21°) ≈ 7.9 m off the polyline at a curve. On the next fix, _goalAt resets, the coast drops to 0 and the damped approach pulls the car back. No test run, because the effect depends on real DateTime between fixes.

confirmed.title: The recenter/locate flight clock advances only by the 16 ms sleep. Time spent awaiting moveCamera is never counted, so on native platforms the 1 s flight runs longer by about (moveCamera latency / 16 ms) × 100%
confirmed.description: In the flight branch, flown advances by dt, and dt is measured from a stamp taken after `await _move(...)` returns, around the 16 ms _sleep only. The time spent awaiting controller.moveCamera (a platform-channel round trip on Android/iOS) is never added. The flight therefore lasts flightDuration × (frame time / sleep time) instead of the documented 1 s ('runs on the clock … start to rest'). The #325 measurement was taken on a release web build, where moveCamera resolves almost at once. frame() and tiltTo() in the same class use absolute elapsed time from start, so the inconsistency is only here and in the damped loop (line 333).
confirmed.failure_scenario: On a phone where each moveCamera await takes about 10-16 ms, a Recenter/Locate tap flies for about 1.6-2 s instead of 1 s, which brings back part of the slow glide #325 removed.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Measure dt from the previous frame's stamp, taken before _move, or compute the flight progress from a start timestamp like frame() does.

verdicts.reason: In the flight branch, google_driver_camera_port.dart:312-317 takes `stamp` after `await _move(...)` returns and only times the 16 ms _sleep. Time spent awaiting controller.moveCamera inside _move (:207-209) is never added to `flown`. The flight therefore lasts flightDuration multiplied by (frame time / sleep time), longer than the documented 1 s ('runs on the clock... start to rest', :102-106). The damped branch (:333-337) has the same omission, but its time constants are approximate there. How much longer depends on the platform-channel round trip (a few ms on a typical Android or iOS device, more under load), so the slowdown is real but usually small.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the _run loop (:259-338): dt is set only from `DateTime.now().difference(stamp)` where stamp comes after _move, and _move awaits moveCamera.

verdicts.corrected_title: The recenter/locate flight clock advances only by the 16 ms sleep. Time spent awaiting moveCamera is never counted, so on native platforms the 1 s flight runs longer by about (moveCamera latency / 16 ms) × 100%
verdicts.reason: In the flight branch, flown += dt (google_driver_camera_port.dart:296). dt is measured from a stamp taken after `await _move(...)` returns, and it covers only `_sleep(16ms)` (lines 308-313). The moveCamera round trip awaited inside _move (line 208) is left out. frame() measures from a fixed start (lines 437-440), so this is inconsistent within the same class. The landing frame count stays about 1e6/dt ≈ 60, but each frame takes 16 + m ms of wall time. The finding's figure of 1.6-2 s needs m of about 10-16 ms. That happens only when the platform-channel reply waits for a busy main thread or vsync. A typical Pigeon round trip of 1-5 ms gives about 1.06-1.3 s.
verdicts.repro: Worked by hand. In the existing test (test/widget/driver_camera_port_test.dart:100 'a locate flight lands in about 1 s'), the fake moveCamera returns at once and DateTime.now() is not faked, so dt = max(16000, ~0) = 16000 and the test counts frames, not wall time. It cannot see this. Wall time = 60 frames × (16 ms + m): m=0 gives 0.96 s, m=5 gives 1.26 s, m=12 gives 1.68 s.

confirmed.title: Radar sweep wedge never fades: SweepGradient with a negative startAngle clamps the whole arc to the end colour
confirmed.description: RadarWedgePainter draws the arc from -tail to 0 rad with SweepGradient(startAngle: -tail, endAngle: 0). Both Skia and Impeller compute a pixel's sweep parameter from its angle in [0, 2π), then remap it with (t - start) / (end - start). Pixels in the drawn arc (-60°..0°) have t in [5/6, 1), which remaps to [6, 7) and is clamped by the default TileMode.clamp to stop 1.0 (white at 0.6 alpha). The documented 'light wedge that fades behind its leading edge' therefore renders as a solid 60° white fan with a hard trailing edge. Worked by hand: a pixel at -30° has t_raw = 11/12, so (11/12 + 1/6) * 6 = 6.5, which clamps to 1.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver goes online. Home's radar orb shows a uniform bright 60° slice rotating around the ring instead of a soft sweep that fades out behind its leading edge.
confirmed.evidence: movera_radar_orb.dart:487-499 `canvas.translate(center.dx, center.dy); canvas.rotate(lead); ... ..shader = SweepGradient(startAngle: -tail, endAngle: 0, colors: [Colors.white.withValues(alpha: 0), Colors.white.withValues(alpha: 0.6)]).createShader(rect); canvas.drawArc(rect, -tail, tail, true, paint);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use startAngle: 2*math.pi - tail and endAngle: 2*math.pi (the same position as -tail..0 in the gradient's [0, 2π) domain), or draw from 0 to tail and rotate by lead - tail.

verdicts.reason: RadarWedgePainter (movera_radar_orb.dart:487-499) uses SweepGradient(startAngle: -tail, endAngle: 0) and draws the arc from -tail to 0. The sweep parameter is computed in [0, 2π), so every pixel of the arc maps past stop 1 and is clamped to the end colour. The documented fading tail (:462-463) renders as a uniform 0.6-alpha 60° fan with a hard trailing edge.

Output: 'deg -2 alpha 153', 'deg -10 alpha 153', 'deg -30 alpha 153', 'deg -50 alpha 153', 'deg -58 alpha 153', 'deg 10 alpha 0'; All tests passed. So alpha is a constant 153 (0.6) with no fade. The file was deleted afterwards.

verdicts.reason: RadarWedgePainter (movera_radar_orb.dart:487-499) uses SweepGradient(startAngle: -pi/3, endAngle: 0). The engine computes a pixel's sweep t in [0,1), so a pixel at -30 deg gets t = 11/12. The remap (t+1/6)*6 = 6.5 is then clamped to stop 1.0, so the whole 60 deg arc is painted the end colour (white at 0.6 alpha) with no fade. The code comment 'so the gradient never wraps' gets this backwards.

Output: 'deg=-2 r=153, deg=-10 r=153, deg=-30 r=153, deg=-50 r=153, deg=-58 r=153'. 153 = 0.6*255 at every angle, so the wedge is uniform and does not fade. Test deleted afterwards.

confirmed.title: core -> features/di import guard only matches single-quoted package: imports, so a relative import from lib/core bypasses it (no current breach)
confirmed.description: The architecture guard extracts directives with `^\s*(?:import|export)\s+'([^']+)'` and then only flags URIs that start with `package:movera_rider/features/` or equal `package:movera_rider/app/di.dart`. A file under lib/core that writes `import '../../features/x/y.dart';`, `import "package:movera_rider/features/x/y.dart";`, or a `part`/deferred/conditional form reaches features without tripping the guard. Relative imports are already in use elsewhere in lib (e.g. lib/features/home/presentation/home_map_style.dart:1, lib/shared/widgets/custom_google_map.dart:12,14), so the style is not forbidden by lint. No current violation exists, so this is a gap in the gate, not a live breach.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A developer adds `import '../../features/booking/application/booking_coordinator.dart';` to a file in lib/core; `flutter test test/architecture/guard_test.dart` still passes and the documented 'core is feature-agnostic' rule in ARCHITECTURE.md is silently broken.
confirmed.evidence:
test/architecture/guard_test.dart:188-206:
```dart
    final directive = RegExp(
      r"^\s*(?:import|export)\s+'([^']+)'",
      multiLine: true,
    );
    ...
    for (final file in dartUnder('lib/core')) {
      for (final uri in importsOf(file.readAsStringSync())) {
        expect(
          uri.startsWith('package:movera_rider/features/') ||
              uri == 'package:movera_rider/app/di.dart',
          isFalse,
```
confirmed.suggested_fix: Match both quote styles (`['"]([^'"]+)['"]`), resolve relative URIs against the file's directory before checking, and also reject any resolved path under lib/features or lib/app/di.dart; optionally add `always_use_package_imports` to analysis_options to make relative imports impossible.

confirmed.title: lock_test idempotency-key tests are vacuous: failNext fails the quote POST, so only one ride POST is ever made and no keys are compared (coverage exists elsewhere)
confirmed.description: Both 'failed finding retry reuses the same logical booking key' (lines 105-126) and 'changed finding intent receives a new booking key' (lines 128-161) set `RecordingMockClient()..failNext = true` and expect the first `submitFinding` to throw. But `BookingCoordinator.submitFinding` first calls `_resolveQuoteBinding` (POST /api/v1/quotes) before posting /api/v1/rides, and `InProcessMockClient.failNext` returns 500 to the next request of any path. So the 500 hits the quote request; the rides endpoint is never reached on the failed attempt, and `RecordingMockClient.send` (which only records POST /api/v1/rides, lines 19-26) records nothing. The second submit records exactly one key. Both tests then assert `hasLength(1)` and `isNotNull`, which is satisfied regardless of whether the coordinator reuses, rotates, or never sends an idempotency key. Neither test compares a key across attempts, so the 'reuse' and 'new key' semantics are untested. Reproduced with a throwaway test (test/_audit_lock_vacuous_test.dart, since deleted) recording request paths: after the failed submit, `rideKeys` was empty and exactly one `POST /api/v1/quotes` had been made; the second submit produced one ride key; `flutter test` output: `00:00 +1: All tests passed!`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A regression that generates a fresh Idempotency-Key on every retry (so a network blip double-books a ride), or that drops the header entirely on retry, passes both tests unchanged, while the test names claim the opposite is guaranteed.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make the failure hit the rides endpoint (e.g. a mock that fails only `POST /api/v1/rides` once, or pre-fetch the quote and pass the quote binding), then assert `idempotencyKeys` has length 2 and `keys[0] == keys[1]` for the retry case and `keys[0] != keys[1]` for the changed-intent case.

The code comment acknowledges the data flow but the public deployment is not a closed test environment, and no privacy notice covers it.
refuted.failure_scenario: A stranger opens the public demo link and grants location: their 6-decimal coordinates are sent to OpenStreetMap's public service on Home load (`detectCurrent` -> `geocoding.reverse`) and again on each pickup-label refresh.

verdicts.reason: This is an explicit, documented design choice rather than a defect. app_geocoding.dart:30-35 records that the Nominatim fallback 'sends the rider's exact coordinates to a third party, so staging and production rely on the backend's reverse geocoder alone', and that only demo, dev and test builds (allowsMockTransport, di.dart:187-190) turn it on. The public Pages build is the demo flavor, whose in-process transport has no geocoder (in_process_mock_client.dart:329-332), so the fallback is the deliberate way the demo shows street names. The web/index.html:220-222 comment the finding cites applies to the JavaScript shell ('from this shell'), not to the Flutter geocoding path. The same demo page already sends the visitor's position to Google Maps for tiles and camera. A privacy-policy wording gap on a mock demo is a product decision, and no runtime defect follows from it.

refuted.title: Editing a reservation duplicates its preferences note and cannot remove them
refuted.description: When editing, `ScheduleRide.initState` copies the stored note into the session (`_session.captureNote(editing.note!.trim())`, schedule_ride.dart:88) and `openScheduledCategorySelector` passes it to `SelectRide(note: …)` (449). SelectRide treats `widget.note` as the rider's free-text extra and prepends it to the freshly selected chips: `note: _driverNote(widget.note)` with `_driverNote` = `[extra, ..._notes.selected].join(' · ')` (select_ride.dart:1170, 1204-1210), while `_notes` starts at `RideNotes.empty` (select_ride.dart:285) so the stored chips are not pre-selected. Result: the stored note (e.g. `Bags`) is always re-sent; choosing bags again yields `Bags · Bags`; de-selecting cannot remove anything. On top, `ScheduledRideBooking.confirm` sends `note: note` and the patch cannot clear a note because `Reservation.copyWith` does `note: note ?? this.note` (reservation.dart:353, local_reservation_repository.dart:207).
