refuted.evidence:
schedule_ride.dart:88 `if (editing.hasPreferences) _session.captureNote(editing.note!.trim());`
scheduled_category_gate.dart:449 `note: session.note.trim().isEmpty ? null : session.note.trim(),`
select_ride.dart:1170 `note: _driverNote(widget.note),`
select_ride.dart:1204-1210 `final parts = <String>[ if (extra != null && extra.trim().isNotEmpty) extra.trim(), ..._notes.selected ]; if (parts.isEmpty) return extra; return parts.join(' · ');`
reservation.dart:353 `note: note ?? this.note,`
refuted.suggested_fix: When editing, parse the stored note into `RideNotes` (chips) and keep only the free-text remainder as `extra`; add a `clearNote` flag to `ReservationPatch`/`copyWith` so an empty selection removes the note.

verdicts.reason: The duplication path cannot happen. openScheduledCategorySelector always passes pickupAlreadyConfirmed: true (scheduled_category_gate.dart:63), and SelectRide sets _pickupConfirmed = widget.pickupAlreadyConfirmed (select_ride.dart:317). The scheduled branch therefore skips the Set pickup sheet (`if (!_pickupConfirmed)`, select_ride.dart:1127), so `_notes = _notes.withBagLevel(...)` at :1141 never runs. The only other write to _notes (:1490) is in the Book now path, which this locked scheduled flow does not use. _notes stays RideNotes.empty, and _driverNote(widget.note) (:1170, :1204-1210) returns the stored note unchanged, with no 'Bags · Bags'. The edit flow has no preferences control at all, so keeping the existing note is consistent behaviour, and the copyWith `note ?? this.note` limit is never hit because nothing sends a cleared note.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: gate :44-72, then SelectRide :281/:317/:1109-1170 and every _notes assignment (:285, :1141, :1490). The only SelectRide caller with editingReservationId is the gate (grep).

refuted.title: Concurrent start(): the failure path cancels the other, still-active recording
refuted.description: `start()` guards with `isRecording` (401), which is only true after `_active` is set at the end (426), after two awaits (permission 407, store init 413-415). Two taps in that window both pass the guard; `RideCheckController.toggleRecording` (ride_check_controller.dart:582-613) and the Safety Kit `_toggleAudio` have no busy flag. If the second `_recorder.start` throws (native recorders refuse to start while recording), the catch calls `_recorder.cancel()` on the shared `AudioRecorder`, which cancels and discards the first recording's file, while the first call then sets `_active` and the card keeps showing a running recording whose later `stop()` yields no file (`NO_AUDIO`).
refuted.failure_scenario: Rider double-taps "Record audio" on the Ride check card: the mic appears to be recording, but the only recording was cancelled; Stop reports no audio file.
refuted.evidence:
safety_audio_service.dart:401 `if (isRecording) {` … :416-425 `try { await _recorder.start(recording.id); } catch (_) { await _recorder.cancel(); await _store.deleteAudio(recording); throw ...`
safety_audio_service.dart:426-428 `_active = recording.copyWith(createdAt: DateTime.now().toUtc());`
refuted.suggested_fix: Set an in-flight flag at the top of `start()` (reject or await a second call) and only cancel the recorder when this call's own start had begun.

verdicts.reason: The failure path needs a second _recorder.start to throw while the first recording is running. The installed native plugins never do that. record_android-2.2.0 RecorderController.start (RecorderController.kt:39-45) finalizes a live session and starts a new take ('start() doubles as next take'). record_ios-2.1.1 Recorder.start (Recorder.swift:34-35) calls stop() first. So on a double tap the catch at safety_audio_service.dart:62-64 that cancels the recorder is not reached. The web build uses UnsupportedSafetyRecorder (safety_recorder.dart and safety_recorder_stub.dart) and throws UNSUPPORTED at line 39 before any await. A double tap can still leave the first take's file orphaned, but that is a different and minor effect, not the claimed cancelled recording with NO_AUDIO on Stop.
verdicts.repro: Traced SafetyAudioService.start (safety_audio_service.dart:35-74) -> NativeSafetyRecorder.start -> record 7.1.1 AudioRecorder.start (_safeCall semaphore) -> the native start implementations in ~/.pub-cache record_android-2.2.0 and record_ios-2.1.1. Neither throws on an already-running recorder.

refuted.title: CODE-14 'machine-specific generated files are not tracked' silently passes when git is unavailable
refuted.description: The test runs `git ls-files -ci --exclude-standard` and `return`s (passing) when the exit code is non-zero. That covers a tarball checkout, but it also covers a missing `git` binary, a sandboxed CI runner, or a `safe.directory` ownership refusal, in which case the guard is skipped without any signal.
refuted.failure_scenario: CI runner lacks git in PATH or refuses the directory as 'dubious ownership'; the test reports green while ignored-but-tracked files (the thing CODE-14 guards) go undetected.
refuted.suggested_fix: Only short-circuit when `Directory('.git').existsSync()` is false; otherwise fail with the git stderr so a broken runner is visible.

verdicts.reason: A missing git binary does not pass silently. Process.runSync('git', ...) at audit_fix_cleanup_test.dart:96 throws ProcessException, so the test fails. The `return` at :101 only covers git running and exiting non-zero, as in the tarball case the comment names. A 'dubious ownership' refusal is speculative for this repo: the CI workflows that run tests check out with actions/checkout@v4 (for example batch7-phase85-final-certification.yml:24,51,77), and that action sets safe.directory. No realistic runner path makes this guard pass silently.
verdicts.repro: Read audit_fix_cleanup_test.dart:95-108 and the .github/workflows checkout steps. Dart's Process.runSync throws ProcessException when the executable is not found; it does not return an exit code.

refuted.title: `_confirmCancel` has no busy guard across its first await, so a double tap opens two stacked non-dismissible cancel sheets
refuted.description: `_confirmCancel` returns early only on `_leaving`, which is set at line 820, after two awaits: `await _cancelFeeNote()` (which itself awaits `RouteChangeController.storedRide()` -> SharedPreferences and `AppScope.instance.riderConfig.forZone(zone.id)`, lines 770-779) and `await showCancelRideSheet(...)`. The same handler is wired to the round cancel button (`MoveraIconButton.round(onPressed: _confirmCancel)` line 1498), to the in-trip panel's 'End trip here' (`onCancel: _confirmCancel` line 1890) and to the PopScope back handling (line 1450). `MoveraIconButton` is a plain `InkWell` with no debounce. Two taps during the fee lookup therefore run two `_confirmCancel` bodies; each calls `showCancelRideSheet`, which opens `MoveraSheet.show` with `swipeDismissible: false, barrierDismissible: false` (cancel_ride_sheet.dart:24-27) and only records `SheetCoordinator.instance.open(RideSheet.cancel)` (a plain field write, sheet_coordinator.dart:27). The second sheet is pushed on top of the first. If the rider taps 'Keep ride' on the top sheet, the first sheet is still there and must be dismissed again; if the rider confirms on the top sheet, the first body's continuation resumes only after the screen navigated away (`if (!mounted) return;`), and a second server cancel is avoided only because `PendingCancelStore.enqueue` reuses the existing entry's idempotency key.
refuted.failure_scenario: On the Waiting-for-driver screen the rider taps the X (cancel) button twice quickly while the fee note is being looked up. Two 'Cancel ride?' sheets stack; tapping 'Keep ride' closes only the top one and the rider sees the same sheet again and has to tap 'Keep ride' a second time (the sheet cannot be swiped or tapped away).
refuted.evidence: waiting_for_driver.dart:802-806 `Future<void> _confirmCancel() async { if (_leaving) return; final feeNote = await _cancelFeeNote(); if (!mounted || _leaving) return; final outcome = await showCancelRideSheet(` | :820 `_leaving = true;` | :1498 `onPressed: _confirmCancel,` | :1890 `onCancel: _confirmCancel,` | cancel_ride_sheet.dart:23-27 `SheetCoordinator.instance.open(RideSheet.cancel); final confirmed = await MoveraSheet.show<bool>( context: context, swipeDismissible: false, barrierDismissible: false,` | sheet_coordinator.dart:27 `void open(RideSheet sheet) => current = sheet;`
refuted.suggested_fix: Add a `_cancelSheetOpen`/`_cancelBusy` flag set synchronously at the top of `_confirmCancel` and cleared in a `finally`, or check `SheetCoordinator.instance.current == RideSheet.cancel` before opening; disable the cancel buttons while the flag is set.

verdicts.reason: The only window for a second _confirmCancel is the await on _cancelFeeNote (waiting_for_driver.dart:804), and every await in it resolves immediately from cached local data. RouteChangeController.storedRide is RideSnapshotStore.read (route_change_controller.dart:135), which reads PreferencesStore.load and so SharedPreferences.getInstance; that instance is cached after first use, and Waiting has used it already. riderConfig is SeedRiderConfigRepository (di.dart:345), whose forZone is `async => seedFor(zoneId)` with no I/O (rider_app_config.dart:486). The continuation therefore runs in the same microtask drain and pushes the non-dismissible sheet before the next frame. From then on the modal barrier takes any further tap on the X or 'End trip here' button. Two human taps cannot both land inside that sub-frame window, so two stacked sheets are not a realistic outcome.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _cancelFeeNote's awaits (storedRide, then RideSnapshotStore._readStored, then PreferencesStore.load and SharedPreferences.getInstance; riderConfig.forZone resolves to the seed with no I/O) and of showCancelRideSheet opening a barrier route (finding_driver/presentation/cancel_ride_sheet.dart:23-27). Not run as a test: a zero-delay double tester.tap with no pump between would not reflect real tap timing.

refuted.title: ZoneClock.toUtc resolves a wall-clock time inside the spring-forward gap with the winter offset, contrary to its own contract
refuted.description: The doc comment (lines 70-72) says that in the hour that does not exist the summer offset is used. The implementation computes `guess = asUtc - offsetAt(asUtc)` and then returns `asUtc - offsetAt(guess)`. For 2026-03-29 02:30 Europe/Stockholm: asUtc=02:30Z -> offsetAt(02:30Z) = +2h (already CEST) -> guess = 00:30Z -> offsetAt(00:30Z) = +1h (still CET) -> result 01:30Z, i.e. winter offset. Verified by throwaway test: toUtc(DateTime(2026,3,29,2,30),'Europe/Stockholm') == 2026-03-29T01:30:00Z, expected 00:30Z. The UI pickers currently let the rider choose any wall-clock minute, so a non-existent time can be selected and the sent `scheduledPickupAt` is one hour later than the doc-specified mapping (and lands on 03:30 local).
refuted.failure_scenario: Rider books a book-later ride for 02:30 on 29 Mar 2026 (Stockholm). The wire time becomes 01:30Z = 03:30 CEST instead of 00:30Z = 02:30 CET-projected/summer mapping; the countdown and the server-side pickup differ by an hour from what the doc promises.
refuted.suggested_fix: After computing the candidate, check whether localOf(candidate) reproduces `wall`; if not (gap), use `asUtc.subtract(offsetAt(timeZone, asUtc))` (the summer offset). Also have the date-time picker reject or snap times inside the gap.

verdicts.reason: The arithmetic is right: for 2026-03-29 02:30 Stockholm, toUtc returns 01:30Z (zone_clock.dart:84-85), not the 00:30Z its doc comment (71-73) promises. But 02:30 does not exist that night, so any mapping is a choice. The code shifts it forward to 03:30 CEST, which is the standard resolution and the same one Dart's own local constructor uses (probe: DateTime(2026,3,29,2,30) becomes 03:30 under TZ=Europe/Stockholm). The summer-offset mapping the doc describes would book 01:30 CET, an hour before the slot the rider picked, which is arguably worse. The doc comment is wrong; the behaviour is not, and riders are not harmed. Fix the comment.
verdicts.repro: Same throwaway probe under TZ=Europe/Stockholm: 'stockholm gap toUtc 02:30 => 2026-03-29 01:30:00.000Z'. The local constructor showed the same forward shift (2:30 → 3:30). Traced the only production caller, scheduled_rides_controller.dart:64 via PickupSchedule.toUtc.

refuted.title: `restoreOnce` marks itself restored before the async load finishes, so concurrent first requests answer with un-restored defaults (fresh random PIN, empty contacts)
refuted.description: `restoreOnce()` sets `_restored = true` (line 49) and then awaits `PreferencesStore.load()` (line 52). There is no shared in-flight future. `InProcessMockClient.send` awaits `safety.restoreOnce()` per request (line 1208), so a second safety request that starts while the first one's load is pending returns immediately and `handle()` runs against the constructor defaults: `_newPin()` (a random 4-digit PIN), empty `contacts`, default `preferences`/`rideCheck`. Those defaults are what the client caches and shows; the restore then silently overwrites state afterwards (and a mutation made in that window is overwritten by `preferences.addAll(...)`, line 63). Reproduced with saved `movera_safety_demo_v1` (contact `ec_saved`, PIN 4321) and three concurrent GETs: `AUDIT C: first=[{id: ec_saved,...}] second=[] pin={... pin: 7214 ...}`.
refuted.failure_scenario: Demo build with `persistSafety: true` (the app's own transport). `WaitingForDriver.initState` calls `SafetyController.shared.load()` while the Safety hub (or ride-check policy fetch) also touches `/api/v1/safety/*` at the same moment on a fresh launch: the second chain gets no contacts and a PIN that differs from the one persisted/shown before the reload; a preference toggled in that window is lost when the restore lands.
refuted.evidence:
safety_mock_api.dart:47-52 `Future<void> restoreOnce() async { if (_restored) return; _restored = true; final generation = _generation; try { final prefs = await PreferencesStore.load();`
in_process_mock_client.dart:1208-1214 `if (persistSafety) await safety.restoreOnce(); final safetyHit = safety.handle(...)`
refuted.suggested_fix: Keep the restore as a memoised `Future<void>? _restoring` and have every caller `await` that same future (reset it in `reset()`), instead of a boolean set before the load completes.

verdicts.reason: The boolean-before-await pattern at safety_mock_api.dart:47-53 is real in isolation, but no real caller can reach it. (1) The restore window is only microtasks long. By the time any safety HTTP request is sent, SafetyStore.load (safety_store.dart:50-51) has already awaited `_local.load()`, which calls PreferencesStore.load() (safety_data_sources.dart:139/194). So SharedPreferences.getInstance() has already resolved, and the awaits inside restoreOnce finish within a couple of microtasks. InProcessMockClient.send has latency=Duration.zero (in_process_mock_client.dart:264) and no other await before line 1208. (2) Within one load(), the four safety GETs run strictly one after another (safety_store.dart:56-59), so the second request always starts after the first one's restore has finished. (3) Every path that calls load() is driven by a gesture or a navigation: WaitingForDriver.initState (waiting_for_driver.dart:245), RideSafetyKitSheet.initState (ride_safety_kit.dart:138, opened by a tap) and SafetyHub.initState (safety_hub.dart:32, opened by a tap or the deep link). None of them starts in the same microtask burst as another safety request. The finding's repro fires three GETs synchronously against the mock directly, which the app never does.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of every /api/v1/safety caller (safety_data_sources.dart) and every SafetyController.load / SafetyStore._ensure entry point. Confirmed that send() has no awaits before restoreOnce at zero latency and that SafetyStore.load warms SharedPreferences before its first remote call. Settling it the other way would need a real code path that issues two safety requests in the same synchronous frame on a cold process; I found none.

refuted.title: Scheduled reservation estimatedDropoffAt is pickup time + driver ETA, not pickup + trip duration
refuted.description: `confirm` computes `final dropoff = when.add(Duration(minutes: ride.etaMin));` and `ScheduledRideCheckout.draftFrom` does the same (scheduled_ride_checkout.dart:32). `etaMin` is the driver's minutes to the pickup (ride_selection.dart 'arrival'/'etaMin', 6-15 min), while the screen the rider just confirmed shows 'Arrive HH:MM' as `scheduled.add(Duration(minutes: _tripMinutes()))` (select_ride.dart:836-840) and Set pickup likewise uses `tripMinutes`. The stored `estimatedDropoffAt` is therefore a few minutes after pickup for every scheduled ride, is written to the reservation JSON (`reservation.dart:370-371`) and the local repository, and disagrees with the time shown at booking. No rider screen reads it today (`ReservationFormat.dropoffAt` has no callers), which keeps this low.
refuted.failure_scenario: Rider schedules a 25-minute trip for 07:00; Select Ride shows 'Pickup 07:00 · Arrive 07:25'; the reservation persists estimatedDropoffAt = 07:08 (etaMin 8).
refuted.evidence: scheduled_ride_booking.dart:53 `final dropoff = when.add(Duration(minutes: ride.etaMin));`; scheduled_ride_checkout.dart:32 `estimatedDropoffAt: when.add(Duration(minutes: ride.etaMin)),`; select_ride.dart:838-840 `if (scheduled != null) { return clockTime(scheduled.add(Duration(minutes: _tripMinutes()))); }`
refuted.suggested_fix: Pass the trip minutes (the same `estimatedTripMinutes` SelectRide shows) into `confirm`/`draftFrom` and use `when.add(Duration(minutes: tripMinutes))`.

verdicts.reason: The arithmetic is wrong as described: scheduled_ride_booking.dart:53 and reservations/application/scheduled_ride_checkout.dart:32 add `ride.etaMin`, the driver's minutes to pickup (ride_catalog_controller.dart:206-214), where select_ride.dart:839 adds `_tripMinutes()`. But nothing ever reads the value. A grep for estimatedDropoffAt/dropoffAt finds only the model (reservation.dart:144-422), the controller pass-through (reservation_controller.dart:422-436) and the local repository (local_reservation_repository.dart:168,198,139 jsonEncode to local storage). ReservationFormat.dropoffAt (reservation_format.dart:151) has no callers, the reservation is not sent to any backend, and contracts/ has no dropoff-time field. No screen, conflict check or wire format is affected, so this is a dormant wrong field with no user-visible effect.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: grepped lib/, test/ and contracts/ for estimatedDropoffAt, dropoffAt and etaMin. Only writers and the local JSON serializer exist, and there are no readers.

refuted.title: RouteTimeMarker caches one rendered PNG BitmapDescriptor per distinct label forever; labels change every minute so the cache grows for the app's lifetime
refuted.description: `_cache` is a static map keyed by `'$pickup|$label'` with no eviction. Callers render time-bearing labels: lib/features/ride_selection/presentation/select_ride.dart:869-872 `RouteTimeMarker.createIcon(pickup: false, label: context.l10n.arriveBy(_arrivalFor(ride)))` for every ride category (the arrival time advances each minute while Select Ride is open or re-opened), and lib/features/finding_driver/presentation/finding_drivers.dart:487-493 with ETA labels. Each entry holds a 3x-scale PNG (`imagePixelRatio: scale`, canvas ~ (bubbleW+24)x(bubbleH+~70) px) that is never released. Over a long session (several bookings, Select Ride left open) this is tens of MB of retained image bytes; the other marker caches are bounded by boolean/int keys, this one is not.
refuted.failure_scenario: Rider keeps the app open across a day of bookings: memory climbs by one PNG descriptor per (category x minute) label; on low-memory web/iOS PWA this contributes to tab eviction.
refuted.evidence: lib/shared/widgets/movera_map_markers.dart:235-236 `static final Map<String, Future<BitmapDescriptor>> _cache = <String, Future<BitmapDescriptor>>{};` :245 `return _cache.putIfAbsent('$pickup|$label', () async {` ... :317-320 `return BitmapDescriptor.bytes(data.buffer.asUint8List(), imagePixelRatio: scale);` (no removal anywhere); select_ride.dart:870-872 `RouteTimeMarker.createIcon(pickup: false, label: context.l10n.arriveBy(_arrivalFor(ride)),`
refuted.suggested_fix: Bound the cache (small LRU, e.g. keep the last ~16 labels) or key only on the current screen's labels and clear on dispose.

verdicts.reason: The cache has no eviction (movera_map_markers.dart:235-245), but the growth is bounded and small, not 'tens of MB'. Keys are clock-minute or ETA-minute labels, and callers (select_ride.dart:856-881, waiting_for_driver.dart:2244-2256, finding_drivers.dart:487-493) skip re-rendering via _timePinKey, so at most one new entry is added per minute of an open map screen. Each entry is a compressed PNG of about 10-13 KB. A ride (a few minutes on Select Ride plus a 20-40 minute trip) adds roughly 40 entries, about 0.5 MB, and the hard ceiling is about 1440 arrive labels per locale (around 14 MB) after a full day of continuous tracking. That is not a realistic memory-pressure path.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_r94_test.dart (since deleted) rendered RouteTimeMarker.createIcon and read BytesMapBitmap.byteData.length. It printed `dest 9985 pickup 13177` per entry, and all tests passed.

refuted.title: 'duplicate assignment keeps last sequence' and 'stale out-of-order sequence' tests cannot fail on the behaviour they name
refuted.description: Line 33 asserts `seq.where((s) => s == 2).length >= 1` after emitting sequence 2 twice: it passes whether the duplicate is deduplicated, delivered twice, or reordered, so the dedup/last-sequence behaviour in the name is not verified. Lines 51-60 emit `driverAssigned` (seq 5) then `findingDriver` (seq 1) and assert only `contains(driverAssigned)`, which is trivially true because it was just emitted; whether the stale seq-1 event is dropped or applied (the actual ordering contract) is never asserted.
refuted.failure_scenario: MockRideRealtime (or a future replacement behind the same seam) starts delivering duplicate or stale-sequence events to subscribers; both tests still pass and downstream RideSession tests are the only line of defence.
refuted.suggested_fix: Assert the exact delivered list (e.g. `expect(seq, [2])` or `[2, 2]` depending on the intended contract, and `expect(statuses, [driverAssigned])` or `[driverAssigned, findingDriver]`) so the ordering/dedup contract is pinned.

verdicts.reason: What the finding says about the assertions is accurate. test/ride/realtime_test.dart:32 passes whether the event arrives once or twice, and :58 only checks the event that was just emitted. But the 'contract' the finding says goes unpinned is not one MockRideRealtime has. MockRideRealtime.emit (lib/core/realtime/mock_ride_realtime.dart:308-321) is a deliberate pass-through: it sets `_sequence = sequence ?? _sequence + 1` and never dedupes or reorders. Delivering duplicate and stale events is how the transport is meant to behave, so the failure scenario ('the mock starts delivering duplicate or stale-sequence events') describes current, intended behaviour, not a regression a test would need to catch. Contract v0.3.0 section 4 puts ordering and dedup in the consumer's shared gate: api_ride_realtime.dart:132-134 ('the shared gate decides'), the FindingDriverController RealtimeGate (finding_driver_controller.dart:142-145), and RideSession ordering by `version ?? sequence` (ride_session.dart:27). That consumer-side behaviour has its own direct tests, for example ride_session_reconcile_test.dart:54 'same version duplicate is ignored'. The second test's name, 'stale out-of-order sequence can be emitted', also says plainly that the transport lets stale events through. The only real issue is cosmetic: the first test's name, 'duplicate assignment keeps last sequence', suggests dedup that the transport was never meant to do. No product behaviour is wrong and no regression goes unguarded.
verdicts.repro: Static trace only, no test run. I read test/ride/realtime_test.dart:25-60 and MockRideRealtime.emit/_emit (mock_ride_realtime.dart:308-377), which only drops events when there is no ride, the ride is disposed or cancelled, or the status is terminal. I checked where the ordering gate lives (api_ride_realtime.dart:125-160, finding_driver_controller.dart:142-145, ride_session.dart:27) and the consumer-side dedup test (test/booking/ride_session_reconcile_test.dart:54-70).

refuted.title: `POST /rides` answers `wallet_amount_invalid` as `invalid_request` with HTTP 409 instead of 400
refuted.description: `_validateQuoteBinding` returns `'wallet_amount_invalid'` for a wallet part that is negative, exceeds the fare, or is non-zero with `useWalletFirst == false` (lines 2247-2255). The route handler sets `status = 409` for every validation result and only swaps the code to `invalid_request` for this one (lines 598-606). CONTRACT.md §1: 'Validation ... are 400 invalid_request'; the mock's own `_error` doc says the code is the contract code. The response is therefore an `invalid_request` body with a conflict status, so a client branching on `statusCode == 409` (the quote-conflict re-quote path) treats a wallet validation error as a quote conflict.
refuted.failure_scenario: Demo flavor: a booking whose `walletAmountMinor` exceeds the quote total (e.g. after the quote was re-priced lower) gets HTTP 409 + `invalid_request`; the client's 409 handling re-quotes or reports a conflict rather than an invalid wallet amount.
refuted.evidence: in_process_mock_client.dart:598-606 `final validation = _validateQuoteBinding(body); if (validation != null) { status = 409; payload = _error( validation == 'wallet_amount_invalid' ? 'invalid_request' : 'conflict', requestId, reason: validation, message: 'Booking quote is missing, expired or does not match.', );`
refuted.suggested_fix: Use `status = validation == 'wallet_amount_invalid' ? 400 : 409` (and a wallet-specific message).

verdicts.reason: No real caller can reach it. The only client that sends a wallet part, BookingCoordinator._prepareFinding, clamps it before sending: `useWalletFirst ? walletAmountMinor.clamp(0, binding.totalMinor) : 0` (lib/features/booking/application/booking_coordinator.dart:384-386), and binding.totalMinor is the same quote total that _validateQuoteBinding compares against. So none of the three wallet_amount_invalid conditions at in_process_mock_client.dart:2247-2254 (negative, above the total, non-zero with useWalletFirst off) can happen. The reservation path requestBooking (booking_coordinator.dart:135-190) sends no walletAmountMinor at all, which defaults to 0 and passes. The finding's 're-priced lower' scenario never gets to the wallet check: a fare that differs from the server total returns quote_price_mismatch first (in_process_mock_client.dart:2240-2241). The client also does not branch on 409 for POST /rides. _isRefusal treats any non-retryable 4xx the same way (booking_coordinator.dart:83-90). What is left is a 409-vs-400 mismatch with CONTRACT.md §1 in a response nothing ever triggers.
verdicts.repro: Static trace. Read _validateQuoteBinding (mock :2225-2257) and the POST /rides handler (:597-611). The only two app callers of POST /api/v1/rides are booking_coordinator.dart:220 (reservation, no wallet field) and :642 (live booking, wallet clamped at :384-386). Read the error handling at :69-90 and :420-425.

refuted.title: Fingerprinted bootstrap/main names plus full replacement of old files break reloads for up to 10 minutes after every deploy (stale cached index.html 404s)
refuted.description: The fingerprint step renames `main.dart.js` and `flutter_bootstrap.js` to SHA-suffixed names and rewrites index.html to reference them; the Pages upload contains only the new names, so the previous SHA's files disappear. GitHub Pages serves every file, index.html included, with `Cache-Control: max-age=600`, and the `<meta http-equiv="Cache-Control" content="no-store">` in index.html (line 21) is ignored by browsers for HTTP caching. A rider whose browser cached index.html in the 10 minutes before a deploy and who reloads (or whose installed PWA relaunches) gets the old index.html, which requests `flutter_bootstrap.<oldsha>.js` -> 404, so Flutter never boots; the HTML boot screen's 20 s fallback (index.html:144) then clears to an empty page. This directly undercuts the documented R-web promise that a live ride must survive a browser reload. Without fingerprinting a stale index.html would still have loaded the new main.dart.js.
refuted.failure_scenario: Rider opens the demo at 10:00, a push to main deploys at 10:03, rider's tab crashes/reloads at 10:05: index.html comes from cache, bootstrap 404s, 'Movera' boot bar runs 20 s then a blank page; their active ride snapshot is intact but nothing restores until the cache expires.
refuted.evidence: .github/workflows/publish-web-live.yml:92-105 `versioned_bootstrap = f'flutter_bootstrap.{version}.js' ... main.rename(build / versioned_main); bootstrap.rename(build / versioned_bootstrap); index_text.replace('flutter_bootstrap.js', versioned_bootstrap)`; lines 116-118 copy only the fresh build/web; web/index.html:21 `<meta http-equiv="Cache-Control" content="no-store">`; web/index.html:144 `setTimeout(clear, 20000);`.
refuted.suggested_fix: Keep the previous deploy's fingerprinted main/bootstrap files in the Pages artifact (e.g. carry over `main.*.dart.js`/`flutter_bootstrap.*.js` from the current web-live branch), or use query-string versioning (`flutter_bootstrap.js?v=sha`) like rider_map_camera.js so a stale index.html still resolves.

verdicts.reason: The scenario as described does not fail. (1) A reload revalidates the top-level document in Chrome, Firefox and Safari, so the browser gets the new index.html, which points to the new fingerprinted files that exist in the artifact (publish-web-live.yml:92-111, 118). Max-age freshness only applies to subresources on reload. (2) On a fresh navigation within 10 minutes (PWA relaunch, link), the cached old index.html asks for flutter_bootstrap.<old>.js and main.<old>.dart.js. Those were fetched seconds after that index.html, so their max-age=600 window ends at the same time or later, and they come from the same HTTP cache. The old build therefore boots consistently. A 404 needs an unusual sequence: an in-window reload that refreshes only index.html's freshness, then a deploy, then a non-reload navigation in the leftover window. Cache eviction of the multi-MB main.<old>.dart.js would also do it. That is a narrow hardening gap (keeping the previous fingerprinted files would close it), not the main-path breakage claimed.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of publish-web-live.yml:80-139 (fingerprint, cp of build/web only, upload-pages-artifact) and web/index.html:21,144-149, checked against browser HTTP-cache semantics: reload revalidates the main resource, and subresources share the freshness window. Not reproducible locally, since it needs the GitHub Pages CDN.

refuted.title: Fingerprinting step versions rider_map_camera.js but leaves movera_ride_snapshot_wipe.js cache-busted only by name
refuted.description: The step's own comment says 'Pages caches plain names: version the map gesture layer too', and it appends `?v=<sha>` to `rider_map_camera.js`. `web/index.html` line 147 also loads `movera_ride_snapshot_wipe.js` by plain name, and it is not versioned, so a changed wipe script can be served stale from the Pages/CDN cache after a deploy while the fingerprinted main bundle is fresh.
refuted.failure_scenario: A fix to movera_ride_snapshot_wipe.js is deployed; browsers that cached the previous copy (Pages serves plain-named assets with long cache headers) keep executing the old wipe logic alongside the new main.<sha>.dart.js until the cache expires.
refuted.evidence:
.github/workflows/publish-web-live.yml:108-112:
```python
          # Pages caches plain names: version the map gesture layer too.
          index_text = index_text.replace(
              'src="rider_map_camera.js"',
              f'src="rider_map_camera.js?v={version}"',
          )
```
web/index.html:147-149:
```html
  <script src="movera_ride_snapshot_wipe.js"></script>
  <script src="rider_map_camera.js"></script>
```
refuted.suggested_fix: Apply the same `?v={version}` replacement to `src="movera_ride_snapshot_wipe.js"` (and any other plain-named script in web/index.html) in the fingerprint step.

verdicts.reason: This is speculative and harmless. movera_ride_snapshot_wipe.js is a stable helper that exposes only window.moveraIsInstalledApp and window.moveraWipeRideSnapshotStorage (web/movera_ride_snapshot_wipe.js:1-6, ~86-87). Its header says it is for QA clear only. No Dart-side API is coupled to a particular version of it. The last change to it is the old merge 48075fb. GitHub Pages sends max-age=600 (not 'long cache headers'), so any staleness is capped at 10 minutes. Many other plain-named assets have the same property (assets/*, manifest.json, firebase-messaging-sw.js). The `?v=` treatment at publish-web-live.yml:106-110 targets the map gesture layer, which works in lockstep with the Dart map code. No current or realistic failure follows from leaving the wipe script unversioned.
verdicts.repro: Read web/index.html:147-149, the full wipe script, publish-web-live.yml:106-111, and grepped lib/ and .github for callers of the wipe globals. None in Dart. git log on the file shows no recent changes.

refuted.title: reportSearchSnapshot is not gated, so release web builds publish the rider's pickup address and coordinates on window.moveraSearchSnapshotJson
refuted.description: Unlike `reportRideCheckSnapshot` (line 202, gated by moveraQaHooksEnabled) and the matching hooks, `reportSearchSnapshot` writes unconditionally. FindingDriverController._reportQa (lib/features/finding_driver/application/finding_driver_controller.dart:1670-1671) calls it on every tick with `qaSnapshot()` which includes `'pickupAddress'`, `'pickupLat'`, `'pickupLng'` (lines 1665-1667) and the rideId. ARCHITECTURE.md:20 says QA window.movera* hooks are gated. Any third-party script on the page (the Google Maps JS SDK is loaded on the same page) or a browser extension can read it in production.
refuted.failure_scenario: Production web rider searches for a driver: `window.moveraSearchSnapshotJson` on the public page contains their pickup street address and precise coordinates for the duration of the search.
refuted.evidence: lib/core/debug/web_qa_hooks_web.dart:83-85 `void reportSearchSnapshot(String json) { globalContext.setProperty('moveraSearchSnapshotJson'.toJS, json.toJS); }` (no `if (!moveraQaHooksEnabled) return;`, compare :202-205); finding_driver_controller.dart:1665-1667 `'pickupAddress': _snapshot?.pickupAddress, 'pickupLat': _snapshot?.pickupLat, 'pickupLng': _snapshot?.pickupLng,`
refuted.suggested_fix: Add `if (!moveraQaHooksEnabled) return;` to reportSearchSnapshot (and reportSafetySnapshot for consistency), as reportRideCheckSnapshot already does.

verdicts.reason: The global really is set in release builds (web_qa_hooks_web.dart:83-85 has no gate, and finding_driver_controller.dart:1670-1671 calls it on every update). But it exposes nothing new. During the same search, FindingDriverController persists the snapshot to localStorage key `flutter.movera_active_ride` (finding_driver_controller.dart:588/735/861/983 -> RideSnapshotStore.save; ride_snapshot_store.dart:198-201 serializes pickupAddress, pickupLat and pickupLng). Any same-origin page script or extension that could read window.moveraSearchSnapshotJson can read that localStorage entry just as easily, and the documented design relies on it for reload survival (ARCHITECTURE.md:9,31,48). The Maps JS SDK receives pickup coordinates anyway to render the map. ARCHITECTURE.md:20's gating rule covers the mutation-capable window.movera* hooks. Several read-only reporters are ungated the same way: reportRestoreSurface, reportMapOwner, reportSafetySnapshot.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: _reportQa -> reportSearchSnapshot (ungated), compared with the _store.save calls in finding_driver_controller.dart and RideSnapshotStore.toJson (ride_snapshot_store.dart:198-201, key at :321-322). The same fields are already readable from localStorage on the same origin.

verdicts.reason: reportSearchSnapshot is ungated (web_qa_hooks_web.dart:83-85), but it exposes nothing new. The same pickupAddress, pickupLat and pickupLng come from FindingDriverController._snapshot, a RideSnapshot (finding_driver_controller.dart:149). That snapshot is already stored as plain JSON in localStorage under 'flutter.movera_active_ride' (ride_snapshot_store.dart:193-201 toJson, :105/:394 prefs.setString). Per DECISIONS.md R-web it deliberately survives reloads for the whole live ride. Any page script, the Maps SDK or an extension in the same origin can read localStorage as easily as a window global, and for longer. The data is the rider's own pickup in their own tab, not someone else's. Other read-only reporters (moveraRestoreSurface, moveraMapOwner, moveraSafetySnapshotJson) are also ungated. QA_HOOKS.md lists only the mutation hooks as gated, plus the ride-check snapshot. The privacy failure scenario therefore adds no real exposure.
verdicts.repro: Traced the call path: _reportQa (finding_driver_controller.dart:1670-1671) -> reportSearchSnapshot(jsonEncode(qaSnapshot())), where qaSnapshot includes _snapshot?.pickupAddress, pickupLat and pickupLng (:1665-1667). Then confirmed RideSnapshotStore.save writes the same fields with prefs.setString(key 'movera_active_ride'), which is 'flutter.movera_active_ride' in web localStorage (ride_snapshot_store.dart:32-33, 105, 193-201). No runtime test was needed.

refuted.title: update() coalesces different patches on the same reservation and silently drops the second
refuted.description: `update` returns the in-flight future for any concurrent call with the same reservationId regardless of patch content (186-195). The callers are the rider's edit confirm (scheduled_ride_booking.dart:62-78) and the simulated trip step writer `_driveMockTrip` (401-410), which calls `update(id, ReservationPatch(status: to))` and returns `true` even if its patch was dropped. `canEdit` is true for `driverEnRoute`/`driverArrived` (reservation_status.dart:34), so in demo builds an edit confirmed while a trip step is in flight either loses the status step (trip then stalls: next step finds `current.status != from` and returns false) or loses the edit.
refuted.failure_scenario: Demo build: driver en route, rider confirms an edit at the moment the simulated "arrived" step writes; one of the two writes is dropped without error — either the simulated trip never progresses or the edit vanishes though Review changes said it was applied.
refuted.evidence:
reservation_controller.dart:186-195 `final pending = _pendingUpdateByReservationId[reservationId]; if (pending != null) return pending;`
reservation_controller.dart:408-409 `await update(id, ReservationPatch(status: to)); return true;`
refuted.suggested_fix: Key the in-flight map by (reservationId, patch identity) or queue updates through the repository's `_oneAtATime` instead of coalescing distinct patches.

verdicts.reason: The coalescing code at reservation_controller.dart:186-195 does return the in-flight future for any patch on the same reservation. But the in-flight window is a single local commit: LocalReservationRepository.updateReservation (local_reservation_repository.dart:189-216) is one queued _oneAtATime step plus one prefs setString (:136-143), which takes milliseconds. Both writers have to land in that window. One is the rider's confirm after the ReviewChangesPage push (scheduled_ride_checkout.dart:78-96 -> scheduled_ride_booking.dart:62). The other is a mock step that fires from a 20s/8s/18s Timer (mock_reservation_dispatch.dart:26-28, 134-139), and that dispatch exists only in mock-transport builds (di.dart:165-168). The 'trip stalls' branch also heals itself. If the status step is dropped, the next step returns false (reservation_controller.dart:403-406), but HomeReservationChrono ticks every 30s (home_reservation_chrono.dart:64-75). Each tick runs startLiveIfDue, which calls _driveMockTrip again for any revealsDriver ride (reservation_controller.dart:338-343), and driveTrip re-arms from the stored status because _steps no longer holds the id (mock_reservation_dispatch.dart:117,135). The only lasting effect would be a lost edit, and that needs a millisecond-exact collision in a demo-only simulation. This is a speculative race, not a realistic path.
verdicts.repro: Traced update() -> _updateNow -> LocalReservationRepository.updateReservation/_oneAtATime/_commit. Traced both callers: the edit confirm via ScheduledRideCheckout.run -> ScheduledRideBooking.confirm, and _driveMockTrip -> MockReservationDispatch.driveTrip timers. Checked the 30s chrono tick that re-arms the trip, and that mock dispatch is built only when environment.allowsMockTransport is set. No test run.

refuted.title: Not a bug in practice: memory fallback asymmetry in SecureTokenStore has no reachable trigger (only a theoretical lock-during-refresh race)
refuted.description: `save` catches a failure of the active store (Keystore/Keychain on phones, sessionStorage on web) and writes the tokens to `_memory` instead, but `readAccess`/`readRefresh` only fall back to `_memory` when the active store THROWS. A store whose write fails while its read answers normally (returns null) means the rider who just signed in reads back no session: `AuthRepository.hasSession()` is false and the restore gate shows Sign in again. Conversely `clear()` swallows a delete failure and clears only `_memory`, so after sign-out the real tokens remain and the next cold start (`_defaultHasSession`) goes straight to Home as the previous rider, defeating `UserDataWipe`. Reproduced with a throwaway test against `SecureTokenStore(override: ...)` using a store that throws on save/clear but reads normally: `flutter test` output `00:00 +2: All tests passed!` where the assertions were `expect(access, isNull)` after `save(access:'A1')` and `expect(await store.readAccess(), 'A1')` after `clear()` (log line `[movera:error] auth.token.secure_clear_failed {}`).
refuted.failure_scenario: Android device whose EncryptedSharedPreferences write fails (plugin throws) but reads return null: OTP verify succeeds, tokens 'saved', app immediately shows Sign in again on the next screen; or Keychain delete fails on iOS: rider signs out, data is wiped, relaunch opens Home signed in with the old tokens.
refuted.evidence: lib/core/auth/secure_token_store.dart:53-58 `try { await _active.save(...); } catch (...) { AppLog.error(...); await _memory.save(access: access, refresh: refresh); }`; lines 62-69 `try { return await _active.readAccess(); } catch (...) { return _memory.readAccess(); }`; lines 82-89 `try { await _active.clear(); } catch (...) { await _memory.clear(); }`.
refuted.suggested_fix: Track a `_memoryFallbackActive` flag set when a save falls back and read from memory while it is set; on clear failure rethrow (or retry) so sign-out does not report success while tokens persist.

verdicts.reason: The code asymmetry is real. save() falls back to _memory when _active.save throws (secure_token_store.dart:52-58), but readAccess/readRefresh read _memory only when _active.read throws (:61-78). clear() swallows a delete failure and clears only _memory (:81-88). No existing test covers the fallback; test/auth/token_store_test.dart has only a memory round-trip. What is missing is a demonstrated real trigger. On web, _SessionStorageTokenStore (web_session_token_store_web.dart) calls setItem/removeItem. removeItem does not throw, so the clear half cannot happen on web. setItem throws only on QuotaExceeded or legacy Safari private mode. On native, the common failure modes (Keystore key loss on Android, Keychain errSecInteractionNotAllowed on a locked iOS device) make reads throw as well, so the memory fallback is used and the 'signs in then immediately signed out' scenario does not appear. Two things would settle it. One is evidence that a target plugin or platform throws on write or delete while reads succeed. The plausible case is iOS: ApiClient refreshes tokens while the device is locked (api_client.dart:208), the Keychain write fails, and after unlock reads succeed and return the old, possibly rotated, tokens instead of the new ones in memory. The other is a browser case where sessionStorage setItem throws but getItem works.
verdicts.repro: Read secure_token_store.dart, web_session_token_store_web.dart and token consumers (auth_repository.dart:122-131, api_client.dart:79,181-208, bootstrap.dart:35-36, ride_restore_coordinator.dart:172-179). The finding's own throwaway test shows the in-code asymmetry with a contrived store. I did not reproduce a real platform that throws on write while reading normally.

verdicts.reason: The fallback is incoherent in code: secure_token_store.dart:53-58 writes to _memory, but :62-79 read _memory only when the active store throws, and :82-88 clear only _memory on failure. However, neither failure scenario has a realistic trigger. On web the active store is _SessionStorageTokenStore (web_session_token_store_web.dart). removeItem never throws, so 'clear fails but read still returns tokens' cannot happen there. setItem throws only when quota is exhausted, and these tokens are tiny; the only other sessionStorage writer is a small search-live flag (web_search_interrupted_web.dart). When sessionStorage is blocked, the `web.window.sessionStorage` getter throws on reads too, so the memory fallback is used for both and works. On iOS and Android, Keychain/Keystore failures (locked device, keystore corruption) hit read, write and delete alike, so reads also throw and fall back to the memory copy. The finding's 'write throws but read returns null' and 'delete throws but read returns old tokens' store has no real counterpart. A narrower variant exists: after a transient symmetric failure, the recovered store serves the older tokens. It needs a background token refresh at the moment of a Keychain lock. The app has only the remote-notification background mode (ios/Runner/Info.plist:48-51), so this is speculative.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test (deleted) using SecureTokenStore(override: Flaky) with a store that fails symmetrically. save(A0) ok; fail=true; save(A1) went to memory; 'during failure read=A1' (fallback works when reads also fail); fail=false; 'after recovery read=A0 refresh=R0'. Result '+2: All tests passed!'. The asymmetric store the finding assumes was not reproduced on any real backend, after reading the web and native store implementations.

verdicts.corrected_title: Not a bug in practice: memory fallback asymmetry in SecureTokenStore has no reachable trigger (only a theoretical lock-during-refresh race)
verdicts.reason:
The asymmetry in the code is real. secure_token_store.dart:53-58 writes to _memory when the save fails, but :62-79 read _memory only when the active read throws, and :82-88 clear only _memory. Neither failure scenario in the finding can happen on a store this app actually uses.

1. The two user-driven entry points run in the foreground on an unlocked device: the save after OTP verify or provider sign-in (auth_repository.dart:122) and the clear on sign-out (auth_repository.dart:141).

2. In flutter_secure_storage 9.2.4, a write cannot fail while a read succeeds.
   - Android, EncryptedSharedPreferences: write and delete are putString/remove plus apply() (FlutterSecureStorage.java:106-126). They use the same keyset as getString, so a Keystore fault breaks reads as well, and resetOnError is off by default.
   - iOS: write first runs containsKey (FlutterSecureStorage.swift:177). That is the same SecItemCopyMatching call that read uses, so whatever blocks the write also blocks the read.
   - Web: removeItem never throws, and setItem throws only when the quota is exceeded. The tokens are tiny, and the only other sessionStorage writer is the small search-live flag.

3. The only background caller of save is the token refresh at api_client.dart:208. It runs only after readAccess has returned a non-null token (api_client.dart:79,89) and readRefresh a non-null one (:185-186). So a store that is already locked or failing never reaches save. I ran this: with a store that is locked from the start, the 401 path made refreshPosts=0 and saveCalls=0.

4. One variant is reachable in a test: the device locks after the read succeeds but before the save. The new tokens then go to memory, and after unlock the reads return the stale A0/R0. My race test confirmed this. On iOS it would need the app still running about 10s after lock, when WhenUnlocked keys are evicted. With only the remote-notification background mode (Info.plist:48-51) and a background push handler that does nothing (firebase_push_service.dart:28-40), iOS suspends the app before that. If a push wakes the app while locked, the read comes first and returns null, so no refresh runs. Even in the race, the cost is one rejected refresh and then Sign in. A cold start would have lost the memory copy anyway.

Nothing in DECISIONS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md or QA_HOOKS.md covers this. The finding's failure_scenario ("ESP write fails while reads return null"; "Keychain delete fails on sign-out") has no real counterpart.
verdicts.repro:
I wrote a throwaway test, /home/user/movera-rider-app/test/_audit_rider11_decider_test.dart, and deleted it after the run. It used SecureTokenStore(override: LockableStore), where LockableStore is the worst case for a locked iPhone: when locked, save and clear throw and reads return null without throwing. ApiClient was built on an http MockClient: /auth/refresh returned A1/R1, and other requests returned 200 only for "Bearer A1", otherwise 401.

- Test 1 locked the store first, then called api.get. Output: "locked-first: refreshPosts=0 saveCalls=0". A locked store never reaches save.
- Test 2 flipped locked=true inside the refresh response. Output: "[movera:error] auth.token.secure_save_failed" (stack: SecureTokenStore.save secure_token_store.dart:54 <- ApiClient._performRefresh api_client.dart:208), then "race: res={ok: true} afterUnlock access=A0 refresh=R0". The stale-token variant exists only through this race.

Run result: "00:00 +2: All tests passed!"

I also read the plugin's native code in /root/.pub-cache/hosted/pub.dev/flutter_secure_storage-9.2.4: ios/Classes/FlutterSecureStorage.swift:118-222 and android/.../FlutterSecureStorage.java:72-126 plus FlutterSecureStoragePlugin.java:126-195. I read /home/user/movera-rider-app/lib/core/auth/web_session_token_store_web.dart as well.

refuted.title: Unawaited `_store.save(...)` in the search-delayed path drops storage errors as unhandled async exceptions
refuted.description: `_evaluatePhase` fires `_store.save(_ordered(snapshot).copyWith(status: RideStatus.searchDelayed, ...))` without awaiting or catching. `RideSnapshotStore.save` (ride_snapshot_store.dart:355-404) awaits `PreferencesStore.load()` and `prefs.setString(key, encoded)` with no try/catch of its own, so a platform-channel/storage failure (quota, private-mode web storage, plugin error) becomes an unhandled asynchronous error raised from a periodic timer tick rather than being logged like the other `AppLog.warning` paths in this controller.
refuted.failure_scenario: On a device/browser where SharedPreferences writes fail (e.g. Safari private mode storage quota), the search passes the 'delayed' threshold; the timer tick's unawaited save throws and the error reaches the zone's unhandled-error handler (crash report / console noise) while the search itself continues.
refuted.evidence: finding_driver_controller.dart:586-594 `final snapshot = _snapshot; if (snapshot != null) { _store.save( _ordered(snapshot).copyWith( status: RideStatus.searchDelayed, savedAt: DateTime.now(), ), ); }` | ride_snapshot_store.dart:391-394 `final prefs = await PreferencesStore.load(); if (token != epoch) return; await prefs.setString(key, encoded);` (no try/catch)
refuted.suggested_fix: Wrap in `unawaited(_store.save(...).catchError((e) => AppLog.warning('ride.finding.snapshot_save_failed', ...)))` or await it inside the existing try path.

verdicts.reason: The effect is harmless and the trigger is speculative. The unawaited save (finding_driver_controller.dart:587-593) can only fail if SharedPreferences.setString throws. That does not happen in practice on the targets: modern Safari private mode has working localStorage, and the 5 MB quota cannot be hit by one small snapshot. If it did throw, the error would not crash anything. bootstrap.dart:134 runs the app inside runZonedGuarded and bootstrap.dart:102 installs PlatformDispatcher.onError, so the error is logged and the search continues, which is what the finding itself says. The awaited saves in the same controller (735, 861, 983) are not try/caught either. The codebase does not treat storage failure as a handled case, so this is at most a log-severity choice, not a behaviour defect.
verdicts.repro: Traced FindingDriverRepository.save -> RideSnapshotStore.save (ride_snapshot_store.dart:355-404) -> PreferencesStore.setString (preferences_store.dart:14), and the zone/platform error handlers in lib/app/bootstrap.dart:91-134. No test run.

refuted.title: A server quote in another currency clears prices but not the old-currency quotes, so discounts and promo prices mix currencies
refuted.description: The `currency` setter (65-69) only does `offeredPrices.clear()`; `authoritativeQuotes`, `quoteExpiresAt` and `quoteIds` keep the quotes priced in the previous currency. `adoptQuote` (457) switches the currency whenever the server prices in another zone's currency (documented as allowed: 'a quote the server prices in another currency moves it'). After that, for every other category `_discountFor` (select_ride.dart:2172-2176) still returns the old-currency discount, so the tile shows a strikethrough `_kr(price + discount)` (2320-2331) that adds the SEK catalog list price to a SEK discount and formats the sum in the new currency, while the main price correctly shows '…'. `_promotionPrices` (2140-2155) likewise hands the old-currency quote amounts to the promotion sheet under `currency: _selection.currency` (2167).
refuted.failure_scenario: Pickup geocoded in Sweden, server answers the first quote in EUR: the other tiles show '…' as price but a struck-through '259 €' discount line, and the promotion sheet lists SEK amounts labelled €.
refuted.evidence: ride_selection_controller.dart:65-69 `set currency(String value) { if (value == _currency) return; _currency = value; offeredPrices.clear(); }`; ride_selection_controller.dart:457 `currency = quote.currency;`; select_ride.dart:2172-2176 `final quote = _selection.authoritativeQuotes[ride.id]; if (quote == null || quote.discountMinor <= 0) return 0; return Money(quote.discountMinor, quote.currency).major;`; select_ride.dart:2320-2324 `if (discount > 0) _fitPrice(context, Text(_kr(price + discount),`
refuted.suggested_fix: Clear `authoritativeQuotes`, `quoteIds`, `quoteExpiresAt` (and add the ids to `unavailableQuoteIds`) in the currency setter, and have `_discountFor`/`_promotionPrices` skip quotes whose `currency != _selection.currency`.

verdicts.reason: The mixed-currency state cannot be reached on a real path. Every SelectRide builds its own fresh RideSelectionController (select_ride.dart:269-275; no caller passes `selection:`). On the first load `authoritativeQuotes` is empty, so a server answer in another currency leaves no stale old-currency quote behind. The finding's own scenario (first quote in EUR for a Swedish pickup) therefore shows no stale discount. Stale quotes could exist only if the pickup moved between zones in one session. The only zones are Sweden, France and Tunisia (rider_zones.dart:39-61), so a Set-pickup pin move across zones is unrealistic. Even then the state is transient. Set pickup that is cancelled after a pin quote reloads all quotes (select_ride.dart:1484). A confirmed pickup books or reloads (1505-1510). `_loadQuote` overwrites every category through adoptQuote or removes it on failure or timeout (ride_selection_controller.dart:401-409). The booking guard `quoteIsAvailable` also rejects a quote whose currency is not the current one (474).
verdicts.repro: Traced the currency setter (ride_selection_controller.dart:65-69), adoptQuote (453-463), loadQuotes/_loadQuote (337-410), SelectRide controller creation (select_ride.dart:269), the pin re-quote flow (1470-1510) and the zone table. No test run.

refuted.title: LiveCancelFeePreview.freeMinutesLeft can go negative when the rule has no free window and the fee evaluates to zero
refuted.description: freeMinutesLeft is `fee.isPositive ? 0 : rule.freeMin - minutes`. The zero branch is meant for 'still inside the free window', but it is also reached when the computed fee is zero for other reasons (a rule whose fixed fee/percent resolves to 0 öre, or a zero fare), in which case `rule.freeMin - minutes` becomes negative once `minutes > freeMin`. Any UI that renders '{n} min free left' would display a negative number.
refuted.failure_scenario: Config publishes a live cancel rule with freeMin 2 and a 0-SEK fee for a promo category; 5 minutes after acceptance the preview reports freeMinutesLeft = -3.
refuted.suggested_fix: Clamp: `freeMinutesLeft: math.max(0, rule.freeMin - minutes)` independent of the fee sign.

verdicts.reason: The only consumer of freeMinutesLeft is waiting_for_driver.dart:793-796: `left <= 1 ? cancelFreeUnderMinute : cancelFreeMinutes('$left')`. A negative value falls into the `<= 1` branch, so no negative number is ever rendered. It is also only reached when the fee really is 0 (waiting_for_driver.dart:790 returns the fee text first when it is positive), so the rider correctly sees that cancelling is free. The setup also needs a server rule whose charge is 0 öre, which no default config has (rider_app_config.dart defaults all have positive values or minimums). The worst effect is the wording 'under a minute' on a cancel that stays free.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: LiveCancelFeePreview.of (rider_app_config.dart:705-721) -> CancelFeeCalculator.live/_charge (contracts/cancel_fee.dart:68-89) -> the single consumer _cancelFeeNote (waiting_for_driver.dart:782-799).

refuted.title: Telemetry sink and ApiClient build URLs by string concatenation; a base URL with a trailing slash passes the release validator but produces '//api/v1/...' on every request
refuted.description: `HttpObservabilitySink._post` does `Uri.parse('$baseUrl$path')` and ApiClient does the same (lib/core/api/api_client.dart:77 `Uri.parse('${_env.apiBaseUrl}$path')`, :189). `TransportComposition.releaseApiBaseUrlProblem` (lib/app/config/transport_composition.dart:18-31) is the fail-fast guard for an unusable MOVERA_API_BASE_URL and rejects empty, non-https and .invalid hosts, but accepts `https://api.movera.se/`. With such a define every API and telemetry call targets `https://api.movera.se//api/v1/...`; most servers/routers treat the empty first segment as a different path (404), and the sink swallows every error (`catchError((_) => http.Response('', 599))`), so a production build would fail every request at runtime, exactly the class of misconfiguration the validator exists to catch at composition time.
refuted.failure_scenario: Staging built with `--dart-define=MOVERA_API_BASE_URL=https://api.staging.movera.se/` passes AppScope composition, then every sign-in, quote and telemetry call 404s.
refuted.evidence: lib/core/observability/http_observability.dart:23 `Uri.parse('$baseUrl$path'),` ; lib/core/api/api_client.dart:77 `final uri = Uri.parse('${_env.apiBaseUrl}$path');` ; transport_composition.dart:18-31 (no check for a path/trailing slash).
refuted.suggested_fix: Normalise once (strip trailing '/' in AppEnv or reject it in releaseApiBaseUrlProblem) or join with `Uri.parse(baseUrl).resolve(path.substring(1))`.

verdicts.reason: This needs an operator to misconfigure the build. No real runtime input reaches it. Every checked-in build define in .github/workflows (api.movera.example, api.staging.movera.example, api.demo.movera.invalid) and the AppEnv default (env.dart:42-45) have no trailing slash. MOVERA_API_BASE_URL is a compile-time constant that the rider cannot change. Whether '//api/v1' actually 404s depends on a server that is not in this repo. This is a hardening suggestion for releaseApiBaseUrlProblem (transport_composition.dart:18-31), not a reachable defect.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: HttpObservabilitySink._post (http_observability.dart:23), ApiClient._send/refresh (api_client.dart:77,189) and di.dart:126, plus a grep of every MOVERA_API_BASE_URL define in workflows and docs.

refuted.title: Trip/booking parsers read the in-process mock envelope (destination, ride.id, flat vehicleMake) rather than the documented TripProjection (dropoff, tripId, driver.vehicle{...})
refuted.description: contracts/CONTRACT.md §2 and openapi.yaml define TripProjection{tripId, pickup: Place, dropoff: Place, fare: Money, driver?: DriverSummary{driverId, firstName, vehicle:{make,model,color,plate}}} and say success responses are the bare resource. RideProjection._place(ride,'destination') (lines 80-101) only looks at `ride['destination']` / `ride['destinationLat']`, never `dropoff`; MatchedDriver.fromJson (lib/core/contracts/matched_driver.dart:78-83) requires `json['id']` and reads flat `vehicleMake`/`vehicleModel`/`plate`, so a DriverSummary with `driverId` + nested `vehicle` yields null (driver card empty, plate missing); BookingCoordinator._requireRideId (lib/features/booking/application/booking_coordinator.dart:92-106) throws FormatException unless the response is `{ride:{id}}`. ApiRideRealtime does accept both shapes via tripProjectionOf, which shows the contract shape is expected elsewhere, so the booking/history/restore paths are inconsistent with it. Confidence is moderate because the docs also call InProcessMockClient the 'v1 mock contract'; if the production server really emits the mock envelope this is intended.
refuted.failure_scenario: Against a server that follows contracts/openapi.yaml: POST /trips returns {tripId,...} -> _requireRideId throws 'Booking response missing ride object' and the rider sees a booking error; GET /trips history returns dropoff -> destination is null -> toSnapshot returns null -> rides disappear; driver {driverId, vehicle:{plate}} -> MatchedDriver null -> no driver/plate shown during the trip.
refuted.suggested_fix: Accept the contract shape as the primary form: read `dropoff` (fallback `destination`), `tripId` (fallback ride.id), `driverId` and nested `vehicle{make,model,color,plate}`; or update CONTRACT.md/openapi to the envelope the app actually parses. Also wrap the `as String?` casts in MatchedDriver.fromJson (a numeric id throws TypeError, which RideProjection.toSnapshot does not catch).

verdicts.reason: The failure scenario assumes a server that serves contracts/openapi.yaml (/trips, TripProjection with dropoff/tripId/driverId and a nested vehicle). The app never calls that surface. It books with POST /api/v1/rides (booking_coordinator.dart:220, :642) and reads /api/v1/rider/trips and /api/v1/rider/trips/active (ride_history_repositories.dart:24, active_trip_repositories.dart:22). Those routes do not exist in openapi.yaml at all (its paths are /trips, /rider/trips and so on). A contract-only server would 404 on the path before any parsing happens. The documents make this intentional. ARCHITECTURE.md:67-74 says release builds 'use the proposed server routes in docs/API_V1_MOCK.md' and that 'InProcessMockClient is the v1 mock contract'. docs/API_V1_MOCK.md:84-104 specifies exactly the {ride:{id,...}} envelope and the destination/flat-driver projection the parsers read. docs/DECISIONS.md P1 says 'Rider rename is R4 (later)' and 'Until a backend exists, each app keeps its current mock'. No real caller receives the contract-shaped response the finding describes. Supporting both shapes is a pending migration (R4), not a live bug.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: grepped lib for the ride endpoints the app calls and compared them with the openapi.yaml path list (grep '^  /'). Read ARCHITECTURE.md:60-80, docs/API_V1_MOCK.md:80-104, docs/DECISIONS.md P1, and the migration note in trip_projection_wire.dart:1-11. I did not run a test.

refuted.title: Fractional amounts and distances always use '.' as decimal separator in fr/sv
refuted.description: formatMoney writes non-whole SEK as '35.50 kr' (:31-33) regardless of locale, while EUR/TND are hand-converted to a comma (:35, :37), so the app itself treats the comma as the correct separator yet shows Swedish kronor with a dot (sv locale expects '35,50 kr'). The same dot-only formatting reaches riders through toStringAsFixed with no locale: place_suggestion.dart:66-70 formatDistanceKm ('1.2 km'), ride_check_trigger.dart:244, trip_detail.dart:203 kmDriven, home_journey_section.dart:366 homeCo2Kg, ride_check_page.dart:44-50 and ride_check_demo_page.dart:159. Reproduced: L10n.use('sv'); formatMoney(Money(3550)) == '35.50 kr'.
refuted.failure_scenario: Swedish rider sees a cancellation fee of '35.50 kr', '4.2 km parcourus' / '4.2 km körda' on the receipt and '1.5 kg' CO2 on Home, where Swedish/French convention is '35,50 kr', '4,2 km', '1,5 kg'.
refuted.evidence: money.dart:31-33 `final major = money.majorString;\n      final isWhole = money.amountMinor % Money.minorPerMajor('SEK') == 0;\n      return '${isWhole ? major.split('.').first : major} kr';`; place_suggestion.dart:70 `: '${rounded.toStringAsFixed(1)} km';`; trip_detail.dart:203 `return L10n.current.kmDriven(km.toStringAsFixed(km < 10 ? 1 : 0));`
refuted.suggested_fix: Route fractional numbers through NumberFormat.decimalPattern(L10n.code) (or a small helper that swaps the separator for fr/sv) in money.dart and the distance/weight helpers.

verdicts.reason: The money part is intentional and pinned by a test. money.dart:13-20 documents one format per currency, not per locale: 'SEK: "35 kr", "35.50 kr" ... (the Swedish fare look, unchanged)', with EUR/TND deliberately using a comma. test/ride/currency_by_zone_test.dart:217-226 ('Swedish prices read exactly as before') asserts formatMoney(Money(3550)) == '35.50 kr'. Using the dot is a recorded product choice, not a defect. The rest is a stylistic decimal-separator preference for distance and CO2 strings: '4.2 km' is unambiguous, nothing is computed or shown wrongly, and no document requires locale-specific numerals.
verdicts.repro: Read money.dart:1-41 and the pinning test currency_by_zone_test.dart:225. Checked DECISIONS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md and QA_HOOKS.md: no requirement for locale decimal separators.

verdicts.reason: The test is a classification manifest by design. Each row points to a behavioural evidence test (phase85_action_effect_matrix_test.dart:44 onward, e.g. :92 ride_check_call_112 -> test/safety/ride_check_card_test.dart). The table checks coverage, uniqueness and that the evidence file exists, plus policy rules: local-only actions must be presentationOnly (:199-212), and honest-unavailable actions must claim no remote effect (:214-223). The behavioural proof is those evidence tests, and they run in the same CI job: batch7-phase85-final-certification.yml has the 'Full unit + widget suite' step `flutter test` right after the matrix step.
