verdicts.repro: Read the matrix test (lines 1-260) and the workflow steps (lines 30-45). Confirmed that the evidence files run in the same job's full-suite step.

refuted.title: An out-of-order GPS fix is ignored by navigation but returned as drawable, so the car, camera and arrival check jump back to an older position
refuted.description: setVehicle returns true for a fix older than the last accepted one. Its contract says true means 'the caller should draw it'. _applyDriverPosition then writes that older fix into _driverPosition and _lastLocation, feeds it to the camera (which accepts any fix under 30 s old) and moves the marker. Navigation progress and the banner stay on the newer fix, so the screen and navigation disagree until the next fix.
refuted.failure_scenario: After a resume, the provider delivers a batched or cached fix stamped earlier than the last accepted one. The marker and camera snap back along the road while the banner distance stays put, and _nearArrivalTarget is evaluated from the older point. Verified by reading the code; not run.
refuted.evidence: navigation_controller.dart:221-226 `if (at != null && _lastMeasuredAt != null && at.isBefore(_lastMeasuredAt!)) { return true; }` ; accept_ride_trip.dart:655-669 `if (!_navigation.setVehicle(location)) { return; } ... _driverPosition = next; ... _camera.update(location: location, ...); _vehicle.moveTo(...)`
refuted.suggested_fix: Return false for out-of-order fixes (as for held jumps) so the caller drops them too.

verdicts.reason: The setVehicle contract states the behaviour: navigation_controller.dart:203-204 says 'Returns false only for a fix held back as a GPS jump ... Every other fix returns true.' The finding describes a real path to no out-of-order fix. Fixes come from Geolocator.getPositionStream (driver_location_service.dart:91-97), which delivers in time order. On resume, _startLiveLocation (accept_ride_trip.dart:614-648) awaits a fresh getCurrentPosition and applies it synchronously before any stream event, and it subscribes only after that. Any fix older than 30 s, or with accuracy worse than 50 m, is already dropped by isDisplayableAt (driver_location_repository.dart:35-58). Even if an older fix did arrive, the marker would move back once by a few metres and be corrected by the next fix. The scenario is speculative.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: navigation_controller.dart:203-232, accept_ride_trip.dart:610-690, driver_location_service.dart:91-106. No source that delivers fixes out of order was found.

refuted.title: Picked document is accepted without checking its type; on web any file passes and is shown as a PDF
refuted.description: allowedExtensions is passed to FilePicker.platform.pickFiles, but on web it only sets the input's accept attribute, which is a hint. The user can switch the dialog to 'All files', and a selectFile port can return anything. After the pick the code checks only that the bytes are not empty, then stores the name and bytes and shows 'File selected successfully'. _buildFilePreview shows every non-png/jpg file with the red PDF icon, so a .docx, .heic or .zip looks like an accepted PDF.
refuted.failure_scenario: On the web build the driver opens 'Tap to upload', picks 'All files' and chooses notes.docx. The step shows a green 'File selected successfully' snackbar and a PDF icon labelled notes.docx.
refuted.suggested_fix: After the pick, check file.extension (lower-cased) against the allowed list, and ideally the magic bytes too, and show couldNotReadSelectedFile for anything else.

verdicts.reason: The effect is harmless. The picked bytes are used only for the 60x60 preview in vehicle_document_upload.dart:199-201. Nothing reads selectedFileBytes or selectedFileName outside this State (grep: they are only written at :256-257 and :220-221 and read in _buildFilePreview). Nothing is uploaded or submitted, and the step's Continue button (additional detail/navigation.dart:159-160, controller.moveToNextStep) does not depend on whether a file was picked. So on web a .docx picked through 'All files' changes only the icon shown. On Android and iOS, FileType.custom with allowedExtensions does filter the picker. The selectFile hook is a test injection port. No document review exists that could accept the wrong file (REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:45 says document review is not a connected service).
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _pickAnyFile, _buildFilePreview, the VehicleRegisteration and VehicleInsurance wrappers, and navigation.dart's Continue handler. Grep for selectedFileBytes usages.

refuted.title: Camera capture of vehicle registration/insurance is downscaled into an 800x400 box, so portrait document photos come out at about 300x400 px
refuted.description: The registration and insurance camera capture passes both maxWidth: 800 and maxHeight: 400 to pickImage. image_picker keeps the aspect ratio and fits the image inside both limits. A normal portrait photo (3024x4032) of an A4 or A5 registration certificate becomes 300x400 px, and a landscape one becomes 533x400. That is too low to read the document's text. The Add vehicle document capture in add_vehicle.dart:850-853 uses only maxWidth: 1024 for the same kind of document.
refuted.failure_scenario: The driver holds the phone upright and photographs a registration certificate on the Vehicle registration step. The returned XFile is about 300x400 px and the certificate text cannot be read in the preview or by any later review.
refuted.suggested_fix: Drop maxHeight, or use a symmetric bound such as maxWidth: 1600, maxHeight: 1600, with an imageQuality setting so the size stays bounded.

verdicts.reason: maxWidth: 800 and maxHeight: 400 at vehicle_document_upload.dart:276-278 do downscale the photo. But the captured bytes are only drawn as a 60x60 BoxFit.cover thumbnail (:200) and never go anywhere else. There is no upload, no review and no later reader (bytes are only used in _buildFilePreview, and Continue in navigation.dart:159 ignores them). So 'the text cannot be read by any later review' cannot happen, and the preview cannot show legible text at any resolution. Document review is documented as not connected (REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:45). This only becomes a real problem if a document upload is wired up later.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _openCamera, _buildFilePreview and the parent stepper's Continue. Grep for selectedFileBytes readers: only :186.

refuted.title: A waiting.byCategory block that omits a category drops the seed per-category rules, so XL loses its contract default of 3 free minutes and 3 min no-show
refuted.description: When `waiting.byCategory` is present, _waiting builds the category map only from the entries the document lists. The seed rules (xl: 3 free minutes and 3 min no-show; premium per-minute) are kept only when byCategory is missing altogether. contract.json#configDefaults says the apps fall back to the defaults (freeWaitMin default 5, xl 3) 'when a document lacks a field or has a bad value', and the contract's own sample document lists byCategory for economy and comfort only. With that document, termsFor(category: 'Movera XL') gives 5 free minutes and a 5 min no-show instead of 3/3. An XL driver waits 2 extra unpaid minutes before the waiting fee starts and before the no-show button appears. A broken xl entry ('xl': 'three') also falls to 5, and a test asserts that.
refuted.failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. Applying the contract sample config (DriverAppConfig.fromJson(contract fixture).apply()) and starting an XL pickup: WaitingRules.current.termsFor(category: 'Movera XL').freeMinutes is 5, not 3. The waiting clock bills from minute 5 and the no-show button appears at 5 min.
refuted.evidence:
driver_app_config.dart:257-263 `final byCategory = _map(json['byCategory']); final categories = <String, WaitingRule>{}; if (byCategory == null) { for (final entry in seed.categories.entries) {...} } else { for (final entry in byCategory.entries) {`
contract.json configDefaults: `"freeWaitMin": {"default": 5, "xl": 3}`
contracts/fixtures/config/driver_app_config.json byCategory: only "economy" and "comfort"
refuted.suggested_fix: Start from the seed category rules (rebased to the document currency) and override them with the entries the document provides, instead of replacing the whole map whenever byCategory exists.

verdicts.reason: Leaving the seed rules out when byCategory is present is a consistent contract reading, not a mismatch. byCategory is the admin's full per-category map (CONTRACT.md:198/209/217), and configDefaults says 'Admin exports them where no setting exists yet' (contract.json:649). The real admin exports list every category, xl included with freeWaitMin 3 and noShowAfterMin 3 (test/fixtures/config/driver_app_config.Z001.json, also FR-PC and TN-TC). So a published zone document does not leave XL out. The contract sample fixture is a schema sample, not a published zone. The rider app does the same thing: rider_app_config.dart:385-405 builds byCategory only from the entries listed, so a category that is not listed falls back to the headline terms. Both apps therefore agree on XL. The behaviour for a broken xl entry is pinned on purpose by test/contract/driver_app_config_test.dart:142,165.
verdicts.repro: Traced driver_app_config.dart:237-292 and compared it with rider_app_config.dart:382-405. Checked the waiting.byCategory keys in contracts/fixtures/config/driver_app_config.json (economy and comfort only) against the admin exports in test/fixtures/config/*.json (all 8 categories, xl at 3/3).

refuted.title: Pickup-pay line on Radar offer cards is hard-coded English ('incl. … pickup') in fr/sv
refuted.description: RadarOfferCard renders PickupPayLine(quote: offer.pickupPay) under the fare (radar_offer_card.dart:386). When admin chooses PickupPayDisplay.fareWithPickupLine, the line text comes from PickupPayQuote.line, which concatenates the English words 'incl.' and 'pickup' around the localized amount and leg label.
refuted.failure_scenario: Admin sets pickup pay to 'fare with pickup line'. A French or Swedish driver sees Radar cards reading 'incl. 21,60 kr pickup · 4.2 km · 9 min'.
refuted.evidence:
pickup_pay.dart:48-49 `String? get line => hasPay && display == PickupPayDisplay.fareWithPickupLine ? 'incl. ${pay.formatted} pickup · ${leg.label}' : null;`
radar_offer_card.dart:386 `PickupPayLine(quote: offer.pickupPay),`
refuted.suggested_fix: Move the template to the ARB files (e.g. tr.pickupPayIncluded(amount, leg)).

verdicts.reason: The English line cannot appear in the shipped app. PickupPayQuote.line returns text only when display == PickupPayDisplay.fareWithPickupLine (pickup_pay.dart:48). That display comes from PickupPayConfig.current (pickup_pay.dart:92-96), which is a const PickupPayConfig() with display defaulting to totalOnly (pickup_pay_config.dart:190,200). Nothing in lib/ assigns PickupPayConfig.current or uses fareWithPickupLine. Only test/widget/pickup_pay_card_test.dart and test/core/pickup_pay_test.dart do. No admin or config parser exposes the setting. The untranslated template is latent and needs moving to the ARB files before the display option is wired up.
verdicts.repro: Searched all of lib/ for PickupPayDisplay, fareWithPickupLine, 'PickupPayConfig.current =' and 'display:'. The only production references are the enum definition, the totalOnly default and copyWith.

refuted.title: A malformed Ride-check log is logged with its raw contents and then silently overwritten, losing every saved check
refuted.description: _read catches FormatException and logs it with `$error`. FormatException.toString includes a source excerpt, so trip IDs, reasons containing road names and the driver's free-text 'What happened' note reach the log channel (the same class as the known prefs_trip_history/prefs_active_ride findings, at a new site). It then returns an empty list. The next _save writes only the new record over the key, so all earlier checks are destroyed. Individual rows that fail RideCheckRecord.fromJson are also dropped and erased on the next save. Unlike the support repository (LocalQuarantine.storeOnce) and the other stores, nothing is preserved.
refuted.failure_scenario: A truncated localStorage write (for example, the Safari tab killed mid-write, as recorded in DECISIONS.md) leaves movera_driver_ride_checks undecodable. The next Ride check logs the raw blob and replaces the whole history with one row, and the past checks shown in trip details are gone.
refuted.evidence:
ride_check_log.dart:103-106 `} on FormatException catch (error) { DriverLog.warn('Ride check log malformed: $error'); } return <RideCheckRecord>[];`
ride_check_log.dart:66-76 `final rows = _read(prefs)..removeWhere(...)..add(record); ... prefs.setString(key, jsonEncode({... rows ...}))`
refuted.suggested_fix: Quarantine the raw value (LocalQuarantine.storeOnce) before overwriting, and log only a generic message without the exception's source excerpt.

verdicts.reason: There is no realistic way to reach the malformed state. The only writer of movera_driver_ride_checks is PrefsRideCheckLog._save (lib/core/safety/ride_check_log.dart:62-77). It writes the whole value with a single jsonEncode + prefs.setString, and saves are serialised through _enqueue. On the web, localStorage.setItem is atomic, so a tab kill cannot leave a truncated value. Native SharedPreferences writes are atomic too. The 'Safari tab killed mid-write' premise is not in DECISIONS.md: docs/DECISIONS.md:79-81 is about HtmlElementView rebuilds causing tab crashes, not about partial writes. Rows the app wrote itself always pass RideCheckRecord.fromJson. docs/LOCAL_DATA.md:16-18 also records the intended behaviour: 'A corrupt value is treated as missing by the readers'. The FormatException excerpt in the log (line 104) and the overwrite are both real code, but they only run on externally tampered storage. That is speculative, and the local ride-check log is demo data.
verdicts.repro: Read ride_check_log.dart end to end (the single writer, the _enqueue serialisation, _read's catch). Checked docs/LOCAL_DATA.md:16 (corrupt treated as missing) and docs/DECISIONS.md:79-81 (Safari crash cause, nothing about truncated writes). No test run, because the trigger needs storage that was tampered with outside the app.

refuted.title: Island spring is under-damped although docs/driver-trip-island.md specifies a critically damped spring
refuted.description: The doc states 'IslandMorph owns one critically damped spring controller for width, height and corner geometry'. The spring uses mass 1, stiffness 210, damping 25. Critical damping is 2·sqrt(210) ≈ 28.98, so the damping ratio is about 0.86 (under-damped) and the motion overshoots past 1. The value is then clamped by `_phase`, so the geometry sits pinned at the target while the spring is still overshooting, and the settle takes longer than the visible motion.
refuted.failure_scenario: A resize with incoming velocity (up to 3.0 carried in) overshoots past 1. The clamp holds the island at the target size until the spring comes back, and the outgoing layers only clear when the spring settles. This differs from the documented critically damped motion.
refuted.evidence:
island_morph.dart:146 `const SpringDescription(mass: 1, stiffness: 210, damping: 25),`
island_morph.dart:64 `double get _phase => _motion.value.clamp(0.0, 1.0);`
refuted.suggested_fix: Use damping = 2*sqrt(stiffness*mass) (≈ 29), or update the doc.

verdicts.reason: The mismatch with the doc is real but has no visible effect. With mass 1, stiffness 210 and damping 25 (island_morph.dart:146), the damping ratio is 25/(2*sqrt(210)) ≈ 0.862. Peak overshoot is exp(-ζπ/sqrt(1-ζ²)) ≈ exp(-5.34) ≈ 0.5%. That excursion is clamped by _phase (line 64), and the default AnimationController bounds of 0..1 clamp it as well. The geometry therefore stays at the target during an overshoot of about 0.005 and a short return. The tolerance (distance .001, velocity .01) means settle, and so the clearing of outgoing layers in _settled (lines 67-72), comes only a few ms after the visible motion ends. The code comment ('a soft settle, like the iPhone island') shows the value was chosen on purpose. At most the doc wording in docs/driver-trip-island.md:11 is imprecise.
verdicts.repro: Computed the damping ratio and the overshoot by hand from the SpringDescription at island_morph.dart:146. Traced _phase (line 64), _settled (lines 67-72) and the didUpdateWidget animateWith path.
